author: andybutland
body:
## Description

Fixes #22955 and #23194.

**The user-facing fix is already in `v17/dev`** — I accidentally committed it directly to the branch in [`dfe98ffa`](https://github.com/umbraco/Umbraco-CMS/commit/dfe98ffa3b7179c778a848635accc22fa4d50a11). That covers the original symptom (clicking a picked content or media ref in the RTE link picker navigated to `/edit/<guid>` and showed *Not Found*) and the remove-dialog "undefined" name bug (by initialising `UmbDocumentItemDataResolver` inside `#loadPickedDocumentItem` so both the "open existing link" and "pick new link" paths produce it).

**What this PR cleans up:**

1. `link-picker-modal.element.ts` — pass `?readonly=${!this.modalContext?.router}` on the picked content ref. `modalContext.router` is assigned synchronously at modal-construction time and is `readonly`, so this signal is stable from first render and correctly distinguishes routable modals (multi-url-picker property editor) from non-routable ones (RTE toolbar via `umbOpenModal`). This avoids any flicker where the reference changes clickable state.
2. `document-item-ref.element.ts` — move the readonly decision out of the shared element and back to the caller. The `dfe98ffa` fix tied `readonly` to `!_editPath` inside the element, but `_editPath` starts as `''` and only resolves asynchronously, so every legitimate routable doc-ref flashed as readonly on first paint. The href guard in `#getHref()` stays, so no broken link is ever rendered; visual readonly is now the caller's responsibility.
3. Comments in `document-item-ref.element.ts` and `input-media.element.ts` documenting why we skip the href when no route context is reachable, and why media uses `disabled` instead of `readonly` (`uui-card-media` doesn't honour `readonly` — there's a `TODO` to switch when it does).

The standalone link picker (routable, opened from the Multi URL Picker property editor) is unchanged: refs stay clickable and open the linked content in an overlay. Replicating that overlay flow inside the non-routable RTE link picker would need deeper architectural work, so for now we just suppress the misleading click affordance.

## Testing

Prerequisites: a content item with a TipTap RTE property, and at least one published content item and one media item to link to.

1. Edit a content item with a TipTap RTE property. Type some text, select it, click the toolbar "Link" button.
2. In the Content section, pick an internal page → Submit.
3. Click the inserted link in the RTE, then click "Edit link" to re-open the picker against the existing link.
4. The picked document ref should render without underline/pointer/hover; clicking it does nothing. (Before: navigated to `/edit/<guid>` → *Not Found*.)
5. Click "Remove" in the ref's action bar. Confirm dialog should read `Are you sure you want to remove <document name>?`. (Before: `…remove undefined?`.)
6. Repeat with a media item: open the picker, switch to Media, pick → Submit, re-open via "Edit link". The card should render without click affordance; the Remove action in the top-right corner should still work.

Regression checks:

7. **Standalone link picker (routable).** Add a Multi URL Picker property to a content type. On a content item, edit that property: pick a document and a media item, save, re-open. Picked refs should still be clickable and open the workspace as an overlay. Confirm overlay opens, close it.
8. **Content collection / document workspace References tab / Media collection.** Row titles, references list items, and media cards should still be clickable and open their respective workspaces.

body:
## Summary

Pure dead-code removal. The `XRT_PLUGIN_BUILD_INPROC_FALLBACK` CMake option was retained briefly post-#263 as a guard against accidental re-introduction of in-tree vendor static-link paths. With #263 (drv_leia extraction) and #286 (cascade-uninstall fix) shipped in runtime v1.4.0 + v1.4.1, and no in-tree fallback code remaining for the option to gate against, the option itself is dead surface area.

Closes #287.

## Net change

```
 CLAUDE.md                                          | 11 +--
 CMakeLists.txt                                     |  6 --
 docs/guides/vendor-integration.md                  | 46 +++-------
 docs/roadmap/vendor-plugin-architecture.md         |  7 +-
 docs/specs/runtime/plugin-discovery.md             | 28 ++++---
 src/xrt/include/xrt/xrt_config_build.h.cmake_in    |  1 -
 src/xrt/targets/common/target_builder_sim_display.c| 46 ++--------
 src/xrt/targets/common/target_instance.c           | 98 +---------------------
 8 files changed, 49 insertions(+), 194 deletions(-)
```

**145 lines net deletion**, no functional behavior change.

## What's removed

### Build system
- `option(XRT_PLUGIN_BUILD_INPROC_FALLBACK ...)` in root `CMakeLists.txt`
- The matching `#cmakedefine` in `xrt_config_build.h.cmake_in`

### C source
- `src/xrt/targets/common/target_instance.c`:
  - The `#ifdef XRT_PLUGIN_BUILD_INPROC_FALLBACK`-guarded `#include \"sim_display/sim_display_interface.h\"`
  - The full sim_display in-proc fallback block in `oxr_system_create` (~75 lines: display-info population, atlas tiling computation, DP factory pointer fallbacks per graphics API)
- `src/xrt/targets/common/target_builder_sim_display.c`:
  - The `#ifdef`-guarded sim_display include
  - The static `sim_display_hmd_create()` fallback in `open_system_impl`
  - The static-archive dim-query branch
  - The static `sim_display_hmd_set_pose_source()` fallback
  - All paths now route exclusively through the plug-in iface (which has been the production path since #256)
  - The error message when no plug-in creates a device now points users at the registry contract instead of a now-impossible \"no static fallback compiled in\" condition

### Docs (intentional historical references kept where they explain what the option was)
- `CLAUDE.md` Key CMake Options
- `docs/guides/vendor-integration.md` legacy-banner reflows to point at the new onboarding guide
- `docs/specs/runtime/plugin-discovery.md` \"what happens with no plug-in\" section — now correctly says `xrCreateSession` fails (was: \"falls back to static `drv_sim_display`\")
- `docs/roadmap/vendor-plugin-architecture.md` decision log gets a `2026-05-23 — #287 landed` entry; the post-#263 state section bumps the explanation

## Behavior change

Pre-PR, with `XRT_PLUGIN_BUILD_INPROC_FALLBACK=OFF` (default), the runtime already routed everything through the plug-in iface — the `#ifdef` blocks compiled out. So this PR is **behavior-preserving** for any build configuration that has been shipped.

The only configuration that loses behavior is `XRT_PLUGIN_BUILD_INPROC_FALLBACK=ON` — which has not been a shipped configuration since v1.4.0 (the `drv_leia` source it linked against is no longer in this tree).

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts\build_windows.bat build` completes clean on the user's machine
- [x] `git grep -ri XRT_PLUGIN_BUILD_INPROC_FALLBACK -- '*.c' '*.cpp' '*.h' '*.cmake' CMakeLists.txt '*.bat' '*.yml'` returns zero hits (all remaining mentions are historical narrative in docs)

body:
## Summary

- **Dead code / logic bug**: Removed `get_or_create_twiddles` and the `TWIDDLE_CACHE` thread-local from `stft.rs`. The function contained a broken early-return that caused the cache to be missed on every call (the `TWIDDLE_CACHE.with(...)` block called `return` inside a closure, which only returned from the closure, not the outer function — so the fallback `TwiddleCache::new(n)` always ran). The cache provided zero benefit while adding misleading code. The existing `fft_with_twiddles` path (used by the main STFT loop) is correct and unaffected.
- **Correctness**: Fixed manual assign-op `d = d % x` → `d %= x` in `audio_graph.rs`; merged identical NAL-R correction branches in `hearmusica/gain.rs`; replaced `len() > 0` with `!is_empty()` in tests; replaced manual range-contains in `hearing_aid.rs` and `wav.rs`.
- **Type safety**: Changed `&mut Vec<f32>` to `&mut [f32]` in `hearmusica/delay.rs` to accept slices without forcing reallocation semantics.
- **Unused code removal**: 35 files touched — removed unused imports, prefixed intentionally-unused parameters with `_`, removed dead `stage` counter in `fft()`, dropped `useless_vec!` in benchmark, removed `enumerate()` where index was immediately discarded.
- **Suppressions with justification**: Added `#[allow(clippy::needless_range_loop)]` on 11 functions where cross-slice multi-dimensional indexing (matrix ops, eigenvector updates, k-means, mask normalisation) makes the range form the only correct and readable option. Added `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` on two fixed-interface mathematical functions.

author: hanfour
body:
## Summary

The relay block (ea31acb on PR #153) trims + requires ws/wss scheme before passing `relayURL` to `RelayClient.dial`, so a user-typed `"abc"` surfaces a named log line instead of silently hanging inside the WebSocket dial. `controllerURL` had the matching trim from PR #157 but **no scheme guard** — a typo like `controller.example.com` (missing `https://`) parses to a `URL` with `scheme == nil` and only fails inside URLSession with an opaque "unsupported URL" message far from the actual mistake.

Closes side-finding #4 from `project_session_state.md`.

## Changes

- **New** `clients/apple/Shared/ControllerURLParser.swift` — `parseControllerURL(_:)` helper that trims whitespace, requires http/https scheme (case-insensitive per RFC 3986), returns nil otherwise.
- **`clients/apple/Shared/ConnectionViewModel.swift`** — 3 call sites (`signInAsync`, `connectAsync`, `refreshPolicyFromController`) now route through the helper. `lastError` + log messages tightened to mention "http or https".
- **`clients/apple/project.yml`** — adds the new parser file to `AppleSharedTests` sources.
- **`clients/apple/Tests/AppleShared/ControllerURLParserTests.swift`** — 9 new tests.

## Why a helper instead of inline guards

Three callers, each with a different error-surface convention (`lastError` UI message, throws, log + return). A helper returning `URL?` keeps each call site's existing shape — just one extra layer of validation at the boundary. Mirrors the inline form the relay block uses; lifted to a function only because three sites multiplies the cost of repetition.

## Test plan

- [x] AppleSharedTests: 35 tests pass locally (was 26 — +9 new).
- [x] BambooApp-macOS compiles cleanly (helper is visible to ConnectionViewModel without extra imports).
- [ ] CI green.

No runtime install on real Macs this PR — it's pure input-validation logic with full coverage; behavior on valid URLs is identical to today (still trim, still URL(string:), still http/https). Failure paths now reject earlier with a clearer message instead of letting URLSession reject later.

# AFDA Rebuild: Full-Stack Implementation with Deployment & Monitoring

## Overview

This PR represents a complete rebuild of the AFDA Booking Platform with production-ready deployment infrastructure and monitoring.

**Branch:** `afda-rebuild-2026`  
**Target:** `main` (via merge to unify histories)

## What's New

### Features & Core (Phases 1–3)
- ✅ Backend Express + TypeScript + Supabase integration
- ✅ JWT authentication with role-based access control
- ✅ Student public app: batch lookup and online booking
- ✅ Staff slot-booking app: batch editor, imports (XLSX), exports (PDF/XLSX/CSV)
- ✅ Audit logging with filtering and export
- ✅ Row-level security (RLS) policies on all tables

### Testing & Performance (Phase 4)
- ✅ End-to-end test suite (Playwright): import workflows, exports, audit logs (5 tests passing)
- ✅ Load/perf test harness: configurable concurrency, response time tracking
- ✅ Security hardening: auth gate on public routes, role gate on staff endpoints, avoided default role escalation

### Deployment & Ops (Phase 5)
- ✅ Vercel Functions backend with serverless adapter
- ✅ Vercel-ready frontend configs (student + staff apps)
- ✅ Environment templates with placeholders (no real secrets tracked)
- ✅ Monitoring setup: health/readiness endpoints + scheduled uptime checks + optional webhook alerts
- ✅ Release checklist and one-command smoke test script

## Validation Completed

### Builds
```bash
npm run build                 # ✅ Full monorepo build passes
npm --workspace backend run build    # ✅ Backend TypeScript compiles
```

### Tests
```bash
npx playwright test --config=tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts  # ✅ All 5 E2E tests pass
npm run perf:test           # ✅ Load test runs without errors
```

### Code Quality
- Backend routes secured with auth middleware + role guards
- Frontend environment separation (NEXT_PUBLIC_* only)
- Logger configured for environment (dev: pretty, prod: JSON)
- Process-level error/rejection hooks for runtime observability
- Smoke test script validates endpoints before/after deploy

## Pre-Merge Requirements

These steps must be completed before merging to main:

### 1. Configure GitHub Secrets (for Monitoring Workflow)
Add these to repository secrets:
- `BACKEND_HEALTHCHECK_URL` → production backend `/api/health` endpoint
- `BACKEND_READINESS_URL` → production backend `/api/ready` endpoint
- `STUDENT_APP_URL` → production student app URL
- `STAFF_APP_URL` → production staff app URL
- `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` *(optional)* → Slack/Teams webhook for uptime alerts

### 2. Deploy Projects to Vercel
1. **Backend:** Create Vercel project from `backend/`, set root to `backend/`, add prod env vars (see `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`)
2. **Student App:** Create Vercel project from `apps/student-public/`, add `NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL`
3. **Staff App:** Create Vercel project from `apps/slot-booking/`, add `NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_BATCH_LINK_BASE`

### 3. Run Database Migrations
Apply `backend/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql` to production Supabase project.

### 4. Verify with One-Command Smoke Test
```bash
BACKEND_URL=https://api.yourdomain.com \
STUDENT_APP_URL=https://book.yourdomain.com \
STAFF_APP_URL=https://staff.yourdomain.com \
BATCH_PATH=/batch/<known-batch-id> \
npm run smoke:test
```
Expected: `Smoke test passed.`

### 5. Manual Product Checks
- [ ] **Student flow:** Search batch → select slot → complete booking → see confirmation
- [ ] **Staff flow:** Create batch → edit slots → publish → export to CSV/XLSX/PDF
- [ ] **Audit logs:** Filter by action/resource → download CSV
- [ ] **Backend endpoints:** 
  - `GET /api/health` → HTTP 200
  - `GET /api/ready` → HTTP 200 (checks database)

### 6. Trigger Monitoring Workflow (Manual Test)
1. Go to Actions → Uptime Monitor
2. Click "Run workflow"
3. Verify all checks pass
4. If webhook configured, verify alert was NOT sent (success = no alert)
5. Archive the run

## Files Changed

### Core Application
- Backend: `backend/src/` (index, middleware, routes, database)
- Student app: `apps/student-public/src/`
- Staff app: `apps/slot-booking/src/`
- Shared types: `shared/`

### Deployment & Infrastructure
- **Vercel adapters:** `backend/api/[...path].js`, `backend/vercel.json`, `apps/*/vercel.json`
- **Environment templates:** `.env.example`, `backend/.env.example`, `apps/*/.env.local.example`
- **GitHub Actions:** `.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml`, `.github/workflows/uptime-monitor.yml`
- **Documentation:** `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`, `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`

### Testing & Operations
- **E2E tests:** `tests/e2e/` (Playwright suite)
- **Performance:** `tests/perf/` (load test harness)
- **Smoke test:** `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (post-deploy verification)

## Merge Strategy

This branch has been bridged to main's history with a merge commit to enable PR comparison. When merging:
- **Option A (Recommended):** Create PR, review, and merge via "Create a merge commit" → keeps both histories visible
- **Option B (Clean slate):** If you prefer to discard old main history, you can rebase this branch onto main and force-push to main directly (not recommended for team repos)

## Post-Merge: Go-Live Sequence

1. Deploy projects via Vercel (trigger builds from main)
2. Set database in production mode (enable RLS enforcement)
3. Monitor uptime workflow for at least 30 minutes
4. Announce completion and release notes in team channel

## Support & Rollback

If deployment issues occur:
- Backend errors: Check `GET /api/ready` response and Vercel function logs
- Frontend issues: Verify `NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL` env vars match deployed backend
- Database issues: Confirm migration was applied and Supabase service role key is set
- To rollback: Revert to previous Vercel deployment via dashboard

### Questions or Issues?
See `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` for detailed troubleshooting and architecture notes.

body:
## Summary
- Teachers on mobile Chrome/Safari hit **"Pop-up blocked — allow pop-ups for vocaband.com"** when clicking **Print roster** because the handler in `ClassRosterModal.tsx` used `window.open()`, which the default popup blocker silently swallows.
- Swap the popup for a hidden same-window `<iframe>` (set via `srcdoc`) and call `print()` on its `contentWindow`. Same-window iframes aren't subject to popup rules, so the print dialog opens reliably.
- Detach the iframe after a 1 s grace period so Safari has time to hand the document to the print pipeline before removal.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open a class roster on desktop Chrome → click **Print roster** → print preview opens (no popup prompt).
- [ ] Repeat on mobile Safari (where popups are blocked by default) → print sheet opens directly.
- [ ] Switch teacher UI to Hebrew/Arabic → roster prints RTL with the PIN column on the correct side.
- [ ] Roster with zero PINs still shows the existing "add students first" error and does not open print.

author: mellonis
body:
Closes #180 *(carry to release PR — v7-branch merges don't auto-close)*

## Summary

`packages/machine/src/classes/State.ts` was carrying ~440 lines of graph serialization / reconstruction on top of the runtime state machinery. Two concerns, one file. Splits them.

- **New `utilities/stateGraph.ts`** holds `toGraph` and `fromGraph` plus the v7 callable-subtree comment block describing the BFS / frame-union / halt-marker passes.
- **`State.toGraph` and `State.fromGraph`** become thin delegates to the extracted functions. Public surface preserved — no consumer changes, no version bump implications beyond what was already planned for stable v7.
- **`STATE_INTERNAL` Symbol** on State exposes a getter/setter view onto the State's private fields (`#id`, `#name`, `#bareState`, `#overriddenHaltState`, `#symbolToDataMap`, `#tags`) for sibling modules in `packages/machine/src`. Exported from State.ts; intentionally NOT re-exported from `index.ts`, so it's off the public surface. Marked `@internal`.

## Design notes

**Designed with #195 in mind.** The accessor's surface covers everything `collectStates` will need (`id`, `name`, plus `symbolToDataMap` for per-transition Symbol enumeration via `.keys()`). Doing #180 first without thinking ahead would have meant extending the accessor when #195 lands; this lands the full surface now so #195 is purely additive.

**`name` setter exists for one site.** `fromGraph` writes graph-sourced composite names (e.g. `A(target)`) into freshly-built bare States, which the constructor would reject because it validates names against `/[()]/`. The setter bypasses that check intentionally — wrappers' composite names containing parens are legitimate when reconstructed from a serialized graph. JSDoc on both the Symbol and the accessor method calls this out.

**Import cycle is benign.** State.ts value-imports `{ toGraph, fromGraph }` (for the delegates). stateGraph.ts value-imports `{ State, STATE_INTERNAL, haltState, ifOtherSymbol }`. ESM resolves the cycle via live bindings — both modules see each other's exports as long as nothing at module-load reads a binding before its source module finishes evaluating. All references in stateGraph.ts live inside function bodies, so by the time `toGraph` / `fromGraph` runs, both modules have evaluated. Rollup flags the cycle as expected in the build output.

## Diff shape

```
 packages/machine/src/classes/State.ts        | 549 +++++----------------------
 packages/machine/src/utilities/stateGraph.ts | 501 ++++++++++++++++++++++++
 2 files changed, 588 insertions(+), 462 deletions(-)
```

State.ts: 891 → 516 lines. Net code delta ~+126 lines, attributable to the `STATE_INTERNAL` Symbol JSDoc, the accessor JSDoc, the delegate-method JSDoc, and the cycle-note header in the new module. The bulk of the move is line-for-line equivalent — `state.#X` becomes `stateInternal.X` where the local was assigned via `const stateInternal = state[STATE_INTERNAL]()`.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` — 473/473 passing (no test changes; existing tests cover both surfaces).
- [x] `npm run lint` clean (added one targeted `@typescript-eslint/no-this-alias` disable on the accessor's `const self = this`; object-literal getters can't be arrow functions, so the standard `this`-capture trick doesn't apply).
- [x] `npm run build` clean (the new cycle prints alongside the pre-existing `State ↔ TapeBlock` one; both resolve at runtime).

## Next: #195

`State.collectStates(initialState, tapeBlock)` lives naturally in this new module. The PR for it will only add code, not touch existing surface. The accessor it needs is already in place.

## Summary
- What changed?
- Split SG-SPEC-0066 aggregate projection record identity/rebuild-basis semantics into new SG-SPEC-0067.
- Hardened split proposal/apply flow so split-required atomicity-pressure candidates can emit proposals, and cluster parents do not gain false blocking child dependencies.
- Link related issue/task (if any): SG-SPEC-0066 / SG-SPEC-0067

## Motivation
- Why is this change needed?
- SG-SPEC-0066 hit an atomicity boundary while refining projection record semantics; the existing supervisor path could leave a split_required gate without a usable proposal/apply path.
- What problem, gap, or user need does it address?
- Keeps aggregate projection semantics bounded while making projected evidence item identity and rebuild basis explicit and trace/evidence-backed.

## Goals
- What should this PR achieve?
- Materialize one bounded child spec, keep SG-SPEC-0066 as the integration boundary, and close the resulting trace/evidence backlog gaps.
- What is intentionally out of scope?
- No storage schema, projection algorithm, dashboard/UI, telemetry collection, or member evidence ownership changes.

## Changes
- Added SG-SPEC-0067 for aggregate projection record identity and rebuild-basis semantics.
- Updated SG-SPEC-0066 to delegate the record-level concern to the child while preserving cluster-member dependencies.
- Added split/apply regression coverage and trace/evidence registry contracts for SG-SPEC-0067.
- Recorded process lessons in CONTRIBUTING.md.

## Validation
- [x] Tests added/updated for changed behavior
- [x] Local checks passed

Commands run:
```bash
python3 tools/spec_yaml_format.py specs/nodes/SG-SPEC-0066.yaml specs/nodes/SG-SPEC-0067.yaml
python3 tools/spec_yaml_lint.py specs/nodes/SG-SPEC-0066.yaml specs/nodes/SG-SPEC-0067.yaml

make viewer-surfaces && make backlog && make next-move

make test
```

## Risks / Notes
- Backward compatibility impact: existing split proposal behavior is preserved for oversized nodes; new path only admits split-required atomicity-pressure targets.
- Migration/config changes required: none.
- Known limitations: SG-SPEC-0067 is semantic-surface backed; it does not claim runtime/storage/viewer implementation.

## Summary

This PR packages the latest Agenteer research-controller work into a durable, test-covered branch. It turns the research pipeline into an auditable controller-driven state machine that can be picked up by a fresh model runner or scheduled process without relying on chat history.

Major additions:

- Adds a first-class Research Controller Agent with durable `controller-state.json` persistence.
- Adds controller CLI surfaces for initialization, stepping, running, patching, resuming, inspection, bounded tools, agenda following, supervisor loops, doctor readiness, operation loops, runner packets, launch runbooks, completion audits, goal audits, capability manifests, repair cycles, and self-tests.
- Adds state-machine governance across intake, context, feasibility, exploration, literature intake, method selection, execution, QA, manuscript generation, external review, repair, inspection, and promotion decision stages.
- Records action contracts, stage reviews, issue ledgers, work plans, execution agendas, checkpoints, model preflight artifacts, decision-quality artifacts, terminal handoffs, re-entry plans, artifact hashes, policy updates, and cost boundaries.
- Adds model-runner handoff artifacts: `controller-runner-packet`, `controller-doctor`, `controller-operate`, and `controller-runbook`. The runbook is the scheduler/external-runner launch envelope with readiness command, launch command, stop criteria, recovery commands, verification commands, budgets, protected paths, required env vars, and evidence refs.
- Expands reviewer integration with DeepSeek dual/triple panels, provider/cost/env reporting, adjudication, review-response/state-reentry outputs, and repair handoffs.
- Strengthens trust/QA surfaces around manuscript QA, methods QA, literature QA, figure QA, semantic value checks, run inspection, and reviewer-driven re-entry.
- Updates command exports, CLI dispatch, public docs, and the command catalog.
- Commits dogfood evidence from DeepSeek-reviewed paper suites and the MIMIC SAVR/TAVR dialysis redo analysis, including figures, QA files, reviewer artifacts, formatted PDF output, run inspection, phenotype/code review, and loop-memory ticks 0409-0429.

## Research Controller Commands Added / Extended

- `agenteer research controller-init`
- `agenteer research controller-step`
- `agenteer research controller-run` / `run-autonomous`
- `agenteer research controller-patch`

## Why This Matters

Before this work, Agenteer could run many research and QA commands, but the actual controller role still depended heavily on the chat operator. This PR creates the durable substrate needed for an external GPT-style runner to operate the research pipeline:

1. The controller state is persistent and inspectable.
2. Every action is gated and recorded.
3. Safe continuation has explicit readiness checks.
4. A fresh model receives a bounded prompt and command envelope.
5. A scheduled process receives a launch runbook with stop criteria and recovery paths.
6. Completion cannot be claimed without completion-audit and artifact evidence.
7. Reviewer findings can re-enter the controller state machine.

## Dogfood Artifacts Included

This PR includes loop-memory evidence from recent dogfood runs rather than only source changes:

- DeepSeek-reviewed paper suite artifacts across multiple statistical methods.
- Figure QA and manuscript QA outputs.
- Review panel, adjudication, response, and state-reentry artifacts.
- MIMIC SAVR/TAVR dialysis redo analysis artifacts.
- Propensity matching outputs, balance diagnostics, source inventory, code-definition review, figures, PDF exports, paper QA, and run inspection.
- Tick logs 0409-0429 documenting the improvement loop.

These artifacts are intentionally included as regression evidence and examples for future controller/model-runner development.

## Testing

Verified locally before commit:

- `npm run build`
- `npm test -- packages/cli/tests/research-controller.test.ts -t "launch runbook"`
- `npm test -- packages/cli/tests/research-controller.test.ts`

- `npm test`

Final full-suite result:

- 60 test files passed
- 472 tests passed

## Notes / Review Guidance

- This is a large PR because it includes both framework implementation and dogfood artifacts.
- The most important source files to review first are:
  - `packages/cli/src/research-machine/controller.ts`
  - `packages/cli/tests/research-controller.test.ts`
  - `docs/research-controller.md`
  - `packages/cli/src/bin/agenteer.ts`

- The new launch runbook is the practical handoff layer for a future external GPT 5.4 controller process.

author: christianalfoni
body:
## New behavior

```
 Session starts
       │
       ▼
 Continuing existing branch?
   ┌───┴───┐
  Yes      No
   │        │
   │        ▼
   │  git checkout main
   │  git pull
   │        │
   └───┬────┘
       │
       ▼
 Identify workflow & proceed
       │
       ▼
 ... work happens ...
       │
       ▼
 PR requested
       │
       ▼
 Determine branch name
 (feat/, fix/, chore/, etc.)
       │
       ▼
 git checkout -b <branch>
       │
       ▼
 Stage & commit changes
       │
       ▼
 git push -u origin <branch>
       │
       ▼
 ./scripts/upsert-pr
   ┌───┴───┐
   │       │
PR exists? No PR yet
   │       │
   ▼       ▼
gh pr edit  gh pr create
   │       │
   └───┬───┘
       │
       ▼
 Report PR URL
```

Adds three artifacts:
- `workflows/PR.md` — step-by-step PR workflow with ASCII-diagram body template
- `scripts/upsert-pr` — bash script that creates or updates the branch PR via `gh`
- `AGENTS.md` — documents the script, the `pr` workflow, and the session-start branch rule

## Assumptions
The `pr` workflow is a terminal step after `implement`, so no other workflows needed updating. `gh` must be installed and authenticated; the script relies on it being on PATH.

## Instructions followed
- **PR workflow** (`workflows/PR.md`): used conventional commit prefixes (`feat:`, `docs:`, `chore:`), one logical change per branch, never committed to `main`, ran `upsert-pr` to create/update the PR
- **PR body template** (`workflows/PR.md`): used ASCII diagrams for new behavior, included Assumptions and Instructions followed sections, omitted Current behavior (new feature with no prior state)
- **Session-start rule** (`AGENTS.md`): this session was a continuation on `feat/pr-workflow`, so no branch switch was needed
- **Scripts over manual search** (`AGENTS.md`): `upsert-pr` script used instead of raw `gh` commands

author: jhfnetboy
body:
## Summary

- **`removeGuardian` now requires ≥ 2 guardian signatures** (RECOVERY_THRESHOLD) — owner can no longer unilaterally remove guardians
- **Blocked during active recovery** — prevents compromised owner from using pre-collected guardian sigs to cancel an in-progress recovery
- **Minimum 2 guardians enforced** — cannot remove when only 2 remain
- **Signature binds to guardian address** (not slot index) + nonce for replay protection
- **Sig array capped at `_guardianCount`** to prevent gas griefing

## Security issues closed

| ID | Severity | Description |
|----|----------|-------------|
| HIGH-1 | HIGH | Pre-signed removal sigs could cancel active recovery |
| HIGH-2 | HIGH | `removeGuardian` was semantically equivalent to `cancelRecovery` but with weaker guarantees |
| MEDIUM-2 | MEDIUM | Signature bound to index not guardian address |
| LOW-1 | LOW | Unbounded sig array allowed gas griefing |

## Attack path closed

```
Before: compromised owner key → removeGuardian(0,1,2) → no guardians → cancelRecovery bypass → account lost
After:  removeGuardian requires ≥2 guardian sigs AND reverts if recovery active
```

## Test plan
- [x] `test_removeGuardian_revertsIfRecoveryActive` — HIGH-1/HIGH-2 regression test
- [x] `test_removeGuardian_minGuardianRequired_reverts` — minimum guardian enforcement
- [x] `test_removeGuardian_insufficientSigs_reverts` — sig count check
- [x] `test_removeGuardian_duplicateSig_reverts` — duplicate sig guard
- [x] `test_removeGuardian_nonGuardianSig_reverts` — non-guardian sig rejected
- [x] `test_removeGuardian_noncePreventsReplay` — nonce replay protection
- [x] All 745 existing tests pass (0 regressions)

## Open discussion

**MEDIUM-1** (Codex): With min 2 guardians and RECOVERY_THRESHOLD=2, losing one guardian makes recovery impossible (2-of-2 liveness failure). Recommend: prefer `replaceGuardian(oldIndex, newGuardian, sigs)` atomic swap in the next version rather than allowing count to drop to 2. Design decision deferred to owner.

## Summary
- Replacement PR for #95 to avoid force-pushing a stale remote branch after final full-PR-diff scan cleanup.
- Adds a QA/dev-only runtime selector verification and autofill-only slice for the first browser-assisted text-field trial.
- Connects only to local CDP, verifies exactly one page target, inspects same-origin documents/frames, and builds a fingerprint before any fill.
- Requires exact approval phrase plus matching approval/current page fingerprints before filling only Short description, Description, and Work notes.
- Revalidates target host, selector counts, expected text/textarea types, writability, unexpected required fields, and fingerprint inside the fill script before mutation.
- Keeps CLI output sanitized: no raw draft values, selectors, ServiceNow URLs, approval phrase, CDP errors, cookies, sessions, storage-state, screenshots, HAR, traces, or HTML artifacts.

Closes #94

## Why replacement PR
- PR #95 was opened before the final local scan-cleanup amendment was on the remote PR branch.
- We intentionally avoided force-push/history rewrite and opened this replacement branch from the locally verified clean state.
- PR #95 should remain superseded/closed and should not be merged.

## Safety boundaries
- No Save, Submit, Update, or Close.
- No ServiceNow API writes or reads.
- No browser process launch by the runtime command; it only attaches to a supervised local CDP endpoint.
- No mock/production-shadow execution; runtime preflight allows only QA/dev with configured targets.
- Missing/changed fingerprints, selector mismatch, ambiguous selectors, wrong element type, non-writable fields, unexpected required fields, multiple page targets, or runtime/CDP errors all block fail-closed.
- This PR does not run a real QA/dev browser trial. It only prepares the reviewed implementation path.

author: amiantos
body:
Closes #85.

## What changed

The `position: fixed` + `transform: translateY(--viewport-y)` machinery from PR #11 is gone. All four shells (`.mchat`, `.chat`, `.modal`, `.settings-page`) now use plain `height: 100dvh` with normal block / flex / grid layout. `useVisualViewportHeight` is deleted; `--viewport-h` and `--viewport-y` no longer exist. `body` gains `overscroll-behavior: none` to suppress rubber-band bounce.

Net: **+39 / −111 lines** across 8 files.

## Why

Live-instrumented this session on iPad Safari and iPhone Safari. The data showed unambiguously that the original workaround was the *cause* of the visible jank, not a defense against it. During the ~70–130ms between `focusin` and `visualViewport.resize` firing, iOS auto-scrolls the layout viewport and drags the `position: fixed` shell to viewport-y `-498` (offscreen above). The counter-translate then snaps it back in a single frame — that's the vanish/reslide.

Removing the workaround means iOS scrolls the page naturally; the textarea (at the bottom of each shell) ends up just above the keyboard chrome; older content scrolls off the top until the user dismisses the keyboard. No JS animation, no CSS transitions to tune, no race with iOS's compositor.

Full investigation summary is in the issue close-out.

## Verification

- iPad Safari: smooth keyboard slide, no jank during open or close.
- iPhone Safari: smooth keyboard slide, no jank.
- `vue-tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Known cosmetic limitations (accepted, see issue close-out)

- **iPhone Safari**: dragging the page down with the keyboard up exposes a small band of bg between the input row and the keyboard's form-nav chrome. iOS chrome adjustment we can't suppress.
- **Modal + Settings on iPad with keyboard open**: inner fields above iOS's auto-scroll point can end up offscreen. Right fix is scrollable inner content — filing as a separate follow-up.

author: cajasmota
body:
## Why

`archigraph_test_coverage` dumped 100 untested entities to answer a single coverage question (Q7 in iter5 quality bench) → **18× token ratio vs grep**. Most callers want "is THIS entity tested?" not "list everything untested in the repo." This was the dominant driver of iter5's 3.72× overall token blowout.

## What

### 1 — `internal/graph/coverage.go`
- Added package-level `kindTests` / `kindCalls` constants (previously local inside `ComputeCoverage`).
- New `EntityCoverageResult` type: `{entity_id, name, kind, source_file, start_line, severity, tested, covering_tests, coverage_fraction}`.
- New `ComputeEntityCoverage(doc, entityID)` function: same two-phase algorithm as `ComputeCoverage` (real TESTS edges then synthetic CALLS fallback) but scoped to one entity. Returns `(nil, false)` when entity ID is not in the document, returns `(result, true)` otherwise.

### 2 — `internal/graph/coverage_test.go`
Five new unit tests:
- `TestComputeEntityCoverage_KnownTested` — entity with TESTS inbound → `Tested=true`, covering test ID returned
- `TestComputeEntityCoverage_KnownUntested` — entity with no TESTS/CALLS → `Tested=false`, empty slice
- `TestComputeEntityCoverage_Unknown` — unknown entity_id → `found=false, result=nil`
- `TestComputeEntityCoverage_SyntheticCALLS` — no TESTS edge but CALLS fallback covers the entity
- `TestComputeEntityCoverage_OutputSize` — 100 entities in doc, only 1 covering test returned (token-budget guard)

### 3 — `internal/mcp/coverage_tools.go`

## Summary

Mermaid label text in dark theme (`slate` scheme) is rendered low-contrast grey because Material defaults `--md-mermaid-label-fg-color` to `--md-default-fg-color--light` (alpha < 1). Subgraph titles, edge labels, sequence-diagram actors, and any text mermaid emits at the SVG level inherit this and end up hard to read on the dark page background.

Node-internal text is unaffected because every `classDef` in our diagrams pins `color:#0f172a` (the near-black we want on the pastel fills), but that doesn't propagate to outer text.

### Fix

- Override the mermaid label / edge / sequence color vars in both schemes (`default` + `slate`) to use the full-contrast `--md-default-fg-color`, which Material auto-adjusts per scheme (dark in light theme, near-white in dark theme).
- Also target the rendered SVG text classes (`.nodeLabel`, `.edgeLabel`, `.cluster-label`, `.messageText`, `.actor`, `.loopText`, `.noteText`) directly as a fallback for Material versions that don't expose every CSS variable.
- Pin `.edgeLabel rect` and `.cluster rect` to `--md-default-bg-color` so edge-label backgrounds remain a solid plate in both themes.

Node-internal text stays exactly as before — the inline `fill` from each classDef takes precedence over the SVG-level `fill` we set here.

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The Railpack build fails with `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/app/package.json'` because `railpack.json` specifies `"provider": "nodejs"`, which is not a valid Railpack provider name. The correct name is `"node"`. Without a recognized provider, Railpack skips file copying and the entire build pipeline. Additionally, `typescript` (needed for the `tsc` build command) was in `devDependencies`, which are skipped when `NODE_ENV=production` during install.

## Solution

Changed `"provider": "nodejs"` to `"provider": "node"` in `railpack.json` so Railpack correctly identifies and sets up the Node.js build pipeline. Moved `typescript` from `devDependencies` to `dependencies` in `package.json` so `tsc` is available during the production build. A `tsconfig.json` was already present in the repo.

### Changes
- **Modified** `railpack.json`
- **Modified** `package.json`

author: ebenezerd77
body:
## Overview

Adds a full-featured blog section to the Campus Link app, allowing students to write, discover, and interact with blog posts from their campus community or the global student network. Built using Flutter with Firebase Firestore for data, Supabase for image storage, and Provider for state management.

---

## Features / Changes

### Blog Feed Screen (`blog_screen.dart`)
- Displays a scrollable list of published blog posts
- **Campus / Global toggle** — switch between posts from the user's university or the worldwide feed
- Notification bell with an unread badge integrated into the app bar
- Floating action button to navigate to the Create Blog screen
- Empty state UI when no posts are available

### Blog Card Widget (`blog_card.dart`)
- Displays cover image, category chip, read time, title, excerpt, and author info
- Shows a **star rating badge** on the cover image when ratings exist
- Bookmark icon to save/unsave a post directly from the feed
- Author avatar with fallback initial when no photo is available

### Blog Detail Screen (`blog_detail_screen.dart`)
- Full blog reading experience with a collapsible cover image app bar
- Renders blog body using a custom markdown renderer
- **Like, Save, and Comment** action bar
- Real-time comments section powered by Firestore streams
- Comment like and delete support
- Blog delete option for the post owner with a confirmation dialog

### Create Blog Screen (`create_blog_screen.dart`)
- Cover image picker from device gallery (Supabase upload)
- Title, content, category dropdown, and visibility selector (Campus / Global)
- Comma-separated tags input
- Markdown hint in the content field (supports `#`, `##`, `>`, `-`, `**bold**`, `*italic*`)
- Auto-computes excerpt and read time before publishing

### Markdown Renderer (`markdown_content.dart`)
- Custom lightweight markdown widget — no external package required
- Supports H1, H2, blockquotes, bullet lists, bold, and italic inline formatting
- Character-by-character inline parser for reliable bold/italic detection

### Blog Category Chip (`blog_category_chip.dart`)
- Color-coded chip for each blog category
- Categories: Campus Life, Career, Lifestyle, Academics, Mental Health, Technology, Sports, Events, Success Story

### Blog Model (`blog_model.dart`)
- Full Firestore serialization with `toMap()` and `fromDoc()`
- Computed properties: `likesCount`, `averageRating`, `timeAgo`, `formattedDate`
- Static helpers: `computeReadTime()` and `computeExcerpt()` from raw content

### Blog Comment Model (`blog_comment_model.dart`)
- Supports nested comment structure via optional `parentId`
- `likedBy` list with `likesCount` computed property
- `timeAgo` display helper

### Blog Repository (`blog_repository.dart`)
- Firestore streams for blog feed (campus or global) and single blog
- Comments stream with client-side sorting
- CRUD: create, update, delete blog (with batch comment cleanup)
- Interactions: `toggleLike`, `toggleSave`, `submitRating` (transaction-safe, one rating per user)
- Comment CRUD: add, delete, toggle comment like

### Blog Provider (`blog_provider.dart`)
- `ChangeNotifier` wrapping the repository for UI state
- Exposes `blogsStream`, `getBlogStream`, `getCommentsStream`
- Handles `isLoading` state during publish
- Feed mode toggle between campus and global

### Blog Storage Service (`blog_storage_service.dart`)
- Uploads cover images to Supabase `blog_covers` bucket as binary JPEG
- Extracts and deletes the correct file path from a public URL on blog deletion
- Custom `BlogStorageException` for clear error reporting

author: goldenwo
body:
## Summary
Wires the existing, unit-tested risk gate (`gate_entry`/`gate_exit`) and order builder (`build_entry_order`) into the **live** dispatch path so the daemon places **correctly-sized real Kalshi orders** — closing the SC-I2/SC-F2 deferral that sub-project E left open (where `_handle_enter` built `size_contracts=0` and every live order was rejected by design).

- **Entry wire:** live `_handle_signal` consults `gate_entry` (Allow → size via `build_entry_order`; Reject → skip, no-notify); per-decision risk-gate metrics.
- **No-op-gate fix (the critical one):** `risk` + a new `RiskContextProvider` are now threaded through the full WS chain (`_ws_loop → dispatch_message → _handle_*_msg → process_tick`), so the gate is actually consulted on the **real live feed** (previously `risk=None` reached the feed → zero orders).
- **Exit wire:** operator-kill is a true full-stop — `gate_exit` halts entries **and** exits (auto-kills never trap exits).
- **Bankroll freshness:** periodic refresh (TTL/2) + one-time sustained-stale WARNING + gate-time `STALE_BANKROLL` soft-reject + a **drain-then-crash fatal supervisor** (a refresh kill-write failure stops the engine fail-loud after the in-flight drain, never masquerading as a clean exit).
- **Live-only / G-parity sacred:** every change defaults to the paper behavior when `risk is None`; paper/replay is byte-identical.

## Review + gates
- 6 money-path tasks (A3/C2/C3/D1/F1/G1) got **full two-stage** review; the rest combined; plus a final **whole-branch integration + security review** (verdict: SAFE — no secret leak, parameterized SQL, order clamped to Kalshi's 1..99 band, kill cannot be bypassed).
- Review caught 4 real bugs gates alone would've missed/surfaced late: a latent live `AttributeError` (provider read a non-existent `TickContext.market_state`), a red ruff gate, a cross-cutting `STALE_BANKROLL` test regression, and a pre-existing `KeyError` from unregistered metrics keys.
- **ruff** ✓ · **mypy** ✓ (138 files) · **full suite** green except the 19 documented gitignored baseline (12× private `test_flow_strategy` + 7× `parity_first_seen`, absent on CI) · **G-parity 11/11 byte-exact** (paper path provably unchanged).

## Deferred (fast-follow)
- **E2** — opportunistic on-fill/settlement bankroll refresh. A precision optimization (the periodic refresh + `STALE_BANKROLL` backstop already guarantee the gate never sizes against a stale balance); deferred because it touches shipped poller/reconciler code with kill-switch-safety implications and is best done deliberately.

## Test plan (pre-cutover)
- [ ] CI green (py3.11 + 3.12)
- [ ] Pre-cutover **runbook gate**: run the ≥5-real-bundle CR-5 parity sweep
- [ ] Pi cutover: bring up the order-capable daemon with **Phase-1 caps** (sizing_pct 0.005 · daily_loss 0.02 · drawdown 0.05 · max_open 5 · min_fill 3 · floors $30 panic / $50 max-order · $200 bankroll)
- [ ] Monitor ≥3 stable Pi days → cut **v1.6.0**

author: vava-1
body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of the staged plan: make the app actually deploy on Render and give it the minimum surface (Dockerfiles, `.env.example`s) the spec asked for. Before this PR both Render services were broken — `pbi-academy-api.onrender.com` returned `502` and `pbi-academy-web.onrender.com` returned `404`. The root causes were real bugs in the source, not Render config.

This PR is rebased on top of `main` (latest `b4ebbe0` "fix: bypass dashboard DATABASE_URL override by using PROD_DATABASE_URL") and leaves `render.yaml`, the `PROD_DATABASE_URL` value, and the build/start commands untouched. Render is already wired correctly — the deploy just couldn't succeed because the code was broken.

**Backend (`/backend`)**
- `app/api/v1/__init__.py` imported each route subpackage instead of the `APIRouter` instance inside it (`from app.api.v1.exams import router as exams_router` resolved to the *module* `app.api.v1.exams.router`, not the `router = APIRouter()` inside it). `app.include_router(...)` then raised `AttributeError: module 'app.api.v1.exams.router' has no attribute 'routes'` and the worker died — that's what produced the `502` on `pbi-academy-api.onrender.com`. Switched to explicit `from app.api.v1.<pkg>.router import router as ..._router`. Verified `uvicorn app.main:app` boots cleanly locally with both SQLite and Postgres URLs, and `/api/v1/health` plus the per-resource routers return 200.
- Added `backend/Dockerfile` (Python 3.12-slim + libpq-dev for asyncpg/psycopg2 builds). The existing `docker-compose.yml` had `build: ./backend` but no Dockerfile existed.
- Added `backend/.env.example` documenting every env var the backend actually reads: `DATABASE_URL`, `PROD_DATABASE_URL`, `FRONTEND_URL`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `JWT_SECRET_KEY`, `REDIS_URL`.

**Frontend (`/frontend`)**
- `tsc -b && vite build` was failing with 14 TS errors + a Tailwind config load error, so Render's static-site build never produced a `dist/`. Fixes are scoped to the broken files:
  - `hooks/useAuth.tsx`: added `isLoading: boolean` to `AuthContextType` (consumed by `ProtectedRoute`).
  - `pages/CoursesList.tsx`: `str` -> `string`, dropped unused `stripePromise` binding.
  - `pages/Dashboard.tsx`: `course.progress` is typed `number | undefined`, coalesce with `?? 0` in the two places it's used arithmetically.
  - `pages/ExamSimulator.tsx`: removed unused `AlertCircle` import and unused `id` destructure; narrowed `currentQuestion` with `'options' in currentQuestion` so the `.options.map((opt, i) => ...)` call type-checks without `?.` and parameters get string/number types.
  - `pages/LiveClassRoom.tsx`: dropped unused `Users`/`MessageSquare` imports; `DailyCall` is now a `type` import (verbatimModuleSyntax).
  - `pages/Register.tsx`: dropped unused `responseData` binding.
  - `pages/Login.tsx`, `Register.tsx`, `CoursesList.tsx`: API calls were hardcoded to `http://localhost:8000` so the deployed SPA could never reach the API. Now route through `import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL` (already wired up in `render.yaml` to `https://pbi-academy-api.onrender.com`) with the same localhost as a dev fallback.
  - `tailwind.config.js` -> `tailwind.config.cjs`: the file uses `module.exports` and `require("tailwindcss-animate")`, but `frontend/package.json` declares `"type": "module"`, so Vite was crashing at config load with `ReferenceError: module is not defined`. Renaming to `.cjs` keeps the existing CJS-style config working under an ESM package.
- Added `frontend/Dockerfile` (Node 20-alpine + Vite dev server). The existing `docker-compose.yml` had `build: ./frontend` but no Dockerfile existed.
- Added `frontend/.env.example` documenting `VITE_API_URL` and `VITE_STRIPE_PUBLIC_KEY`.

Verified locally:
- `cd backend && uvicorn app.main:app` -> `/`, `/api/v1/health`, `/api/v1/exams/` all return `200`; `19` routes registered.
- `cd frontend && npm run build` -> 0 TS errors, `dist/` produced (`index.html`, `assets/index-*.css`, `assets/index-*.js`).

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Merge this PR to `main` and confirm both Render services flip to green: `https://pbi-academy-api.onrender.com/api/v1/health` should return `{"status":"healthy",...}` and `https://pbi-academy-web.onrender.com/` should serve the SPA (currently `502`/`404`).
- [ ] Heads up: `render.yaml` has a real internal Postgres password committed in `PROD_DATABASE_URL`. It's an internal Render host so it isn't reachable from the public internet, but it's still in a public git repo — consider rotating that DB password and switching to `fromDatabase:` blueprint syntax or `sync: false` after this deploy is green. I did NOT change that in this PR to avoid breaking the existing deploy.
- [ ] Verify the SPA can actually hit the API end-to-end: `/login`, `/register`, and the Stripe checkout button on `/courses-list` — these now use `VITE_API_URL` but the underlying auth/payments routes in `backend/app/api/v1/...` are still mocked, so behavior in prod is "fetch succeeds and returns mock JSON," not real auth. Real auth is Phase 2.
- [ ] `/app` and `/server` still exist alongside `/frontend` and `/backend`, and `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` still targets Vercel + Railway from those legacy folders. The "Run Tests" CI check on this PR is failing — but it's preexisting on `main` (same job has been failing since well before this PR). It runs `eslint` against the legacy `/app/` folder, not `/frontend/`. None of my files are involved. Worth deleting `/app`, `/server`, `vercel.json`, and the Vercel/Railway parts of `deploy.yml` in a follow-up so there's a single source of truth.

### Notes
- The 14 TS errors and the CJS config file have been on `main` for a while — this is why every push since `5c2e490` ("fix: convert frontend from submodule to regular directory for Render deployment") has produced a broken `pbi-academy-web` service.
- I did not delete the existing `print(f"Connecting to database with scheme: ...")` debug line in `backend/app/core/database.py` — it's harmless and useful for diagnosing the next deploy from the Render logs.
- This PR is Phase 1 of the staged plan. Phases 2-7 (real Auth, Dashboard, AI Tutor, Exam Simulator + AI grading, Gamification, i18n + polish) are intentionally NOT in this PR — they'll be separate PRs after Phase 1 is confirmed green in production.

body:
Closes #404

## Problem
When `--fix` runs a package manager command and it fails, the error message gave no guidance on what to check. In minimal CI containers the package manager may not be available, or permissions may be wrong, but users had no way of knowing what to fix.

## Before
Error: Failed to apply fixes: spawn npm ENOENT
Error: Fix command exited with status 1

## After
Error: Failed to apply fixes: spawn npm ENOENT
Hint: Check that `npm` is available and you have write access to node_modules.
If running in CI, ensure the install step has already run before cve-lite --fix.

## Solution
Added a hint to both fix command failure errors in `src/index.ts`:
- Names the **specific detected package manager** (npm/yarn/pnpm/bun) instead of listing all options generically
- Mentions write access to node_modules
- Guides CI users to ensure the install step has already run before `cve-lite --fix`
- Extracted hint to `fixHint` local variable to avoid duplication

## Changes
- `src/index.ts`: Extracted `fixHint` variable and appended to both error throws
- Existing `--fix` success paths are completely unaffected
- All 284 existing tests pass

author: sora32127
body:
## Summary

[isitagentready.com](https://isitagentready.com/healthy-person-emulator.org) のスキャンで未対応扱いだった項目のうち、サイトの性質に合致する「Easy Wins」3点を実装した。

- **トップページのMarkdown content negotiation**: `Accept: text/markdown` 付きリクエストでサイト概要と最新/人気投稿一覧をMarkdownで返す
- **記事ページのMarkdown content negotiation + `.md` URL**: `Accept: text/markdown` ヘッダー、または `/archives/{postId}.md` URL で記事をMarkdown形式 (タイトル/投稿日/タグ/いいね数/本文/コメント/類似記事) で返す
- **`/.well-known/agent-skills/`**: v0.2.0 スキーマ準拠の `index.json` と、サイトの利用方法・エンドポイント一覧・引用ルールを記述した `SKILL.md` を配信。digestはSKILL.mdからSHA-256で動的算出

## なぜ

AIエージェントが本サイトのコンテンツ構造とアクセス方法を低コストで把握できるようにする。HTMLパースを経由しないMarkdown経路を提供することで、要約・検索・引用の品質向上を狙う。

## スコープ外と判断した項目

- Link headers — ヘッダー操作の追加対応が必要、効果に対してコストが見合わない
- OAuth/MCP server/A2A/WebMCP — 認証付きエージェント連携を提供する予定がないため不要

author: wucm667
body:
## 寻求 review 意见

本 PR 已实现完整代码并通过本地测试，希望先听 maintainer 对两个稳健性设计的意见：

### 1. 只重写 codex_cli_rs 版本号，其它 originator 一律透传不动

codex-rs login/src/auth/default_client.rs 列出 5 个合法 originator：
codex_cli_rs / codex-tui / codex_vscode / codex_atlas / codex_chatgpt_desktop。
它们是不同产品，独立版本周期，互不对齐（例：codex_vscode 走 VSCode Marketplace
版本号，与 codex_cli_rs 完全无关）。

本 PR 的稳健选择：
- 仅当下游 UA 匹配 ^codex_cli_rs/\d+\.\d+\.\d+ 时，重写版本号部分
- 其它 originator（含 codex-tui / codex_vscode / codex_atlas / codex_chatgpt_desktop）
  一律原样透传
- 不强制统一 originator —— 把 vscode 改成 cli_rs 是伪造痕迹，反而成为反指纹信号

理由：99% 的 API 网关下游用户实际伪装的就是 codex_cli_rs；其它 originator
正常不通过网关代理，如出现大概率是真实流量，透传 = 不撒谎。

如果倾向同时支持多 originator 版本管理（如未来加 openai_codex_vscode_version 等独立字段），
可在 review 评论标记，作为后续 PR 扩展。

### 2. 仅替换版本号片段，原样保留 OS / arch / terminal / suffix

下游真实 UA 结构（来自 codex-rs/login/src/auth/default_client.rs:133）：
  codex_cli_rs/{version} ({OS} {OS_VER}; {ARCH}) {TERM}[ ({suffix})]

严格匹配版本号片段：
  ^codex_cli_rs/\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:-[\w.]+)?(?=\s|$)

仅替换 "codex_cli_rs/{old_version}" 这一段，OS / 架构 / 终端信息 / suffix 全部原样保留。

锚定细节：
- ^ 锚定字符串起始：避免误匹配 "Mozilla/5.0 codex_cli_rs/0.1.0" 这种历史 hash 测试 UA
  （见 backend/internal/service/generate_session_hash_test.go:523）
- (?=\s|$) lookahead 不消耗后续字符：保留 " (Darwin...)" 部分不被截断
- \d+\.\d+\.\d+ 严格三段 semver：拒绝 codex_cli_rs/0.125 或 0.125.0.0 等异常格式
- (?:-[\w.]+)? 可选 prerelease：支持 0.125.0-beta.1 这种官方偶发的 release tag

如果对正则锚定方式或 prerelease 支持有顾虑，可在 review 评论标记。

### 影响范围（不在本 PR 改动）

下列路径完全不动，保持现有行为：
- account.credentials.user_agent（旧字段，完整 UA 覆盖，最高优先级）
- gateway.force_codex_cli（兜底硬编码，用于非 Codex UA）
- overrideBrowserUserAgent（浏览器 UA 兜底）
- 现有全局 openai_codex_user_agent（仅对浏览器 UA 生效）

新增 openai_codex_cli_version 字段仅在透传模式 + 下游 UA 是合法 codex_cli_rs 时生效，
与上述四条路径互不干扰、可并存。新字段默认值为空，等价于"透传 = 现状"。

## 背景

Sub2API 聚合多个下游用户到同一个 OpenAI 账号时，下游 Codex CLI 版本可能天然分散。上游看到同一账号在短时间内带着多组 `codex_cli_rs/X.Y.Z` UA 版本访问，容易形成不稳定指纹。

本 PR 增加“Codex CLI 版本固定”能力：管理员可以配置全局版本号，也可以在账号 credentials 中配置账号级覆盖。配置为空时完全透传下游 UA，与现状一致。

## 设计依据

- codex-rs 当前 `get_codex_user_agent()` 构造真实 UA：`{originator}/{version} ({os} {os_ver}; {arch}) {term}[ ({suffix})]`，见 openai/codex 的 `codex-rs/login/src/auth/default_client.rs`：https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/login/src/auth/default_client.rs#L957-L1019
- 同一文件把第一方 originator 分为 `codex_cli_rs` / `codex-tui` / `codex_vscode` / `codex_atlas` / `codex_chatgpt_desktop` 等产品族： https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/login/src/auth/default_client.rs#L957-L970
- PR #1940 已经证明“手工 bump Codex CLI 硬编码版本”是实际痛点： https://github.com/Wei-Shaw/sub2api/pull/1940
- 命名对齐项目已有模式：`antigravity_user_agent_version` / `min_claude_code_version`
- 默认行为不变：字段留空 = 完全透传 = 与现状一致
- Go regexp 不支持 lookahead；实现中使用前缀正则 + 下一字符边界检查，等价实现 `(?=\s|$)` 的保留后缀语义
- 组级 UA、自动拉取最新版、其它 originator 独立版本管理都留到后续 PR，避免本 PR 范围扩散

## 改动（分 commit 列）

- `feat(openai-gateway): add rewriteCodexCLIVersion helper and tests`
  - 新增 `rewriteCodexCLIVersion()` helper
  - 覆盖 codex_cli_rs、其它 originator、浏览器复合 UA、空值、非法 semver、prerelease 等矩阵

- `feat(settings): add openai_codex_cli_version global setting`
  - 新增全局设置 `openai_codex_cli_version`
  - DTO / handler / SettingService getter / 缓存 / handler 校验
  - SettingsView 增加配置区块和软校验提示
  - zh/en i18n 同步

- `feat(account): per-account codex_cli_version override via credentials`
  - 新增 `Account.GetCodexCLIVersion()`
  - Create/Edit/ReAuth 账号入口支持 `credentials.codex_cli_version`
  - 编辑时提示旧 `credentials.user_agent` 完整 UA 覆盖优先级更高
  - zh/en i18n 与前端单测同步

- `feat(openai-gateway): apply codex_cli_version rewrite on passthrough path`
  - 仅在 OpenAI passthrough request build 路径接入重写
  - 只在下游原始 UA 是合法 `codex_cli_rs` 且未被完整 UA / force / browser fallback 覆盖时生效
  - 新增网关集成用例覆盖账号优先、全局兜底、空配置透传、既有 UA 覆盖/force 不受影响

## 优先级链

1. `account.credentials.user_agent` 完整 UA 覆盖：保持最高优先级，新字段不改写
2. `gateway.force_codex_cli`：保持现有硬编码兜底，新字段不改写
3. OAuth 非 Codex UA 安全兜底 / `overrideBrowserUserAgent`：保持现有行为，新字段不改写兜底结果
4. `account.credentials.codex_cli_version`
5. 全局 `openai_codex_cli_version`
6. 两者都为空：透传下游 UA，行为等同现状

## 兼容性

- 不改 ent schema，零 migration
- 全局设置走现有 settings K-V 表
- 账号设置走现有 credentials JSON
- DTO 字段为 optional，不影响旧前端/旧请求
- 默认空值不改变任何现有行为
- 不影响现有 `openai_codex_user_agent` / `force_codex_cli` / `overrideBrowserUserAgent`
- 不影响非 OpenAI 账号

## 测试

已通过：

- `cd backend && go test -tags=unit ./...`
- `cd backend && go test -tags=integration ./...`
- `cd backend && golangci-lint run ./...`
- `cd frontend && pnpm install`
- `cd frontend && pnpm test:run src/views/admin/__tests__/SettingsView.spec.ts`
- `cd frontend && pnpm test:run src/components/account/__tests__/CreateAccountModal.spec.ts src/components/account/__tests__/EditAccountModal.spec.ts`
- `cd frontend && pnpm typecheck`
- `cd frontend && pnpm lint:check`
- `cd frontend && pnpm build`

全量前端测试现状：

- `cd frontend && pnpm test:run` 当前有 13 个既有测试/fixture 失败，失败集中在 `AccountUsageCell` 调用参数断言、图表 `formatCost` fixture、`EmailVerifyView` pending auth payload、`settings.authSourceDefaults`、`usePersistedPageSize` 等，与本 PR 新增 Codex CLI version pinning 逻辑无关
- 本 PR 新增/相关测试在全量输出中均通过：`SettingsView.spec.ts`、`CreateAccountModal.spec.ts`、`EditAccountModal.spec.ts`

## 非目标

- 不做组（group）级 UA 配置（后续 PR）
- 不做自动从 GitHub 拉最新版本（PR2 范围）
- 不做其它 originator 的版本管理（codex_vscode / codex-tui / codex_atlas / codex_chatgpt_desktop 全部原样透传）
- 不改动现有 openai_codex_user_agent / force_codex_cli / overrideBrowserUserAgent 任何行为
- 不重构 Claude Code mimicry 模块
- 不引入新的 ent schema 字段、零 migration
- 不重写非透传路径（非透传 / WebSocket / images / chat_completions_raw 四处 UA 处理点）的现有 UA 兜底逻辑

## Summary

Perf-only refile of [#2828](https://github.com/GaijinEntertainment/daScript/pull/2828) — same `daslib/linq_fold.das` change, without the regression tests that triggered the CI-linux-only lint failure tracked in [#2830](https://github.com/GaijinEntertainment/daScript/issues/2830). #2828 stays open while Boris debugs the typer-pass-order bug on a linux box.

When the body of a decs splice's inner for-loop only references `decs_tup` via field access (no whole-var refs), the named-tuple wrap plus every per-element `decs_tup.<field>` read are pure overhead — iter vars already hold each field. `DecsTupFieldFlattener` rewrites each `decs_tup.<userName>` → matching iter var and skips the bind. Falls back to the unpruned-bind path on:
- whole-var refs (bare `to_array`, `push_clone(decs_tup)`, pass-to-user-fn), or

author: k2gl
body:
Fixes a cluster of dev-stack issues that surface on any project with FrankenPHP auto-HTTPS enabled (i.e. `SERVER_NAME` set). All were reproduced on a fresh checkout.

## What was broken

| Area | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| compose healthcheck | `wget http://localhost/healthz` → Caddy 308 to HTTPS on `SERVER_NAME` → cert host mismatch → container **`unhealthy`** forever | probe HTTPS with `curl -fsS -k --resolve ${SERVER_NAME}:443:127.0.0.1 …` |
| `make smoke` | same redirect; also defaulted to wrong port | run the probe **inside** the container against `$SERVER_NAME` |
| console env | `bin/console` has a custom bootstrap without `Dotenv::bootEnv`, so it reads only the real process env. `MERCURE_*` weren't in compose `environment` → `Environment variable not found: MERCURE_URL` on any console command | pass `MERCURE_*` through compose `environment` (mirrors the CI workflow) |
| `make test*` | `phpunit --fail-fast` — not a PHPUnit 11 option | `--stop-on-failure` |
| db/redis ports | hardcoded `5432:5432` / `6379:6379` blocks running multiple franken projects side by side | `${DB_PORT:-5432}` / `${REDIS_PORT:-6379}` (defaults unchanged) |
| Pint | linted the auto-generated, gitignored `config/reference.php` → local `make check`/`ci` fail once it's generated (CI never generates it) | `notPath: ["config/reference.php"]` |

## Notes

- Behaviour with defaults is unchanged (ports still 5432/6379 unless overridden).
- Optionally `.env.dist` could document `DB_PORT`/`REDIS_PORT`; left out to keep this minimal.

Found while bootstrapping a downstream project on this skeleton.

## Summary
- `.agentis/config` gains `audit.persist_actions = true` plus an explicit `audit.signing_key_path = .agentis/identity/private.key`, replacing the silent in-memory default.
- The hermetic bootstrap script now `mkdir -p`s `.agentis/audit/` and `.agentis/identity/` (neither created by `agentis init`) and bootstraps an ed25519 keypair (`agentis identity init` with `openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519` fallback), `chmod 600`.
- Five new `test-run-research.sh` assertions pin the config emission, the extended mkdir, the keypair bootstrap, and the chmod (143 to 148 tests).

## Why
Epic #738 child P1. agentis-core #584 M2 tamper-evident action audit chain is silent substrate in research-foundry today (`audit.persist_actions` was unset, no identity key on disk). This PR activates it with explicit ed25519 signing so audit-ledger rows carry `seq` + `prev_hash` chain fields AND `signer_pubkey` + `signature`, verifiable post-run via `agentis audit verify-actions`.

## Operator security note
Per #584 M2 release note, `.agentis/audit/` becomes credential-grade after this — `chmod 600` is applied to the private key, and forensic readers should restrict read access to operators only. Identity key in `.agentis/identity/private.key` is also `chmod 600`.

## Summary

- **model-worker.ts**: `_cumulativeBytes` was only accumulated via `progressCb({status:"downloading"})`. When OPFS is active, transformers.js calls `customCache.put()` directly and never fires `progressCb` for the CDN download path — so bytes stayed 0.

body: This Pull Request introduces a global theme switcher, allowing users to toggle between Light Mode and Dark Mode. While the user-facing feature is straightforward, its implementation required a substantial amount of refactoring and underlying architecture changes ("plumbing") to ensure that theme state changes propagate cleanly across all application layers, map tiles, and custom widgets. Key Changes & Architecture Breakdown 1. State Management & Plumbing for Theme Configuration Global Theme State: Introduced a state notifier / provider to manage the user's selected theme preference across the app lifecycle. Persistent Settings: Integrated local storage mapping to ensure the chosen theme preference persists across application restarts. Context Propagation: Updated the root configuration (MaterialApp or equivalent) to dynamically rebuild and apply properties based on the active theme state. 2. UI & Component Restructuring Widget Modernization: Refactored a large number of hardcoded color properties in existing views and dialogs to use semantic colors from Theme.of(context) (e.g., colorScheme.surface, colorScheme.onSurface). Theme Switcher Control: Added an intuitive toggle button/option inside the user interface settings to trigger the switch. 3. Map Customization & Integration Adaptive Map Styling: Connected the theme switcher to the map rendering layer. The application now swaps map source tiles or applies specialized dark/light styling configurations dynamically to match the active system mode, protecting user night vision during emergencies. Why are there so many files changed? To prevent a fragmented user experience, every custom card, bottom sheet, and map element had to be adapted to drop hardcoded styles and instead listen to the central theme state. This ensures strict UI consistency when flipping the toggle. Type of Change [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) [x] ♻️ Refactor / Code plumbing (widespread structural updates for theme support)

author: copilot
body:
This PR adds a focused research report on whether Reikan can run as a strictly isolated lightweight runtime on top of existing Linux/Windows/macOS hosts without a VirtualBox-style VM-first workflow. It clarifies where Docker-class isolation is achievable, where semantics diverge, and what operating model is realistic for Reikan.

- **Added: Cross-platform isolation feasibility report (EN/JA)**
  - `research/cross-platform-isolation/cross-platform-isolation.md`
  - `research/cross-platform-isolation/cross-platform-isolation.ja.md`
  - Covers:
    - isolation primitive comparison across Linux/Windows/macOS
    - feasibility limits of a kernel-agnostic abstraction
    - recommended direction: **Reikan Hosted Runtime** with per-OS backend + explicit guarantee tiers
    - additional option analysis for delegating isolation to Docker-compatible container stacks, including explicit pros/cons and positioning as a hosted/transitional mode

- **Updated: research indexes (EN/JA)**
  - `research/README.md`
  - `research/README.ja.md`
  - Added the new report to the Operating Systems survey table.

- **Recommendation captured in report**
  - Linux: first-class target for strict host-level isolation
  - Windows: strong isolation with model differences from Linux
  - macOS: strong sandboxing, but strict parity often requires VM-backed mode
  - bare-metal Reikan remains the primary target, while container-delegated operation is documented with scoped guarantees

- **GPU governance caveat added**
  - Clarifies risks when isolation is delegated to container/runtime/driver layers:
    - Reikan may not fully control GPU visibility/scheduling
    - fine-grained constraints (per-agent VRAM budgets, fairness, deterministic accounting) may be runtime/vendor dependent
    - end-to-end auditable accelerator control guarantees can be weakened in container-delegated mode

Example (new index entry):

```markdown
| [Cross-Platform Resource Isolation](cross-platform-isolation/) | Feasibility of Docker-class isolation on Linux/Windows/macOS for a hosted Reikan runtime | [cross-platform-isolation.md](cross-platform-isolation/cross-platform-isolation.md) · [cross-platform-isolation.ja.md](cross-platform-isolation/cross-platform-isolation.ja.md) |
```

author: fovirdev
body:
# Problem Browsers implement named access on windows object, which means any DOM element with an `id` attribute can be accessed via `window.`. For example, if an attribute's `id` is `process`, like: ```html

Process

``` Then, `window.process` points to a DOM element instead of being `undefined`. And FlexSearch's bundle entry point contains: ```javascript if(typeof module!=='undefined')self=module;else if(typeof process !== 'undefined')self=process;self._factory=_f; ``` When `window.process` is a DOM element, `typeof process !== 'undefined'` is true, so `self` is assigned to the DOM element, causing FlexSearch initialization to fail. # Fix Add a `typeof process.env !== 'undefined'` to exclude DOM elements ```javascript if(typeof module!=='undefined')self=module;else if(typeof process !== 'undefined' && typeof process.env !== 'undefined')self=process;self._factory=_f; ```

## Summary
- Post-merge of #256, the `credential-enumeration` lint job started failing on main even though the same workflow passed on the PR.
- Root cause is nimble's SAT solver, not our code: tagged nph releases either pin `nim < 2.1` or carry broken transitive deps (`toml_serialization`, `hldiff`), while `choosenim` installs Nim 2.2.10. The PR run happened to resolve nph from HEAD and built fine; the main-branch run hit a different resolution path and failed.
- Install nph directly from `https://github.com/arnetheduck/nph` so nimble fetches HEAD instead of solving across tagged versions.

🎯 **What:** Disabled Loguru's `diagnose` feature in local development logging.
⚠️ **Risk:** Having `diagnose=True` active means if an exception is raised, Loguru will log all local variables at each level of the stack frame, potentially leaking sensitive information, API keys, or user data into the standard output.
🛡️ **Solution:** Changed `diagnose=True` to `diagnose=False` in `src/utils/logger.py` to prevent local variables from leaking upon exceptions. The code will still correctly log traceback details without sensitive data exposure.

### Motivation
- Corrigir erros em produção causados por consultas SQL que tratavam enums PostgreSQL de forma incorreta e por referências a colunas/tabelas opcionais inexistentes, evitando que o painel GED quebre.
- Fazer o serviço mais resiliente para que falhas parciais em contadores não derrubem a página nem causem exceções não tratadas.
- Fornecer ferramentas de diagnóstico para inspecionar schemas/enums do schema `ged` no ambiente do banco.

### Description
- Ajusta todas as consultas relevantes para tratar enums como texto antes de operações textuais, por exemplo `upper(s.status::text)` e `coalesce(status::text,'N/A')`, e atualiza as queries do `GedDashboardService` para usar esses casts onde aplicável.
- Introduz checagens dinâmicas com `TableExistsAsync` e `ColumnExistsAsync` usando `information_schema`, e adiciona `ResolveConfidentialColumnAsync` que detecta a coluna de confidencialidade candidata ou escolhe fallback seguro quando ausente.
- Torna o cálculo de documentos sigilosos e a junção de setores condicionais: quando a coluna/tabela não existir, retorna `0` ou `null` respectivamente e registra um `Warning` em `ILogger` sem lançar exceção.
- Preserva e amplia a degradação graciosa com blocos independentes via `TryLoad`, adiciona `try/catch` no `GedDashboardController` para retornar um `GedDashboardVm` seguro em falhas inesperadas, e atualiza a view para tolerar `Model` nulo; também adiciona o script de diagnóstico em `database/diagnostics/diagnostico_dashboard_ged.sql`.

### Testing
- Executado `dotnet build` no ambiente de confirmação e a tentativa falhou devido à indisponibilidade do SDK (`dotnet: command not found`).

---

## 🛠️ Changes
* **`refactor`**: Modularized the JavaScript file structure. Separated state management (task arrays, categories) from direct DOM manipulation.
* **`fix`**: Resolved broken logical flows that caused runtime bugs during task updates, filtering, and state transitions.
* **`style`**: Cleaned up indentation, standardized variable naming conventions (`camelCase`), and eliminated redundant or dead code blocks to improve scannability.
* **`perf`**: Optimized event listeners by using event delegation where appropriate, reducing unnecessary memory overhead.

---

## 🧪 Verified Functionality
The following core modules are now fully decoupled, structurally sound, and operating without errors:
* **Task State Engine:** Smooth adding, toggling (complete/incomplete), and bulk clearing (`Clear Done`).
* **Dynamic Filtering System:** Real-time filtering by status flags (`All`, `Pending`, `Done`) and custom category categories (`Work`, `Personal`, etc.).
* **Live Aggregator/Counters:** State listener correctly drives the real-time update of total task counters and the progress percentage bar.
* **Utility Scripts:** Restructured the integration hooks for the application **Theme Switcher** and the **PDF Export** library.

---

## 🛑 Impact Analysis
* **Breaking Changes?** No. Core features remain identical for the user, but the underlying execution engine is completely stabilized.
* **Dependencies:** None. Pure, semantic Vanilla JS.

Closes #1973

author: agostiniandrea
body:
## What changed

Color tokens in `config/customizations/colors.ts` are now CSS custom properties (`var(--color-X)`) instead of hardcoded hex values. The actual values are defined in `GlobalStyle`:

- `:root` — dark palette (default, all browsers)
- `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)` — light palette override

### Light palette

| Token | Dark | Light |
|---|---|---|
| `background` | `#0a0a0f` | `#f5f5fa` |
| `headline` | `#ffffff` | `#0a0a0f` |
| `paragraph` | `#a0a0b0` | `#6a6a80` |
| `button` | `#1d4ed8` | `#1d4ed8` |
| `button_text` | `#ffffff` | `#ffffff` |
| `stroke` | `#1a1a2e` | `#d0d0e4` |
| `main` | `#a0a0b0` | `#c0c0d4` |
| `highlight` | `#3b82f6` | `#1d4ed8` |
| `secondary` | `#ffffff` | `#0a0a0f` |
| `tertiary` | `#3b82f6` | `#1d4ed8` |

No component files were touched — all color usage goes through `theme.colors.X` which now resolves to the CSS var string.

## Why this approach

Pure CSS — no JS, no `useMediaQuery`, no `useState`, no hydration risk, no flash of wrong theme on SSR. Follows the user's system preference automatically.

## Test changes

- All snapshots updated to reflect `var(--color-X)` values in generated CSS
- Removed `toHaveStyle` color assertions from `Button`, `Text`, and `Link` unit tests — jsdom doesn't resolve CSS custom properties at runtime, so those assertions were false negatives. Snapshot tests cover color output.

## How to test

1. Set your OS to **light mode** — site should render on a light (`#f5f5fa`) background with dark text
2. Set your OS to **dark mode** — site should render on the original dark (`#0a0a0f`) background
3. Run `yarn test` — all 142 tests pass

author: ultramcu
body:
## Summary

A custom `BackupTimeFormat` that uses `.` as a **separator** (rather than as a fractional-second indicator) is silently rejected by `ValidateBackupTimeFormat`, causing the logger to fall back to the default format.

`ValidateBackupTimeFormat` truncates a reference time to the precision returned by `countDigitsAfterDot`, which counts the digits after the **first `.` anywhere** in the layout. For a layout like `2006-01-02_15.04.05` (or `2006.01.02-15-04-05`), the `.` is a separator, not a fractional-second specifier — but `countDigitsAfterDot` reports a non-zero precision, so the reference time is truncated incorrectly, the format → parse round-trip comparison fails, and the format is reported invalid.

### Reproduction

```go
l := &timberjack.Logger{BackupTimeFormat: "2006-01-02_15.04.05"}
err := l.ValidateBackupTimeFormat()
// before: err != nil  -> format rejected, falls back to default
// after:  err == nil  -> format accepted
```

## Fix

Replace `countDigitsAfterDot` with `fractionalSecondDigits`, which only counts a `.` or `,` followed by a run of `0`s or `9`s — the way Go denotes fractional seconds in a layout. A `.` used as a separator (followed by other digits, e.g. `.04`) is no longer mistaken for fractional seconds.

The validation still correctly **rejects** lossy/ambiguous formats (e.g. `20060102-15-05`, which drops the minute), so existing behavior is preserved.

## Testing

- `TestFractionalSecondDigits` (renamed/updated from `TestCountDigitsAfterDot`) covers fractional formats, comma separators, and `.`-as-separator cases.
- `TestSuffixTimeFormat` now also asserts `2006-01-02_15.04.05` and `2006.01.02-15-04-05` are accepted (these failed before this change).
- `go vet ./...` clean; full suite passes with `-race`; coverage **91.9%** (≥ 85%).

Commit follows Conventional Commits (`fix(format): ...`).

body: ## Problem After Brief 48 (full first name), Team Sheet starters rendered UPPERCASE but substitutes rendered title case. Root cause: starters used CSS class `.starterName` which had `text-transform: uppercase`; subs had no class and no transform. Brief 48 removed the JS `.toUpperCase()` from both formatters but left the CSS transform on starters, creating the inconsistency. ## Fix **2 files changed:** | File | Change | |------|--------| | `src/app/(app)/fixtures/[id]/team-sheet/page.tsx` | Added `.toUpperCase()` to both starters and subs `playerName` formatters | | `src/features/team-sheet/TeamSheet.module.css` | Removed `text-transform: uppercase` from `.starterName` class | Casing is now applied in the **data/formatter layer** (single source of truth), not CSS. `.starterName` retains `font-weight: 600` and `letter-spacing: 0.03em` — only the redundant CSS uppercase is removed. **Result:** Both starters and subs render UPPERCASE — "ZAI GALORSOKHI", "AAIDEN LYTHCOTT", "XANDER ALLEYNE", "AARON GILL-HARDING". Edge cases (hyphens, apostrophes, multi-word surnames) handled correctly by `.toUpperCase()`. ## Sub Card — excluded (A3/A4 from brief are N/A) Sub Card excluded — has no data-driven player name surface. The substitution card PDF (Brief 43) is a blank handwritten form with no populated state. A3/A4 from the brief are N/A. Brief 48's original assessment was correct; the digital substitution tracking (Brief 47) lives in the Live Match Tracker, not in the printed sub card form. ## Inspection findings - **Casing bug location:** `TeamSheet.module.css` line 315 — `text-transform: uppercase` on `.starterName` class only (not applied to subs rows) - **Subs row:** `TeamSheet.tsx` line 262 — `{row.playerName}` with no class - **Consumers:** `TeamSheet` — one consumer only (`team-sheet/page.tsx`). `SubstitutionCard/Sheet` — one consumer only (`sub-cards/page.tsx`) - **No shared helper** between Team Sheet and Sub Card - **No other surface affected** — casing change is scoped to the `playerName` prop assembly in `team-sheet/page.tsx` ## Smoke test (post-merge) 1. Verify subs UPPERCASE — "XANDER ALLEYNE", "AARON GILL-HARDING" 4. Verify edge cases (hyphens, apostrophes) render correctly 5. 🚨 Severity: HIGH
💡 Vulnerability: The authentication state check relied on `document.cookie.includes('bt_auth=true')`. An attacker could inject a differently-named cookie containing this substring (e.g., `fake_bt_auth=true`), bypassing the authentication check.
