author: ali-ghafori
body:
## Summary

This branch contains all fixes and documentation updates from the v1.3 debugging sessions. Tested over multiple hours of real AI CLI traffic (Claude Code, OpenCode) through restrictive networks with only occasional connection resets.

### Bug Fixes

- **Zombie session fix** (`cmd/server/main.go`): `handleServerConn` now uses `defer engine.CloseSession()` instead of `defer engine.RemoveSession()`. This sends a `Close=true` envelope to the client so HTTP/2 connections get a clean EOF rather than silently dying and accumulating as zombies.
- **HTTP/2 Write fix** (`internal/transport/conn.go`): `VirtualConn.Write()` now returns `net.ErrClosed` when the session is closed. Previously it silently accepted writes on dead sessions — the HTTP/2 client would write a request successfully, then get immediate EOF on the next read, causing "socket connection closed unexpectedly".
- **TOCTOU race fix** (`internal/transport/engine.go`): Tombstone check and session map lookup are now atomic under `sessionMu`, preventing phantom `OnNewSession` callbacks after cleanup.
- **Upload retry** (`internal/transport/engine.go`): Failed uploads retry up to 3× with exponential backoff; data loss is now logged as a warning.
- **404 vs transient errors** (`internal/transport/engine.go`): Download 404s (cleanup race) are no longer retried, preventing an infinite retry loop on permanently gone files.
- **Goroutine leak fix** (`internal/storage/google.go`): Pipe-writer goroutines in `Upload` are now unblocked via `pr.CloseWithError` on HTTP error.
- **Idle timeout log** (`internal/transport/engine.go`): Sessions closed by idle timeout now log which session and how long it was idle.
- **OAuth2 token refresh logging** (`internal/storage/google.go`): Token refresh events logged with timestamps.

### New Features

- **`-log` flag** (`cmd/server/main.go`, `cmd/client/main.go`): Write logs to a file while also printing to stdout.
- **`CloseSession` method** (`internal/transport/engine.go`): Marks session closed for clean propagation to peer without immediately removing it from the map.

## Summary

The paper was four tables, zero figures. This adds the two highest-impact figures, both pure PGF/TikZ + pgfplots so the CI's existing `texlive-latex-extra` compiles them without any new build dependency.

### Figure 1 — CPG vs training-set size, with val MSE secondary axis (§5.6)

Twin-axis plot. Left axis: val MSE on log scale, drops $\sim\!150\times$ across {200, 2 000, 20 000} transitions. Right axis: CPG with **asymmetric** Agresti-Caffo CI error bars, stays exactly flat at +0.267 with bounds [+0.191, +0.335] in every cell. Single image, single punchline: predicting better did not plan better.

### Figure 2 — Uprightness coverage histogram (§5.7)

Bucketed bar plot of $u = \cos\theta_1 + \cos\theta_2$. Random rollouts ($n = 2000$, red) vs oracle planner ($n = 846$, blue). Visual proof that the upright regime ($u > 1$) is **strictly absent** from random rollouts (0/2000 states) while the oracle planner spends 20.2% of its trajectory there. Caption mentions TD-MPC2's intermediate coverage (max u = 1.439, 10.6% above 1, zero above 1.5).

## Preamble change

`paper/main.tex` gains `\usepackage{tikz}`, `\usepackage{pgfplots}`, `\pgfplotsset{compat=1.18}`. All ship with `texlive-latex-extra` which the paper-pdf CI workflow already installs. No new apt or pip dep.

## Adversarial review findings addressed before PR

- **F1 MINOR** — val_mse at data=20000 was rounded to 0.0004; other cells used 3 sig figs (0.0651, 0.0233). Bumped to 0.00042 for parity.
- **F2 MINOR** — CPG whiskers were symmetric ±0.072 but the real AC CI is asymmetric around the raw point (lower 0.076, upper 0.068, because the plus-4 adjustment offsets the AC midpoint 0.263 from the raw +0.267). Switched to asymmetric error bars via pgfplots' inline-table syntax (`y error plus` / `y error minus`). The figure now draws exactly [+0.191, +0.335] around the raw point, identical to Table 2.

Three minor follow-ups acknowledged as acceptable for v0.15 rather than blocking here:
- F7 — `docs/paper.md` (HTML mirror) not updated with the two figures; will be synced when v0.15 ships Cartpole.
- F8 — float placement specifier `[t]` could be `[!htbp]` for more LaTeX freedom; current CI build shows acceptable placement.
- F8b — legend overlap risk on the twin-axis (two legends in opposite corners); current build is visually clean.

Two paper-pdf workflow runs on this branch are GREEN (run 26330637126 for the initial commit, 26330724627 for the review fixes). Same TeX Live install as production, so the bundle will compile on tag push.

author: oliverwu1024
body:
## Problem

After v2.11.3 the app no longer crashes and the foreground-service notification correctly reverts to 'Sleep tracking active' when audio init fails silently — but the user still doesn't know WHY init is failing, and asking them to grep adb logcat is a non-starter when they don't always have a USB cable to hand.

## Fix

Surface the same diagnostic chain that adb logcat would, directly inside Sleep Preferences. A new \`com.ultiq.app.audio.AudioInitStatus\` singleton holds a single \`MutableStateFlow<String>\` describing the most recent init attempt. Every step in the pipeline writes to it:

- \`SleepTrackingService.maybeStartAudioTracking\` — pref read, mic-permission check, FGS-type upgrade, aggregator init, classifier create, classifier start
- \`SleepAudioClassifier.start()\` — options build, model load, AudioRecord create, AudioRecord state, startRecording(), pipeline-live confirmation

Errors are formatted as **\`<stage> failed → <ExceptionClass>: <message>\`** — one short line, screenshot-friendly.

UI: \`SleepSettingsScreen\` gets a new \`AudioInitStatusCard\` directly below the audio toggle. It subscribes via \`collectAsState\` so it updates live as the next session goes through init.

## How to use after merging

1. Update to v2.11.4 from the in-app banner
2. Start a sleep session (with or without audio toggle on)
3. Open Settings → Sleep Preferences and scroll to "Sleep sounds"
4. Read the "Last audio attempt" line directly under the toggle — it'll say either:
   - "Pipeline live — listening for snore + cough." (working)
   - "Off — toggle is disabled in Sleep Preferences." (off intentionally)
   - "Off — RECORD_AUDIO permission not granted to Ultiq." (system perm denied)
   - "SleepAudioClassifier.create returned null — Android revoked the mic permission at the framework level. Toggle the mic permission off and on in system settings."
   - "<stage> failed → <ExceptionClass>: <message>" (e.g. "MediaPipe classifier init failed → NoClassDefFoundError: …")
5. Screenshot whatever it says and send it to me

## What ships on merge

- \`deploy-landing\`: version.json → 2.11.4, page.tsx URL → \`/ultiq.2.11.4.apk\` (already uploaded), CloudFront /* invalidate
- AAB at \`android/app/build/outputs/bundle/release/app-release.aab\` for Play Console internal-testing upload

author: jlc488
body:
Quick fix for the `build(deps)(deps): ...` (and `build(ci)(deps): ...`) double-scope titles dependabot was producing.

## Root cause

```yaml
commit-message:
  prefix: "build(deps)"  # scope inlined here
  include: "scope"       # dependabot also inserts "(deps)" between prefix and ":"
```

Dependabot composes `<prefix><scope>: <message>` → `"build(deps)" + "(deps)" + ":" + ...` → doubled.

## Fix

Keep `include: "scope"` (the part that varies per dep / group / ecosystem and is genuinely useful), trim `prefix` to just the conventional-commit type:

| Ecosystem | prefix before | prefix after | Example PR title |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gradle (SB3 entry) | `build(deps)` | **`build`** | `build(deps): bump foo from 1 to 2` |
| Gradle (SB4 entry) | `build(deps)` | **`build`** | `build(deps): bump the spring-boot group ...` |
| github-actions | `build(ci)` | **`ci`** | `ci(deps): bump actions/checkout from 5 to 6` |

## Verification

Config-only. CI `detect` will identify zero demos changed (no `*-demo/` paths touched) and build job will skip.

## Test plan

- [ ] Next Monday's dependabot run produces clean titles

body:
TARGET and RRR were visible in first innings because UI gating depended on `innings2` existing, not on the active innings being a chase. This updates Match Center logic so chase-only metrics render only when innings 2 is actually in progress.

- **Scope**
  - `src/app/match/[runtimeMatchId]/page.tsx`

- **Chase-state guard**
  - Introduced a single guard derived from engine state:
    - `isSecondInningsChase = (currentEngineState.currentInningsIndex ?? 0) === 1`
  - Reused this guard across computation and rendering paths to avoid divergent behavior.

- **Target/RRR computation**
  - Restricted target/runs-needed/balls-left/RRR calculation to second-innings chase only.
  - Prevents first-innings precomputation from leaking into UI.

- **Header + stats pills rendering**
  - `MatchHeader` now receives `target`/`rrr` only when chase conditions are true.
  - Stats pills for **Target** and **RRR** now render only during second innings (and still respect match-ended behavior).

author: copilot
body:
XML imports were failing in environments where Dropbox department roots use legacy names (`qualicontax-*`) instead of canonical names (`Fiscal`, `Contabil`, etc.). Both scheduled runs and manual/bulk triggers could scan non-existent paths and duplicate department execution.

- **Department naming model (canonical + aliases)**
  - Introduced canonical/legacy alias mapping per department.
  - Separated accepted inputs from execution set:
    - `DEPARTAMENTOS`: accepts canonical and legacy names.
    - `DEPARTAMENTOS_CANONICOS`: single source for scheduler and run-all execution.
  - Added normalization helpers to canonicalize incoming department values before processing.

- **Dropbox root resolution by existence**
  - Added dynamic root resolver in `DropboxService` to detect which department root actually exists in Dropbox.
  - Updated folder builders (`NOVO`, `IMPORTADOS`, `ERROS`) to use resolved root instead of hardcoded naming assumptions.
  - Added cache/logging around resolved roots to avoid repeated lookups and improve traceability.

- **Execution flow alignment (manual + scheduler)**
  - Normalized department values at endpoint/background-entry boundaries.
  - Updated scheduled and manual “run all” loops to iterate only canonical departments, preventing duplicate/invalid scans.
  - Adjusted summary/accounting to reflect canonical execution cardinality.

```python
DEPARTAMENTO_ALIASES = {
    "Fiscal": ["Fiscal", "qualicontax-fiscal"],
    "Contabil": ["Contabil", "qualicontax-contabil"],
}

def pasta_novo(self, departamento: str) -> str:
    root = self.resolve_departamento_root(departamento)
    return f"/{root}/NOVO"
```

author: steverowley
body:
Closes #370 (with engine-side resolver wiring tracked separately).

## Summary

**The audit's "single highest-leverage PR in the entire roadmap."** Every shipped match previously ran as a polished football sim with atmospheric prose because the 37 reality-rewriting interference types in `src/features/architect/logic/CosmicArchitect.ts:773` were excluded from production by a TODO in `supabase/functions/match-worker/architect.ts:45`.

This PR closes the **narrative half** of that gap: the Architect now actually speaks during matches, picking up to 3 dramatic moments per fixture and emitting in-voice proclamations that surface in the live commentary feed and an `architect_interventions` audit row.

## Architecture — post-simulation, not in-loop

The source `maybeInterfereWith` is a synchronous per-minute LLM call inside the 90-minute simulation hot path. Porting it that way would add ~14s of in-line latency per match.

Instead this PR runs interference selection **after** `simulateFullMatch` returns:

1. `pickInterferenceSlots` scans the events for goals / red cards / late-match tension
2. Picks up to `MAX_INTERFERENCES_PER_MATCH = 3` with `MIN_MINUTES_BETWEEN_INTERFERENCES = 12` spacing
3. Per slot, one Claude call — cosmos may choose `interfere: false`
4. Each success appends an `architect_interference` event + writes an `architect_interventions` audit row

## Deferred — engine-side mutation

The chosen `interferenceType` (curse_player, gravity_flip, identity_swap, etc.) is **narrative-only today**. The engine doesn't apply mechanical effects based on it yet. That's the next slice; this PR closes the audit's "make the headline mechanic visible" half.

## Safety

- Empty `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` → no-op. Match completion is never blocked.
- Per-slot LLM failure → log + skip; remaining slots still attempted.
- Budget cap: ≤3 Sonnet calls per match.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] `npm run test` → 1037 pass (no src/ regressions)
- [ ] Manual: next match-worker tick should emit 0-3 `architect_interference` rows visible in `/matches/:id` commentary + `architect_interventions` table
- Worker tests not added — Deno runtime is separate from vitest (`src/`-only config). Pure-logic `pickInterferenceSlots` could be extracted to `src/features/architect/logic/` and tested there as a follow-up.

author: copilot
body:
Closes the gap between the existing `core/` multi-agent scaffold and a functional AGI runtime across all seven capability areas.

## New modules

- **`core/memory/sqlite_backend.py`** — `SQLiteMemoryBackend`; opt-in via `MemoryStore(db_path=...)` for cross-restart event persistence
- **`core/ingestion/pipeline.py`** — `FileDataSource`, `HttpDataSource`, `DataQualityValidator`, `IngestionPipeline`; writes validated records to memory as `ingested_record` events
- **`core/knowledge/graph.py`** — Pure-Python `KnowledgeGraph` (BFS), `ConceptLinker` (event→entity mapping), `OntologyLoader` (YAML/JSON)
- **`core/bus.py`** — Thread-safe `AgentBus` pub/sub for inter-agent messaging
- **`core/agents/human_feedback_agent.py`** — Accepts structured human input, writes to memory, publishes to bus
- **`core/notifications.py`** — Outbound webhook adapter (urllib POST) with stdout fallback

## Agent enhancements

- **`TrainingAgent`** — `performance_history`, `self_assess() -> {"assessment": "ok"|"degraded"|"insufficient_data"}`, LoRA signal dispatch to `logs/lora_signals.jsonl`
- **`PlannerAgent`** — Attaches `confidence`/`risk`/`priority` to every plan step; sorts by priority descending
- **`GoalEvolutionAgent`** — `horizon` payload param (`"short"`/`"long"`) adjusts prompt framing and is reflected in the result
- **`LLMAgent`** — `ReasoningStep` dataclass + `reasoning_mode=True` payload flag enables observe→hypothesize→conclude chain
- **`LLMClient`** — `ARIA_USE_REAL_LLM=1` bridges to `AGIProvider` with automatic simulator fallback
- **`TaskRouter`** — `classify_intent(text) -> task_type` + `route_text(text)` for NLU-driven dispatch
- **`ToolRegistry`** — `register_remote(name, url)` for HTTP-backed tool calls

## AriaRunner wiring

Self-assessment loop, `AgentBus`, `HumanFeedbackAgent`, `KnowledgeGraph` query tools (`graph_neighbors`, `graph_find_related`, `graph_shortest_path`), and `ConceptLinker.link_recent()` per cycle are all registered automatically.

```python
runner = AriaRunner()
# Knowledge graph tools available out of the box
result = runner.router.route(Task(type="tool", payload={
    "tool": "graph_find_related", "args": {"entity": "improve_runtime"}
}))

# NLU routing
result = runner.router.route_text("plan how to optimize memory usage")
# → routes to planner_agent

# Human feedback ingestion
runner.router.route(Task(type="human_feedback", payload={"message": "prioritize safety"}))
```

No new dependencies — stdlib only throughout.

## Summary by Sourcery

Extend the Aria runtime into a more complete AGI-style system by adding ingestion, knowledge graph, messaging, enhanced planning/reasoning, persistent memory, and self-assessment loops, all wired through the runner.

New Features:
- Introduce a pluggable ingestion pipeline with file and HTTP data sources, data quality validation, and writing of ingested records into memory.
- Add a pure-Python knowledge graph with ontology loading and concept linking from recent memory events, plus exposed graph query tools.
- Add a thread-safe AgentBus and a HumanFeedbackAgent to capture operator input into memory and broadcast it across agents.
- Add a NotificationAdapter for outbound webhooks and support for registering HTTP-backed remote tools via the tool registry.
- Enable LLMAgent reasoning chains with structured reasoning steps and a reasoning_mode flag on tasks.
- Allow the LLM client to call a real AGI provider when enabled via configuration or environment.

Enhancements:
- Extend the GoalEvolutionAgent to support configurable goal horizons and persist horizon metadata alongside evolved goals.
- Enhance the PlannerAgent to attach confidence, risk, and priority metadata to plan steps and to sort steps by priority.
- Update TaskRouter with simple NLU-style text intent classification and a helper for routing raw text into tasks.
- Wire AriaRunner to use a SQLite-backed MemoryStore for persistence, register new agents and tools (including knowledge graph tools), and run a self-assessment loop after each autonomous cycle.
- Expand TrainingAgent with performance history tracking, self-assessment, and LoRA signal logging to disk.
- Extend LLMAgent and LLMClient behavior to remain backwards compatible while supporting the new planning, reasoning, and provider integration paths.
- Augment MemoryStore with an optional SQLite backend for durable event storage across process restarts.

Tests:
- Add an end-to-end AGI features test suite covering ingestion, knowledge graph operations, training self-assessment, reasoning mode, real-provider stubbing, bus and feedback routing, notifications, remote tools, and runner wiring.

body:
Implements Phase A of the admin/HR aggregate dashboard plan (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-18-admin-dashboard.md`): the data model and three ADMIN_TOKEN-gated bootstrap endpoints that Phase B's aggregate read API will layer on top of.

## Key design decisions

- **Cross-org tenant isolation at the schema, not the handler.** `team_memberships` carries a denormalised `org_id` with composite FKs back to `users(id, org_id)` and `teams(id, org_id)`, so cross-org rows are unrepresentable at the SQL level even if a future code path inserts directly. The original draft plan caught cross-org adds only with a handler-level 400; the round-1 plan-eng critic surfaced this as a privacy-contract leak before any code was written.
- **role_grants audit table** captures every authority hop that unlocks Phase B's aggregate org-health reads. UK GDPR Art 5(2) accountability.
- **Conservative privacy defaults from the source plan** accepted as-is (single member/admin role, distribution-only metrics, no individual drilldown). The schema supports tightening or loosening later.
- **All three handler `:id` params UUID-pre-validated** so a malformed id returns a clean 400 instead of PG 22P02 escaping as a 500.

## Test plan

- [x] `node server/test-admin-schema.js` runs 17 information_schema assertions including CASCADE delete_rule on every new FK (Art 17 right-to-erasure path).
- [x] `node server/test-admin-endpoints.js` runs 15 integration tests against real PG, including the schema-level cross-org INSERT regression (asserts raw INSERT errors with PG code `23503`), 22P02 to 400 regressions for malformed UUID `:id`, atomic role-grant + audit-row write, no-op when role unchanged, and case-insensitive UNIQUE on `teams.name` per org.
- [ ] **Reviewer: please re-run `npm test --workspace=server` locally before merging.** The single in-episode test run succeeded (48/48 pass under real PG); the verify-stage re-run was blocked by environment issues (bootstrap PG died with the execute agent's process group; NetworkService-owned backends held the port). The two 22P02 regression tests added during review have not been re-run since being added (3-line regex pre-validations whose tests are reviewable, but worth a fresh run).

## Out of scope (separate future episodes)

- Phase B: aggregate read API + `requireOrgAdmin` session middleware + min-N=5 suppression
- Phase C: admin dashboard UI
- Phase D: employee history view
- Self-service org-admin onboarding (still uses ADMIN_TOKEN bootstrap)

Built via `/dev-framework-rl` episode `01KSA2C6YSMSFFDE0X37PZ3EK0`. plan-eng-critic round 1 FAIL 58 (cross-org leak in original draft) revised to PASS 84. code-review PASS 88. independent-review PASS 86 (one med 22P02 to 400 fixed at root + 2 regression tests). ship-readiness PASS 88.

body:
## Summary

End-to-end crypto-policy distribution lands in this PR. The Cloudflare worker now serves a signed policy blob at \`/v2/config/crypto-policy\`; the iOS client fetches it at boot + every 24h, verifies the Ed25519 signature against bundled public keys, clamps to local bounds, merges stronger-of-two with the bundled default, and publishes the result to \`@Published SecurityPolicyStore.current\`.

## What ships in this PR

### Cryptographic plumbing
- **\`SignedCryptoPolicy\`** wire envelope (Swift + TypeScript mirror)
- **\`CanonicalJSON.serialize(_:)\`** byte-stable serializer (RFC 8785 subset, sorted keys at every depth, no whitespace, no slash escapes)
- **\`SecurityPolicyStore.parseSignedPolicy(_:publicKeys:)\`** with the 4-stage error precedence: malformedJSON → unsupportedSchemaVersion → invalidSignature → invariantViolation
- **\`SecurityPolicyStore.fetchAndUpdate()\`** async fetch + clamp + stronger-of-two merge + cache persist + \`@Published\` publish
- Boot-time synchronous cache read (replaces PR1's bundled-only placeholder)
- 24h periodic refresh task spawned at init

### Worker side
- \`GET /v2/config/crypto-policy\` route in \`cloudflare-worker/src/index.ts\`
- \`handleCryptoPolicy()\` handler with cache headers (\`max-age=3600, s-maxage=86400\`)
- Bundled-default JSON inlined into the worker bundle at build time (\`prebuild\` script in \`package.json\`)
- Operator override via \`env.CRYPTO_POLICY_JSON\` Workers secret

### Tooling
- **\`tools/sign-crypto-policy.swift\`** standalone offline signer (reads unsigned policy + private-key file, emits signed blob to stdout)
- **\`cloudflare-worker/dev-signing-key.json\`** development Ed25519 keypair (clearly labeled DEVELOPMENT-ONLY; production keys live offline per spec §5.3)
- **\`cloudflare-worker/bundled-default-policy.json\`** (source) and **\`.signed.json\`** (output) — v5.4 ship default

### Documentation
- **\`docs/security/crypto-policy-format.md\`** with operator workflow, signing-key custody, schema versioning, rollback procedure

## Production-readiness notes

- **CryptoPolicyPublicKeys Info.plist entry** updated from \`PLACEHOLDER_REPLACED_IN_PR4\` to the dev public key. The PRODUCTION key is generated separately at ship time; the public key bundle gets updated in a follow-up commit pre-release.
- **The worker isn't deployed yet** — this PR adds the code and tests but does NOT trigger a \`wrangler deploy\`. Deploy happens at ship time (PR8 wrap-up).
- **CryptoHardeningMetrics records** policy.fetch_{success,failure}, policy.signature_invalid, policy.version_unsupported, policy.value_out_of_bounds, policy.cache_hit, policy.expired_in_use (spec §8.1).

## Tests added

- \`SignedCryptoPolicyTests\` (2) — wire envelope round-trip + nested-policy shape
- \`CanonicalJSONTests\` (5) — sort top-level, sort nested, preserve array order, determinism, reject unsupported types
- \`SecurityPolicyStoreParseTests\` (7) — happy path + 4 error branches + empty keys + invariant violation
- \`SignCryptoPolicyToolTests\` (1) — bundled-default signed blob round-trip CI tripwire
- \`SecurityPolicyStoreFetchTests\` (5) — empty boot, valid fetch, invalid signature, network error, cached boot
- \`PolicyFuzzTests\` (1, 10K iterations) — parseSignedPolicy never crashes on mutated input
- \`cloudflare-worker/src/__tests__/cryptoPolicy.test.ts\` (6 vitest) — happy, override, cache headers, CORS, route integration

## Test results

**Step 1 — v5.4 suites:** 95 tests across 25 suites, 0 failures ✅

**Step 2 — Regression suites** (RelayTrustGateIntegrationTests + TrustGateTests + ChatIntegrationTests): 20 tests, 0 failures ✅

**Step 3 — Worker vitest** (7 test files, includes cryptoPolicy.test.ts): 60 passed, 1 skipped (pre-existing skip), 0 failures ✅

## Coverage delta vs PR3 baseline

| File | PR3 | PR4 |
|------|-----|-----|
| SecurityPolicy.swift | 100% | 100% ✅ |
| SecurityPolicyStore.swift | 100% (PR3 had far less code) | **91%** — new fetch/cache/refresh paths exercised by fuzz + targeted tests; drop from 100% expected and acceptable per plan |
| SignedCryptoPolicy.swift | n/a (new) | 100% ✅ |

The C1/C2/C3 numbers match the PR3 baseline exactly (77%/90%/77%); the SecurityPolicyStore.swift drop is expected (new async fetch/error paths are exercised but the gate predates the PR4 fetch expansion). author: mshery
body:
## What
Replaces React Router's default \"Hey developer 👋\" error panel with two app-owned fallback pages:

- `NotFoundPage` — friendly 404 with a Go-home CTA.
- `AppErrorPage` — root \`errorElement\` that branches on \`isRouteErrorResponse\`. 404 errors render the not-found panel; any other thrown error renders a generic apology with Reload + Go home.

Wires both into the router: \`errorElement\` on the root route + a top-level \`path: \"*\"\` catch-all.

## Why
Any unknown URL — a typo, a stale bookmark, a removed route — currently shows the React Router development panel. From `.claude/rules/error-handling.md`:

> Show a generic apology — never an internal stack trace.
> Offer a recovery action (Reload, Sign in again, Go home).

This is a production-blocker for any non-trivial deploy: the moment a user mistypes a URL, they see a dev message implying the app is broken.

Caught during production-readiness browser QA.

## How
- `src/shared/pages/NotFoundPage.tsx` — single panel, brand-tokened, lucide icon, accessible heading + CTA.
- `src/shared/pages/AppErrorPage.tsx` — uses \`useRouteError\` + \`isRouteErrorResponse\`. Logs the underlying error via \`console.error\` so the dev / error monitor still gets the breadcrumb, but never displays it.
- `src/core/routing/router.tsx`:
  * \`errorElement: <AppErrorPage />\` on the root.
  * Catch-all \`{ path: \"*\", element: <NotFoundPage /> }\` appended to the routes array.

## Testing
- [x] \`npx tsc --noEmit\` — zero errors
- [x] \`npm run lint\` — zero warnings (had to drop an unused \`eslint-disable-next-line no-console\` once I confirmed our eslint config allows \`console.error\`)
- [ ] Manual: navigate to \`/tenant/orders\` (a real typo a user might make) — should now render NotFoundPage with Go-home CTA, not the React Router dev panel.

## Rollout / risk
Pure addition. Two new pages + three lines of router config. No existing route changes; if a user is already on a valid URL nothing changes.

author: sam-saffron-jarvis
body:
## What changed

- Added `GetLatestVisibleMessageID` to the session store interface.
- Implemented it in `internal/session/sqlite.go` as a targeted single-row query over the `messages` table:
  - filters to visible continuation roles (`user`, `assistant`)
  - orders by newest sequence
  - returns only the latest message ID
- Replaced the full-history `GetMessages(..., 0, 0)` calls in `cmd/serve_responses_durable.go` with the new targeted lookup for:
  - durable `previous_response_id` validation
  - latest durable response ID reporting for a session
- Added a SQLite test covering the behavior that non-visible tail rows (for example `tool` or `event`) are skipped.
- Updated the no-op, logging, and test store implementations to satisfy the new store interface.

## Why this is high-value

These durable response ID helpers sit on hot Responses/web paths, including completion finalization, continuation validation, and ask-user state reporting. Before this change they loaded the entire persisted transcript for the session and deserialized every message `parts` JSON blob just to answer a tail question.

This fix reduces that work from:

- O(n) row reads over the whole session history
- O(n) JSON deserialization/allocation for message parts

…to a single small SQL lookup that returns one ID.

That directly cuts latency and allocation cost for long-lived persisted sessions, which are exactly the sessions most likely to hit this path repeatedly.

## Validation

- Verified the issue in current code by inspecting `cmd/serve_responses_durable.go` and `internal/session/sqlite.go`.
- `gofmt -w` on changed files
- `go build ./...`
- `go test ./...`

author: mark-liu
body:
Faithful behavioural port of mcpguard from Go to Rust. Go is the source of truth; no redesign.

What this is
* `mcpguard proxy` — transparent stdio middleman around any MCP server. Scans tool_response strings for prompt-injection patterns, optionally compresses tool payloads.
* `mcpguard hook` — Claude Code PostToolUse scanner (same engine, JSON envelope on stdin).
* `mcpguard audit` / `explain` — log reader + pattern reference.

Build pipeline (spec-build / Rule #30)
* Opus wrote SPEC.md at `~/scratch/mcpguard-rust-rewrite-20260522/SPEC.md`.
* Sonnet did the mechanical port in a worktree. Opus owned the subtle-correctness pass (panics, UTF-8 boundaries, Unicode Cf table, regex/literal semantics, JSON key ordering, scan-before-compress invariant, SIGTERM forwarding).
* `/codex:adversarial-review` flagged 4 findings — all closed with named regression tests:
  * Codex #1: `truncate_at_char_boundary` shared helper — `&s[..n]` panicked on multibyte boundaries (emoji, CJK).
  * Codex #2: 16 patterns rewritten with explicit ASCII classes (`[\t\n\f\r ]`, `[0-9A-Za-z_]`) — Rust regex `\s`/`\w` is Unicode-aware; Go RE2 is ASCII.
  * Codex #3: `to_rfc3339_opts` instead of chrono::format with a Go layout literal (Go layout strings are treated verbatim by chrono).
  * Codex #4: 7 dead-code items resolved per its guidance.

Parity evidence
* 101/101 unit + integration tests pass on release build.
* Differential battery: 59 fixtures × 3 sensitivities = 177 (verdict + score + pattern-id set + match count) — 0 mismatches vs the Go binary at tag v0.1.0-go.
* Live verified: SIGTERM forwarded to child; Playwright MCP roundtrip through mcpguard succeeded (23 tools, --stats line emitted, 0 false positives).

Notable Rust-specific decisions
* aho-corasick `find_overlapping_iter` (not `find_iter`) — pm-002 is a prefix of pm-001; non-overlapping would silently drop one match. Go's per-pattern `strings.Index` doesn't have this trap.
* `unicode-general-category` crate for the full Cf table — hand-rolled `is_cf` missed Unicode 14+ additions (U+0890 evasion proven concretely).
* `aho_corasick::AhoCorasickBuilder::ascii_case_insensitive(true)` — avoids the lower-then-slice panic; AC returns offsets into the original text.
* `serde_json` with `preserve_order` for JSON-RPC key-order fidelity.
* `signal-hook` + one `unsafe { libc::kill }` for SIGTERM forwarding — audited; SAFETY comment in source.
* No async, no tokio — synchronous stdio proxy via `std::thread`, matching Go's goroutine fanout. Lower deps, easier to reason about.

Audit log invariant (Rule #28)
* metadata only — pattern_id, category, severity, offset, text_len, sha256 prefix. Matched bytes never persisted. Verified across all hit-emitting paths.

Release machinery swap
* delete `cmd/`, `internal/`, `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `.goreleaser.yaml`, `.github/workflows/{ci,release}.yaml` — Go-targeted, no longer needed.
* add `.github/workflows/release.yml` (cargo-dist generated; publishes to mark-liu/homebrew-tap on `v*` tag push, macos-15 runner pin to dodge Sonoma SDK 14.5 hang on macOS 26).
* add `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `cargo build --release`, `cargo test --release`, `cargo clippy --release -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.

Out of scope (deliberately not touched)
* No new patterns or sensitivity tuning.
* No async/tokio refactor.
* No JSON-RPC framing change.

Spec + dashboard + differential artifacts: https://github.com/mark-liu/mcpguard/tree/rust-rewrite

author: 0xartex
body:
## What's new in 1.7.0

### `--help` actually helps now (#174)
Per-subcommand `--help` was silently routing to the parent menu on phone, email, compute, domain, and chat. Fixed: each subcommand now prints its own focused help (required/optional flags, price, copy-paste example). Mirrors the existing `WALLET_HELP` pattern.

### Phone CLI surface expanded from 4 → 18 (#175)
The server exposes 18 `/phone/*` operations; the CLI was only wrapping 4 of them. Added SDK methods + CLI subcommands for the missing 14:

| New subcommand | Endpoint | Price |
|---|---|---|
| `phone list` | GET /phone/numbers | $0.01 |
| `phone messages --id` | GET /phone/numbers/:id/messages | $0.02 |
| `phone calls --id` | GET /phone/numbers/:id/calls | $0.02 |
| `phone release --id` | DELETE /phone/numbers/:id | $0.01 |
| `phone call-info --call` | GET /phone/calls/:id | $0.02 |
| `phone speak --call --text` | POST /phone/calls/:id/speak | $0.08 |
| `phone play --call --url` | POST /phone/calls/:id/play | $0.08 |
| `phone dtmf --call --digits` | POST /phone/calls/:id/dtmf | $0.02 |
| `phone gather --call` | POST /phone/calls/:id/gather | $0.08 |
| `phone record --call` | POST /phone/calls/:id/record | $0.10 |
| `phone record-stop --call` | POST /phone/calls/:id/record/stop | $0.02 |
| `phone hangup --call` | POST /phone/calls/:id/hangup | $0.02 |
| `phone answer --call` | POST /phone/calls/:id/answer | $0.02 |
| `phone transfer --call --to` | POST /phone/calls/:id/transfer | $0.10 |

Phone-number ops use `--id`, call-control ops use `--call`. Each operation is its own per-item paid step.

### Base payments work on fresh installs (#179)
Agents that ran `palmyr wallet create` then any paid command on Base were getting `Failed to build EVM payment authorization — no wallet configured`, even though there was an obvious wallet sitting in the vault. Root cause: Solana had a 5-step resolution chain (explicit → config → env → **auto-pick first vault wallet** → **legacy keyfile**); Base had only the first three. Now matches Solana's auto-pick. Bonus:

- Decryption failures (e.g. missing OS-keychain session secret) now throw a separate, actionable error — `EVM wallet load failed for <id>: <reason>. Set PALMYR_WALLET_PASSPHRASE=… or pass --passphrase…` — instead of the misleading generic "no wallet" message.
- `noEvmWalletError()` differentiates "no vault wallets" from "vault wallets exist but none expose an EVM address" and recommends the right command for each.

## Test plan
- [x] `tsc` clean, `palmyr --version` reports 1.7.0
- [x] `palmyr phone <sub> --help --json` returns focused subcommand JSON for all 18 subcommands
- [x] `palmyr phone --json` lists all 18 subcommands in the parent menu
- [x] Validation errors clean (`phone hangup` without `--call` → `{"error":"--call <id> required","exitCode":2}`)
- [ ] After npm publish: smoke `npx @palmyr/cli@1.7.0 phone search --country US --json`

author: delicioushouse
body:
## DO NOT MERGE without live-dashboard verification

Per [[feedback-user-visible-completion]]: social-content fixes do not count as done until rendered UI in Brendan's dashboard at `aries.sugarandleather.com` confirms captions/hashtags/CTA appear on the right posts and asset→post reverse links resolve correctly.

## Root cause

`parsePosts` in `backend/social-content/runtime-state.ts` dropped `entry.id` while parsing the weekly content plan. Two downstream effects:

1. `normalizedSocialPostId` fell through to `social-post-${index+1}`, so `socialCopyByPostId.get(...)` could not match the planner's `post-1`/`post-2`/... keys and finalized captions/hashtags/CTA failed to attach to the right dashboard post.

2. `createPosts` then hardcoded the same synthetic id on the projected `MarketingDashboardPost`, so `attachPostRelationsToAssets` (which keys by `post.id`) wrote synthetic ids into `dashboard.assets[].relatedPostIds`, breaking the asset→post reverse link the operator dashboard uses.

## Fix (3 surgical edits)

- `backend/social-content/runtime-state.ts`: add `id: string` to `WeeklyPost` type; `parsePosts` carries `entry.id` forward.
- `backend/social-content/dashboard-projection.ts`: `createPosts` uses `post.id || \`social-post-${index + 1}\`` for dashboard post id. Legacy plans that omit id still get the synthetic fallback.
- `tests/frontend-api-layer.test.ts`: un-skip test 56.

Repo-wide grep confirms zero consumers of `social-post-N` format outside the just-deleted test comment.

## Unit-test evidence

- test 56 passes
- `npm run validate:social-content` 92/92
- full `tests/frontend-api-layer.test.ts` 56/56
- `npm run verify` + `npm run typecheck` pass

## Verification gate

Before merging, do **one** of:

- (a) `/pair-agent` against `aries.sugarandleather.com` and capture before/after screenshots showing a weekly post with finalized caption/hashtags rendering correctly AND an image asset showing the correct post in its "related posts" link. Attach both to this PR.
- (b) Brendan verifies manually in his dashboard and posts confirmation here.

body:
## Summary
`execution_quality = submitted ÷ proposed` counted DRY-logged proposals in the denominator, but a DRY proposal can never be "submitted" — it's an intentional non-submission (live trading disabled for that venue/strategy), not a failure. With the book correctly mostly DRY/paper (only `commodity_carry` live), this dragged the score to ~2% and read as "execution is broken" when the one live strategy was submitting fine.

Track `proposals_dry` per cycle and grade `submitted ÷ (proposed − dry)`. All-DRY cycles score neutral (5/10), not 0. Genuine submit failures (live, risk-approved, didn't place) still score low.

author: devxoul
body:
Four small UX improvements to `typeclaw init` aimed at non-developer first runs. Each one targets a friction point identified in the recent init-UX audit.

## Changes

### 1. Inline API-key validation (`src/init/auth/validate.ts`, new)

After the user pastes an API key, the wizard now probes the provider's `/v1/models` endpoint (5s timeout) to detect typos, expired keys, wrong-account keys, and project-scoped keys **before** they propagate into `secrets.json`. On 401/403 the wizard renders a clear rejection note with a "Try a different key / Save anyway" branch. Flaky networks (timeout, 5xx) degrade to "couldn't verify, saving anyway" rather than blocking init.

- OAuth-only providers (`openai-codex`) skip validation entirely.
- Anthropic uses `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01`; OpenAI/Fireworks/Z.AI/Z.AI-coding use `Authorization: Bearer`.
- Goes through `WizardPrompts.validateApiKey` so tests stub it without hitting the network.

### 2. Per-provider dashboard deeplinks

Before each `password()` prompt the wizard now prints a "Get a `<Provider>` API key" note with a direct link to the provider's key-creation page. Non-devs no longer need to know what to Google to find the dashboard.

### 3. Surface `typeclaw role claim` in the success message

When init wired a chat channel (Slack/Discord/Telegram/KakaoTalk — not GitHub, which doesn't gate on roles), the post-hatch `done()` block now leads with a **`Claim your agent: typeclaw role claim`** hint and a separate boxed note explaining that the agent will silently drop every inbound message until ownership is claimed. This was the #1 "why isn't my agent answering?" trap documented in the audit.

### 4. Advertise `typeclaw doctor` in the success message

Adds a `Diagnose issues: typeclaw doctor` hint to the post-hatch summary so users hit by Docker / port / dependency drift can self-serve the diagnostic instead of digging through docs.

## Tests

- 7 new unit tests in `src/init/auth/validate.test.ts` covering provider-specific auth headers, 401 rejection, network-error degradation, OAuth-only skip, and dashboard-URL coverage.
- All 548 existing init / ui / init-pipeline tests pass.
- The 3 pre-existing `--help` / `_hostd` integration test failures reproduce on `main` and are not caused by this PR.

## Follow-ups (separate issues)

This PR ships Tier-S items from the init-UX audit. Tracking issues will be filed for Tier-A/B/C improvements: `typeclaw init --yes`, three-choice provider intro, Gemini OAuth provider, first-task demo prompt, `typeclaw cron add`, pre-flight gate before wizard ends, Slack OAuth-installer, `typeclaw init --resume`.

## Screenshots / sample UX flow

After paste:
```
◇  Get an OpenAI API key
│  Don't have a key yet?
│  Get one at https://platform.openai.com/api-keys
│  Then come back and paste it below.
│
◆  Put your OpenAI API key (will be saved to secrets.json)
│  •••••••••••••
│
◐  Checking your OpenAI key...
◇  OpenAI key looks good.
```

On rejection:
```
◐  Checking your OpenAI key...
✖  OpenAI rejected the key (HTTP 401).
◇  OpenAI key rejected
│  The provider says this key is not valid.
│  Common causes: typo, expired key, wrong account, or pasting a project-scoped key.
│
│  Get a fresh one at https://platform.openai.com/api-keys
│
◆  What do you want to do?
│  ● Try a different key
│  ○ Save this key anyway
```

Success screen with channel wired:
```
◇  One more step
│  Your agent will not respond on Slack until you claim ownership.
│  This prevents strangers from talking to it.
│  Run `typeclaw role claim` to finish setup.
│
◇  Hatched. Your agent is ready.
│  Claim your agent:   typeclaw role claim
│  Attach TUI:         typeclaw tui
│  Follow logs:        typeclaw logs -f
│  Stop:               typeclaw stop
│  Diagnose issues:    typeclaw doctor
```

P2-Wave-2.5 D2 PR — structural-infra changes from `p2_artifacts/reference_findings.md`. Independent of D1; can merge in either order.

### F3 — pre-fix deep-numeric telemetry

**Investigation finding:** The W9 id=91 `§1.8.3.6` deep-numeric headings I flagged in Phase B were generated PRE-P2-F (May 21) when `renumber_headings` skipped renumbering on articles with cross-refs. P2-F (May 22) fixed this: re-running numbering_fix on the frozen W9 id=91 article produces **0 remaining 4+-level numeric headings** after the strip-and-rebuild pass.

**But:** the writer still attempts the violation (30 instances in W9 id=91 before strip). The auto-fix is invisible in drift logs. F3 adds `pre_fix_deep_numeric` to the `cap_violations` dict so we can audit writer-side compliance over time.

### F4 — architect TOC expansion: 8 → 5-14 top-level sections

Phase A showed the reference averages **12.6 top-level sections** vs our **3.5**. Our old `<=8` schema cap was below the leaderboard envelope. New schema is `5-14` with depth-tier-aware guidance:

| Scope | Top-level sections |
|---|---|
| compact / standard | 5-7 |
| deep | 8-12 |
| comprehensive | 12-14 |

Plus explicit anti-filler clause: "every section must advance analytical coverage; no 'misc' or 'appendix'-style filler".

## Expected weighted ΔO

- F3: +0.001 to +0.004 (mostly telemetry; small Readability lift from auto-fixing previously-shipped violations)
- F4: +0.002 to +0.008 (Comprehensiveness lift from broader coverage)
- **Combined: +0.003 to +0.012**

body:
<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
This pull request introduces soft deletion capabilities for customers and tickets, along with corresponding UI controls and permission management.

Key changes include:

*   **Soft Deletion for Customers**:
    *   A `status` column (`active` or `removed`) has been added to the `customers` table.
    *   Removing a customer now sets its status to `removed`, soft-deletes all associated tickets by setting their `deletedAt` timestamp, and sets the status of all associated users to `removed`.
    *   Customer removal is prevented if there are active (open or in-progress) tickets linked to that customer.
    *   API endpoints for fetching customers now filter to only return `active` customers by default.
*   **Soft Deletion for Tickets**:
    *   A `deletedAt` timestamp column has been added to the `tickets` table.
    *   All API queries for tickets, comments, activities, and attachments have been updated to exclude soft-deleted tickets.
*   **Frontend User Interface**:
    *   "Remove" buttons with confirmation dialogs have been added to the customer list, customer detail, and global user list pages.
    *   A new `ConfirmDialog` component was introduced for consistent confirmation prompts.
    *   A `canRemoveUser` permission helper was implemented to control the visibility and functionality of these remove actions based on the requesting user's role and the target user's role/customer association.
*   **Documentation**:
    *   The `SUMMARY.md` file has been extensively updated to provide a comprehensive overview of the project's features, including the new soft-delete functionality, detailed API endpoints, permission system, integrations (Discord, GitHub, S3), and the cloud SSO/iframe integration.
    *   New documentation (`docs/infra-sso-rs256-setup.md`) has been added for setting up RS256 SSO with `kodus-ai`.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

author: waymedev
body:
## Summary

The sidebar's Refresh All only kicked the RSS scheduler + IMAP newsletter poll, so every `readwise://reader/later` source stayed stale until the user opened Settings and clicked Sync Now.

Root cause: `db::feeds_to_refresh` deliberately skips the synthetic Readwise feed (`WHERE source_type NOT IN ('newsletter', 'readwise')`) because Reader uses a paginated, throttled HTTP API rather than a feed-document fetch — but `refresh_all` had no parallel polling step for it. The Reader integration only existed behind the manual `readwise_reader_sync` Tauri command on the Settings panel.

Fix (minimal, single-source): add a `poll_readwise_reader` step to `refresh_all`, mirroring the existing `poll_newsletters`. It reads the user's last-saved category / withHtml settings (same keys the Settings panel writes — `readwise_reader_category`, `readwise_reader_with_html`), reuses `readwise_reader::fetch_documents` + `db::upsert_readwise_document`, and tallies new docs into the same Refresh All total so the "N new" toast covers Reader too.

Touched files: `src-tauri/src/ingestion/scheduler.rs` only.

## Behavioral notes

- No token configured → skip silently (returns 0). A user who never set up Reader shouldn't see an error toast on every refresh.
- Network / API failure → recorded as the Readwise feed's `fetch_error`, same as RSS / newsletter failures. The refresh continues.
- DB writes use a short critical section (token + settings read up front, HTTP pull outside the lock, upserts inside one lock) — matches the existing `readwise_reader_sync` discipline so the writer lock isn't held across the slow 20-req/min API pull.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check` — clean
- [x] `cargo test --lib` — 211 / 211 pass
- [x] `cargo clippy --lib -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `pnpm test` — 70 / 70 pass
- [ ] Manual: configure a Readwise token + a Reader doc, click Refresh All, verify Reader docs sync (and the same click still refreshes RSS / newsletters).

## Summary

Adds `test/validation_test.dart` (19 tests) pinning the behaviour the **Dart wrapper itself owns** — argument validation, error mapping, streaming-context state, and the data plumbing around the FFI boundary. It deliberately does not re-verify BoringSSL's cryptographic correctness, which the existing KAT/round-trip suites already cover.

## What's covered

- **`getRandomValues`**: 65536-byte limit, the boundary itself, and `lengthInBytes` handling for non-`Uint8List` `TypedData`.
- **AES key/IV guards**: the CTR/GCM invalid-key-length paths and the CBC/CTR IV-length paths that weren't previously exercised (CBC key length was already covered).
- **Streaming contexts** (AES-CBC, Hash): `update` + `finish` equals the one-shot result, and `StateError` once the context is finished.
- **KDF**: PBKDF2 non-positive iteration counts and unsupported-hash rejection.
- **EC keys**: unsupported curve, unparseable SPKI, and curve-mismatch on import.
- **`constantTimeEq`**: length and content branches.

The file header documents the suite's intent (wrapper contract, not crypto correctness).

author: williamzujkowski
body:
Two `pip install`s at the same commit could previously resolve to different transitive trees — and one might pick up a CVE in a transitive the other didn't have. `uv.lock` fixes that: every CI run, every cf push, every developer install resolves to exactly the same pinned set.

## What's added

- **`uv.lock`** at the repo root — 133 packages, ~480 KB. Generated by `uv lock` against the current `pyproject.toml`. Stays committed; reviewers eyeball the diff on dep refreshes the way they would for any infra change.
- **`make lock` target** — regenerates `uv.lock` against `pyproject.toml`.
- **`docs/dependencies.md`** — daily workflow, lockfile semantics, refresh cadence, the dependabot interaction (range-bump PRs from dependabot will trip `--frozen` and need `make lock` in the same PR).
- **`docs/configuration.md`** + **`AGENTS.md`** — short pointers to the new doc.

## CI changes (verify, integration, sbom-scan jobs)

- Drop `pip install --upgrade pip; pip install -e ".[dev,db,ingestion]"`.
- Add `astral-sh/setup-uv@v6` step (with cache).
- Replace install with `uv sync --frozen --extra dev --extra db --extra ingestion`. **`--frozen` refuses to mutate the lock** — a PR that updated `pyproject.toml` without running `make lock` now fails fast at the install step rather than silently drifting.
- Add `echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"` so subsequent steps (ruff, mypy, pytest, bandit, pip-audit, syft) find binaries in the new venv without each step needing `uv run`.
- Drop `cache: pip` from setup-python — uv has its own cache.

## Out of scope

- **`[real-embeddings]` and `[otel]` extras** — neither is in the default sync set. Both are deploy-time choices (heavy local inference; opt-in tracing). `docs/dependencies.md` documents this.
- **Dependabot auto-relock** — dependabot won't run `make lock` itself; documented as a manual step on dependabot PRs.

## Verification

- `uv sync --frozen --extra dev --extra db --extra ingestion` — resolves to 133 packages, ~25 s cold / ~3 s warm.
- `.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit -q --no-cov` — **688 pass, 2 skip** (the two `[otel]`-gated tests; `[otel]` is not in the sync set by design).
- `.venv/bin/pip-audit --skip-editable` — **zero known vulnerabilities** (PR #195's CVE-fixed floors carried through to the lock).
- `.venv/bin/ruff check src tests` + `mypy src` — clean.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Visible | `< lg` (< 1024 px) |

body:
## Summary

Takes the scanner from the 8.2/10 rating the ChatGPT review gave it to a closer-to-institutional setup, and ships the previously-approved recommender crash fix in the same PR.

### Z0 — Recommender None-format crash fix (was previously approved but unshipped)

- `recommend_action` line ~1755 built an f-string outside the `_gt` guards; when yfinance returned `debtToEquity: None`, `f"{None:.2f}"` raised `TypeError: unsupported format string passed to NoneType.__format__` and the whole Deep Dive card collapsed to "Recommender error". Replaced with a value-based critical-bear check.
- Every bull/bear `append` now runs through a `_flag(cond_fn, fmt_fn)` helper — any single bad value silently drops just that bullet.
- Whole `recommend_action` wrapped in a top-level `try/except` returning a HOLD stub on unexpected failures, so one per-stock edge case can never blank out the card.
- `estimate_upside` ATR-based target capped at `2 × min(ATR%, 25%)`; Fibonacci extension capped at `2 × price`; all candidates sanity-bounded to `[1.02·price, 3·price]`.
- `recommend_action.targets`: rename `"fib" → "technical"`, every target validated to be within `[0.5·price, 5·price]` (drops yfinance analyst targets of `0.01` or `999,999`).

### Z1 — Market Regime Filter

`compute_market_regime` reads Nifty position vs 50/200 DMA, MA50 slope, `^INDIAVIX` band, breadth above MA50/MA200, % at 52W highs. Composite score 0-100 → `AGGRESSIVE` / `SELECTIVE` / `DEFENSIVE` label with score multiplier `1.0 / 0.85 / 0.7` baked into the Grade. New banner above the tabs row.

### Z2 — Sector Leadership Engine

New `SECTOR_INDICES` mapping our 14 sectors to NSE indices (`^NSEBANK`, `^CNXIT`, `^CNXPHARMA`, `^CNXAUTO`, `^CNXMETAL`, `^CNXENERGY`, `^CNXFMCG`, `^CNXREALTY`, `^CNXFIN`, `^CNXMEDIA`, `^CNXINFRA`, `^CNXCONSUM`). `compute_sector_strength` ranks them by `0.4·3M + 0.3·1M + 0.2·above-DMA + 0.1·breadth` → Top 5 = "In play", 6-10 "Watch", else "Laggard". Old "Sector Heatmap" tab is now "Sector Leadership" with the new ranking on top and the in-scan breakdown below. Top-5 sector membership feeds into Grade.

### Z3 — Minervini-style RS Percentile Rank

`attach_rs_rank` adds an `RS_Rank` (0-99) column = percentile of `RS vs Nifty` across the scan universe. `RS_Rank ≥ 90` replaces the old "RS > 1.1" flag in `recommend_action`. Coloured column in the Momentum Scan table.

### Z4 — Base Pattern Detection (VCP, Flat Base, Cup-and-Handle)

Three vectorised detectors built on a 5-bar swing-extrema scan; each returns `{name, quality (0-100), key_levels}` or `None`. `detect_base_pattern` picks the highest-quality match ≥50. `Pattern` + `Pattern Q` columns added to scan output and the Search Stock tab.

### Z5 — Conviction Grade A+ / A / B+ / B / C

`attach_grade` blends `0.35·Score + 0.20·RS_Rank + 0.15·sector_in_top5 + 0.10·pattern_q + 0.10·regime + 0.10·stage` → 0-100 → letter grade. New Grade column in the scan table with colour coding. "A+ Picks" KPI added to the top strip.

### Z6 — Edge flag (free tier)

`New 52W High` boolean (price within 0.5% of 52W high). ATH and earnings-within-15d flags are deferred to a follow-up since they need per-stock Ticker calls (and per-stock Crumb hits).

### Deferred to future work (paid data / scraping)

Documented in the plan: delivery volume %, FII/DII flows, mutual-fund holdings, insider transactions, block/bulk deals, options OI, earnings transcript sentiment, theme tagging maintenance.

author: kitsuyui
body:
## Problem

The text output loop uses INT 10h/AH=0Eh (TTY write character) without first
explicitly setting a video mode. BIOS INT 10h TTY output depends on the active
video mode; if firmware does not initialize to text mode, output is silently
lost or corrupted.

BIOS typically boots into text mode (mode 3: 80×25 color), but this is
convention, not a guarantee. Some BIOS implementations and emulator
configurations may start in a graphics mode.

## Change

Add INT 10h/AH=00h (set video mode) with AL=03h (mode 3, 80×25 color text)
before the print loop. This makes the text-mode assumption explicit and ensures
portable output behavior across BIOS implementations.

Two named constants are introduced to document the values:
- `BIOS_FUNCTION_SET_VIDEO_MODE` (0x00)
- `VIDEO_MODE_TEXT_80x25` (0x03)

## Verification

- `make` succeeds; binary output remains exactly 512 bytes.
- The `times` padding recalculates automatically for the 4 additional bytes.
- String output loop logic is unchanged.

author: briandevans
body:
## What does this PR do?

On Windows, when Hermes runs from a venv via a Scheduled Task with a restricted `PATH`, the kanban dispatcher's `_resolve_hermes_argv()` (and the gateway's parallel `_resolve_hermes_bin()`) can resolve a *different* interpreter's `hermes.exe` console-script launcher (e.g. the system Python's, leftover on PATH) instead of the venv's. Spawning that `.exe` then dies with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_cli'` because the system interpreter has no `__editable__` `.pth` for the venv's editable install — the worker never starts, and the kanban task stays stuck in `running`.

Add a Windows-venv guard to both resolvers: when `_IS_WINDOWS` AND running from a venv (`$VIRTUAL_ENV` set OR `sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix`) AND `$HERMES_BIN` is not explicitly set, go straight through `sys.executable -m hermes_cli.main` so the venv's own interpreter is used directly and the pip launcher is bypassed entirely.

`$HERMES_BIN` still wins so operators can pin a specific shim. Non-Windows code paths and non-venv Windows code paths are unchanged.

> Mirrors `gateway.run._resolve_hermes_bin` precedence: `\$HERMES_BIN` > Windows-venv guard > `shutil.which(\"hermes\")` > `sys.executable -m hermes_cli.main`. Both resolvers get the same guard because both spawn detached `hermes` subprocesses that hit the same restricted-PATH Scheduled-Task / detached-process context.

> Audited siblings: confirmed there are exactly two `hermes` argv resolvers in the tree — `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py::_resolve_hermes_argv` (worker spawn) and `gateway/run.py::_resolve_hermes_bin` (detached `/restart`, `hermes update`). Both are patched. No other code paths spawn the `hermes` CLI as a subprocess.

## Related Issue

Fixes #30943

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- \`hermes_cli/kanban_db.py\` — add module-level \`_running_in_venv()\` helper; insert Windows-venv guard in \`_resolve_hermes_argv()\` between the \`HERMES_BIN\` branch and the \`shutil.which\` lookup; expand docstring with the new step #2.
- \`gateway/run.py\` — insert the equivalent Windows-venv guard inline in \`_resolve_hermes_bin()\` (kept inline because the function already inlines the \`importlib.util.find_spec\` fallback); update docstring.
- \`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py\` — 5 new tests: Windows venv via \`\$VIRTUAL_ENV\`, Windows venv via \`sys.prefix\` divergence (unactivated), Windows non-venv still uses shim, POSIX venv still uses shim, \`HERMES_BIN\` override beats venv guard.
- \`tests/gateway/test_update_command.py\` — 4 new tests covering the same matrix for \`_resolve_hermes_bin\`.

## How to Test

\`\`\`
uv run --with pytest --with pytest-xdist --with pytest-asyncio --with pytest-timeout python3 -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_db.py tests/gateway/test_update_command.py tests/gateway/test_restart_drain.py
\`\`\`

Expected: 9 new tests pass + 207 existing resolver / update / restart tests continue to pass (216 total).

Regression-guard: I verified the bug behavior by stashing only the production-code changes (keeping the new tests) — all 4 Windows-venv tests then fail with exactly the reported symptom (resolver returns the wrong \`.exe\` shim instead of falling through to \`sys.executable -m hermes_cli.main\`). With the production code restored, they pass.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (\`fix(scope):\`, \`feat(scope):\`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run focused tests for the touched code and all pass
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: macOS 15.x (Windows behavior exercised via monkeypatched \`_IS_WINDOWS\` / \`sys.platform\` / \`sys.prefix\` / \`\$VIRTUAL_ENV\`)

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, \`docs/\`, docstrings) — docstrings on both resolvers now describe the new precedence step
- [x] I've updated \`cli-config.yaml.example\` if I added/changed config keys — N/A
- [x] I've updated \`CONTRIBUTING.md\` or \`AGENTS.md\` if I changed architecture or workflows — N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — the guard is gated on \`_IS_WINDOWS\` / \`sys.platform == \"win32\"\` so POSIX behavior is unchanged
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — N/A

## Related / Positioning

Adjacent prior work in this area:

- #28398 (merged, teknium1 salvage of #27483) — added \`_is_windows_batch_shim\` / \`_safe_which_no_cwd\` to avoid launching \`.cmd\`/\`.bat\` shims as argv[0] and to skip the \`.\`-on-PATH attack. **Orthogonal**: that fix handles the case where the *shape* of the resolved shim is unsafe; this PR handles the case where the *interpreter behind* the resolved \`.exe\` is wrong.
- #23222 (merged, teknium1 salvage of #23198) — established the \`sys.executable -m hermes_cli.main\` fallback when no shim is on PATH. This PR uses the same fallback but triggers it earlier on a more specific condition (Windows venv with \`HERMES_BIN\` unset).
- #24528 (closed, shanewas) — proposed an \`importlib.util.find_spec(\"hermes_cli\")\` check before returning the module form. Different concern (defensive import check vs. cross-interpreter avoidance); both could coexist but this PR doesn't depend on it.

## Screenshots / Logs

N/A — covered by the new regression tests. The user's reproduction in the issue body (\`hermes gateway\` via Scheduled Task in a venv, kanban worker spawn → \`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_cli'\`) is exercised by \`test_resolve_hermes_argv_windows_venv_prefers_module_form\` and \`test_resolve_hermes_argv_windows_unactivated_venv_prefers_module_form\`.

author: yehazkiell
body:
This PR hardens the security foundation of Kiel-AI by addressing two critical bypass vectors:
1. **Base64 Obfuscation in non-Latin scripts**: The previous Base64 detector relied on ASCII printability, which failed to detect prompts encoded in scripts like Chinese or Arabic. The new logic uses UTF-8 validation and control character ratio analysis to accurately detect encoded text across all languages.
2. **SSRF via non-canonical IPv4-in-IPv6**: Attacker-controlled URLs like `https://[::ffff:0177.0.0.1]` (octal) or `https://0x7f000001` (hex) could bypass string-based filters before being normalized by the URL parser. The hardened host extraction now manually inspects raw host components for these non-canonical prefixes in both standard and bracketed formats.

All changes have been verified with targeted reproduction tests and the full security suite (89 tests).

author: geniuskey
body:
Previously the top-down view rendered each lens group as an independent symmetric superellipse, even when neighbors had very different sizes. Real CIS reflow + plasma etch couples adjacent OCLs through two documented mechanisms, both of which now appear in the Top view as visible asymmetry around heterogeneous boundaries.

Model:

- For each lens group G and each of its 4 sides, identify the neighbor group N along that side using the bbox midpoint cell.
- Mass-flow asymmetry (Choi et al.; Stanford E241 reflow survey): dSpread_side = k_mass * thermal_dose * sigma_s, sigma_s = (A_N - A_G) / (A_N + A_G) The smaller lens edge bulges toward the larger neighbor; the bigger lens contracts symmetrically on its small-neighbor side. Sigma is 0 for same-size pairs and grid edges, so all-1x1 / all-2x2 layouts reduce exactly to the previous independent model.
- Plasma microloading (Mogab 1977; Gottscho et al. 1992): dGap_side = k_load * v_lat * t_etch * rho_s, rho_s = max(0, (A_G + A_N - 2) / 6) Dense neighborhoods deplete etchant and slow lateral closure, so the boundary between a 1x1 and a 2x2 OCL ends up with a slightly larger residual gap than a 1x1-1x1 boundary.

UI:

- Top view final-footprint path uses a new asymmetric superellipse with per-quadrant radii from the four side-edge offsets, so heterogeneous layouts visibly pull lenses toward larger neighbors.
- Gap markers use the per-side gaps, not the symmetric finalGapX/Y.
- New Calibration sliders: 'Proximity coupling gain' (k_mass scale) and 'Microloading gain' (k_load scale), default 1.0x, range 0~2.0; setting either to 0 recovers the original independent-lens behavior.
- New status flag 'proximity asymmetry' when any group's per-side sigma spread exceeds 0.6 (e.g., a 1x1 with a 2x2 on one side and a 1x1 on the other).

Theory & references:

- New 9th formula in SimulatorTheory documenting sigma_s, dSpread_side, rho_s, dGap_side and the k_m/k_l gains. Playwright formula-row count updated 8 -> 9.
- New references: Lee et al. (Covered Microlens, COPP 2023), Mogab (loading effect, 1977), Gottscho et al. (microscopic uniformity, 1992), and a grouped citation of Sony/Samsung/OmniVision OCL design-rule patents (US8941766, US11765476, US12022217, US12069384).
- EN/KO markdown pages updated with the new mechanism bullet and reference entries; 'Known Missing Physics' clarifies the surrogate does not solve Young-Laplace flow between islands.

author: ldsenow
body:
## Summary

The project's `.claude/settings.json` failed schema validation and, more importantly, two of its hooks **never executed**. This PR fixes the schema, rewrites the affected hooks to run natively on Windows, and provisions `pwsh` in the remote Linux environment so the same hooks work there too.

## What was wrong

`PostToolUse` and `PreToolUse` placed `matcher` + `command` as siblings, missing the schema-required nested `hooks: [...]` array. Effects:
- IDE/schema validation flagged the file as invalid.
- Claude Code only runs commands found *inside* the nested array, so **both hooks were silently no-ops**.
- The protect-file hook used bash `exit 1`, which doesn't block `PreToolUse` anyway (only `exit 2` / a `permissionDecision: deny` payload does).

## Changes

**`.claude/settings.json`** (commit `0c44b66`)
- Nest both hooks correctly under `hooks: [...]`.
- Rewrite both as Windows-native PowerShell (`"shell": "powershell"`), reading the edited file from the hook's stdin JSON (`tool_input.file_path`) instead of the unreliable `$CLAUDE_FILE_PATH`.
  - **PostToolUse**: `dotnet format` `.cs` files only; guarded with `try/catch` + `exit 0` so it never blocks.
  - **PreToolUse**: block edits to `packages.lock.json`, `.editorconfig`, `Directory.Build.props` via a `permissionDecision: deny` payload, matching the exact leaf filename (`Split-Path -Leaf` + `-in`) — no fragile regex, and no over-matching of lookalikes like `my-packages.lock.json`.
- `SessionStart` left as-is: it is a remote-Linux-only SDK installer.

**`.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`** (commit `e25a6c9`)
- Install PowerShell as a .NET global tool (`dotnet tool install --global PowerShell`) during the remote bootstrap, so the PowerShell hooks can run in the Claude Code on the web environment too (no `pwsh` there by default).
- Add `$DOTNET_ROOT/tools` to `PATH` so the installed `pwsh` is discoverable.
- Guard the install for idempotency under `set -euo pipefail`; add a `pwsh --version` canary.

## Verification

- `python -m json.tool` — settings.json is valid JSON.
- `jq` — all three events expose a reachable command hook through the nested array.
- **Behavioral pipe-test** (synthetic stdin JSON → `pwsh`):
  - PreToolUse emits deny JSON for all three protected files.
  - PreToolUse allows an ordinary `.cs` file (empty output, exit 0).
  - PreToolUse does **not** over-match `my-packages.lock.json`.
  - PostToolUse skips `dotnet` cleanly (exit 0) for non-existent / non-`.cs` paths.
- `bash -n` — session-start.sh has no syntax errors.
- NuGet — package `powershell` 7.6.2 (Microsoft, Verified) confirmed; .NET 10 SDK already in the install list satisfies its runtime.

## Caveat not yet exercised

The remote install path is gated behind `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true` and only runs in the Linux web sandbox, so `dotnet tool install` first executes on the next remote session. The startup log line `[session-start] pwsh version:` confirms success.

body: ## Problem The `ProjectInputStepView` component is used in two different contexts: | Context | File | Step Position | Back Action | |---------|------|---------------|-------------| | **OnboardingApp** | `OnboardingApp.cs` | 3rd step of 4 | Navigates to previous step | | **AddProjectDialog** | `AddProjectDialog.cs` | **1st step of 3** | Closes the dialog (`CancelAndClose()`) | In `AddProjectDialog`, the view is the **first step** in the flow — there is no previous step to navigate back to. However, the button was hardcoded as **"← Back"**, which is misleading. The `onBack` action actually calls `CancelAndClose()`, so the button should reflect that. ## What needed to be done The button label and icon needed to adapt to the context: - When used as a **middle/later step** (e.g. in Onboarding) → show **"← Back"** with an arrow icon - When used as the **first step** (e.g. in AddProjectDialog) → show **"Cancel"** without an arrow icon ## What was changed ### `ProjectInputStepView.cs` - Added a new optional constructor parameter `backButtonText` (default: `"Back"`) — following the existing pattern already used for `skipButtonText` and `nextButtonText` - The button now uses `backButtonText` instead of the hardcoded `"Back"` string - The arrow icon (`Icons.ArrowLeft`) is now **conditionally rendered** — it only appears when the button text is `"Back"`, and is hidden for `"Cancel"` since a left arrow doesn't make sense for a cancel action ### `AddProjectDialog.cs` - Passed `backButtonText: "Cancel"` when constructing `ProjectInputStepView` at step 0 ### No changes to `OnboardingApp.cs` The default value `"Back"` preserves the existing behavior — no modifications needed. ## Result | Context | Before | After | |---------|--------|-------| | AddProjectDialog (step 0) | ← Back | Cancel | | OnboardingApp (step 2) | ← Back | ← Back (unchanged) |

- **`src/webhooks-config.json`** — added `"media-api.l42.eu": "KEY_LUCOS_MEDIA_METADATA_API"` to `consumerTokens`. This is the immediate fix: `getAuthHeader()` will now return a `Bearer` token for deliveries to `media-api.l42.eu` rather than `null`, ending the 401 run that has persisted since 2026-05-20.

- **`src/webhooks.js`** — added `validateWebhooksConfig(config)` (exported). Iterates all subscriber URLs in the config, extracts hostnames, and throws if any hostname lacks a `consumerTokens` entry. - **`src/index.js`** — calls `validateWebhooksConfig(webhooksConfig)` immediately after loading the config file, before constructing the `Webhooks` instance. Any future subscriber-without-token mistake will now surface at boot (and therefore in CI) rather than in production delivery logs.

## Summary
- Add mobile auth session state backed by secure storage and SDK `HonuaAuthToken` contracts.
- Support bearer credential sessions, token refresh before API/sync use, re-auth-required state, and sign-out secret clearing with offline edit policy messaging.
- Make field sync resolve auth tokens through the auth service, block expired/invalid sessions without draining pending edits, and surface re-auth messages in sync/auth view models.
- Expand redaction coverage for bearer/access/refresh tokens and update auth fakes across tests.

Closes #218.

## Platform Impact
- MAUI-facing auth and sync view models now expose session status, expiry, and re-auth-required state.
- Secure secret persistence continues through MAUI `SecureStorage`; no platform-specific storage paths changed.
- Android/iOS/Windows behavior should remain shared through the field collection core service and MAUI view-model bindings.

## Sync Impact
- Full sync, pull, and push call `EnsureValidSessionAsync()` before remote work.
- Expired bearer tokens refresh before sync/API operations when refresh support exists.
- Invalid or expired sessions return a re-auth message and leave pending offline edits queued.
- Sign-out clears stored auth secrets while explicitly preserving local offline edits unless a separate data cleanup policy removes them.

author: nv-slang-bot[bot]
body:
## Summary

codex 0.124's `--json` output shape changed in two breaking ways that left buddy without ledger continuity:

1. **`thread.started` event** carries `thread_id` (not top-level `session_id` like before)
2. **`item.completed` events** wrap the agent message in `.item.text` (was top-level `{type:"agent_message",message:"…"}`)
3. **`codex exec resume`** no longer accepts `-s` (sandbox) or `-C` (cwd) — both are inherited from the persisted session. The old script passed `-s danger-full-access` on resume → `unexpected argument '-s' found` → empty stdout → script's empty-stdout fallback drops the thread-id → every fire becomes a fresh init.

Net effect before this patch: thread-id never saved; every buddy fire a fresh `codex exec` init; charter re-sent each batch; no ledger continuity across batches. Buddy still produced per-batch reviews but they were context-isolated.

## Fix

Two named helpers extracted for clarity + test pinning:

- **`extract_thread_id`** — `(.thread_id // .session_id // empty)` tolerates both new and old shapes
- **`extract_response`** — prefers `.item.text` from `item.completed/agent_message`, falls back to old top-level shape

Resume invocation switched from `-s danger-full-access -C /workspace/agent` to `-c sandbox_mode=danger-full-access --skip-git-repo-check`. The config-key form is accepted by both `codex exec` and `codex exec resume`, matches how codex MCP server is wired in `container-runner.ts`, and is forward-compatible if `-s` shorthand gets deprecated.

## Test plan

- [x] 8 new vitest tests in `src/buddy-call.test.ts` (extract live selectors from script, run them through jq):
  - thread_id from new `{type:"thread.started",thread_id:"…"}`
  - thread_id back-compat with old `{session_id:"…"}`
  - thread_id empty-input → empty output, no error
  - response from `item.completed/agent_message`
  - response: last-of-many (paired with script's `| tail -1`)
  - response back-compat with old `{type:"agent_message",message:"…"}`
  - response ignores non-agent items (turn.started, tool_use)
  - codex flags pin: `-c sandbox_mode` in `CODEX_FLAGS`, no `-s danger-full-access` near `codex exec`
- [x] All 16 buddy-call tests pass; prettier clean; `pnpm run build` passes

**Verified live on lego (perfhound)**:
```
T+0   calling-codex-init      (first fire)
T+5s  thread-saved            ← UUID 019e5561-620e-71e0-931f-ce5ba88c8123 saved
T+5s  ok-or-malformed
T+15s no-reviewable-tools
```

Future fires now call `codex exec resume <UUID>` instead of init, restoring cross-batch ledger continuity.

author: broomva
body:
**Frontend PR B of Phase 3 (RFC #248).** Stacks on the engine routes from PR A (#23, already merged into fork/main).

When `advanced.git_panel` is on AND the agent's working directory is a git repository, a new **Git** tab appears next to the agent's other tabs. v1 is read-only: status, log, file diff.

## How it gates

Two-layer gating — flag is per-install, repo-check is per-agent — so non-code agents (Bookkeeper, etc.) stay un-cluttered even with the flag on.

```
advanced.git_panel (FeatureGate-equivalent) + useIsGitRepo(agent.folderPath) === true
→ tab injected at workspace-shell.tsx render time
```

The `useIsGitRepo` hook matches on `HoustonEngineError.kind === GIT_NOT_A_REPO_KIND` to resolve `false` cleanly instead of throwing a generic toast.

## Panel layout

Two-pane:
- **Left** — tab strip (Status | Log). Status rows are clickable and drive the right pane.
- **Right** — diff viewer. Empty-state when no file is selected. Loading state when fetching.
- **Empty state for non-repo cwd** — renders the actual cwd + hint to point the agent at a repo or `git init` there.

## What's in this PR

| File group | Count |
|---|---:|
| New components (`app/src/components/git/*` + `tabs/git-tab.tsx`) | 5 |
| New hook (`use-git-queries.ts`) | 1 |
| New KB doc | 1 |
| New i18n namespace `git` (en/es/pt) | 3 |
| TS engine client extensions (`types.ts`, `client.ts`) | 2 |
| Wrapper (`tauri.ts`) | 1 |
| Tab resolver + shell injection | 2 |
| Flag registry + settings i18n × 3 + agents i18n × 3 + d.ts | 8 |
| Test extension | 1 |

**Total**: 25 files. `bun run typecheck` (all 14 workspaces) green, `bun --filter houston-app check-locales` (17 namespaces) green.

## Validation

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `bun run typecheck` (14 workspaces) | green |
| `bun --filter houston-app check-locales` (17 namespaces) | en/es/pt sync, no em-dashes |
| Pre-commit lint-staged (typecheck + locales + rustfmt) | green |

## cwd source — v1 limitation (documented)

The panel queries `agent.folderPath` directly. For worktree-mode agents whose `.houston/<agent>/` is a real git checkout the panel works. For agents whose work happens in a different cwd (e.g. an `installCommand` pointing at `~/code/myproject`) the empty state surfaces with the actual path. v2 may add a per-agent `gitCwd` config or auto-derive from the active activity worktree.

## Stack

| | |
|---|---|
| PR A | #23 (already merged, `9ed906a`) — engine routes |
| **PR B** | **this** — frontend |

## Provider parity

N/A — this is a UI feature on top of `git` shell-out; provider-agnostic.

## Summary

Small safety PR on top of PR #40. Temporarily hides `/vision` from public discovery (search engines + site nav) until the owner walks through the three production smoke / owner-review checklists. The URL itself stays reachable by direct entry so the owner can verify the page on the live deploy. Flipping back to publicly-published is a one-line owner edit.

## What changed

- **New `apps/web/lib/config/vision-publication.ts`** with `VISION_PUBLIC: boolean = false` + `isVisionPublic()` helper. One canonical place to flip when smoke PASSES.
- **`/vision` page**: while the flag is `false`, `generateMetadata()` returns `robots: { index: false, follow: false, googleBot: { index: false, follow: false } }`, and an "Internal preview" badge + banner renders above the hero. When the flag flips to `true`, both behaviours disappear automatically.
- **`SiteNav`**: filters its LINKS through a small `vision-gate` visibility marker. While `isVisionPublic()` is `false`, the `/vision` link is removed from the public nav. The href stays in source so the flip is a one-line owner change.
- **LT + EN i18n**: new `vision.internalPreviewBadge` + `vision.internalPreviewBanner` (both include the "smoke" keyword so the honesty signal cannot drift).
- **Owner review checklist** (`docs/evidence/supergrand-vision-os-leap-v1/owner-review-checklist.md`) appended with the explicit "after smoke PASSES, flip `VISION_PUBLIC`" instruction.
- **Guards** — +2 vitest assertions (84 / 84 total vs PR #40's 82). Updated the PR #40 nav guard to acknowledge the visibility gate (i18n key + SiteNav href entry remain in source for the future flip; visible nav is filtered at render time).

## What is intentionally NOT touched

- **`/vision` route is still reachable by direct URL** — owner runs the smoke against it.
- **`/vision` page DESIGN** — body is identical to PR #40, only the chrome around it changes when the flag flips.
- **role / feature / activity catalogues** — unchanged.
- **PR #18** — not merged, not modified, not rebased.
- **`supabase/migrations/`** unchanged (file-count guard still holds).
