author: vincentmakes
body:
Sprint 1 of the multi-sprint plan to harden the Turbo EA MCP server's
write surface. This commit ships the audit foundation every later
safeguard rides on: every MCP write opens a batch, the batch id flows
through to the audit log, and large commits gate on a confirm-token
issued by the prior dry-run.

Backend
- New `mutation_batches` table + `events.batch_id` column (migration
  094); model in `app/models/mutation_batch.py`.
- New service `mutation_batch_service.py` with open/commit helpers,
  a 15-min TTL `confirm_token`, and a constant-time token check.
- New API at `POST/GET /api/v1/mutation-batches`,
  `POST /mutation-batches/{id}/commit`, and
  `GET /mutation-batches/{id}/events` (the per-batch change history).
  Batch owners can read their own; cross-actor reads need
  `admin.events`.
- `event_bus.publish` now accepts an optional `batch_id` and reads
  a new `request_batch_id` contextvar populated by the origin
  middleware from the `X-Turbo-EA-Batch` header. Existing publish
  call sites are unchanged.
- CORS allow-list extended with `X-Turbo-EA-Batch`.

MCP server
- `TurboEAClient` accepts an optional `batch_id` and emits the header
  on every backend call so the audit-log stamping happens
  transparently.
- New `batches.py` async context manager (`mutation_batch`) is the
  standard wrapper for write tools — opens the batch, yields a
  pre-configured client, commits on clean exit, error-tags and
  commits on exception.
- `create_cards_bulk` refactored as the canonical example; other
  write tools follow in a later sprint.
- New `get_change_history` MCP tool surfaces the audit endpoint to
  agents (read-only).
- New `identity.py` decodes JWT `sub` claim for actor stamping;
  decode is unverified by design (backend re-verifies on every call).
- MCP `ToolAnnotations` (`readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`,
  `idempotentHint`) added to all 31 tools.
- New env vars: `MCP_BATCH_CONFIRMATION_THRESHOLD` (default 20),
  `MCP_REQUIRE_DRYRUN_FIRST` (default true).
- Wrapper enforces the confirm-token gate before any backend call so
  the agent gets a clear actionable error when a large commit lacks
  the dry-run token.

Tests
- 15 new MCP tests in `test_safeguards.py` covering the confirmation
  gate, the 3-POST batch lifecycle, `get_change_history` routing,
  the JWT actor decoder, and per-tool annotations.
- 6 new backend unit tests in `test_mutation_batch_service.py`
  (TTL + constant-time match logic, DB-less).
- 7 new backend integration tests in `test_mutation_batches.py`
  (open/commit/list/permissions/end-to-end header → event stamping).
- Existing `test_write_tools.py` tests for `create_cards_bulk`
  updated for the new 3-POST flow via a `_patched_post_batch_aware`
  helper that routes mocked POSTs by path.

Docs
- CHANGELOG entry under 1.29.0; VERSION bumped to 1.29.0.
- CLAUDE.md gains a "Mutation batches" bullet describing the wrapper
  + audit trail and updates the env-var list.
- OpenAPI spec regenerated.

author: dangpham112000
body:
Update `nginx/nginx.conf` to configure dynamic DNS resolution for upstream container proxying.

**Root Cause:**
In a Docker Compose deployment where only the backend and frontend are redeployed/recreated (e.g. from GitHub Actions), their internal IP addresses will change. The Nginx reverse proxy, which starts before them and isn't restarted since its configuration didn't change, statically caches the old IP addresses for `http://frontend` and `http://backend` leading to `502 Connection Refused` logs.

**Fix:**
Configured Docker's embedded DNS server (`resolver 127.0.0.11`) and forced variable interpolation on the `proxy_pass` destinations. This instructs Nginx to re-query the Docker DNS cache for the container's IP dynamically upon request, ensuring routing works automatically after automated deployments.

body:
## Summary
- Fixes the install paths so `serac` actually runs after install on Mac/Linux/Windows
- Triggered by [Reddit feedback](https://www.reddit.com/r/servicenow/s/agUCLjh3He) from `cavemanrv`: `zsh: command not found: serac` on Mac, `snow-code: Binary not found for windows-arm64` on Windows
- All three were rebrand fallout: bash installer + npm postinstall + npm launcher still pointing at `groeimetai/snow-flow`, and the bash installer never created a `serac` alias

## Changes
- `install`: download from `serac-labs/serac`, expect `snow-flow-<target>.tar.gz` (matches what `publish-npm.yml` actually ships), always `.tar.gz` + `tar` (no more broken `.zip` path on Mac), extract `bin/` and `mcp/` into the install prefix, create `serac` + `snow-flow` aliases next to `snow-code`
- `packages/opencode/scripts/postinstall.cjs`: REPO -> `serac-labs/serac`, serac-branded messages
- `packages/opencode/bin/snow-code`: error message points at the new repo
- All three paths: `windows-arm64` falls back to the `windows-x64` tarball (Windows 11 runs it under the built-in x64 emulator). Avoids needing a separate native ARM64 build (which `@parcel/watcher-win32-arm64` would also need wiring up).

## Test plan
- [ ] Merge -> `publish-npm.yml` builds v1.0.20, attaches `snow-flow-*.tar.gz` to the GitHub release, publishes `@serac-labs/core@1.0.20` to npm
- [ ] On Windows ARM64 PC: `npm install -g @serac-labs/core` should download `snow-flow-windows-x64.tar.gz`, drop `snow-code.exe` in `bin/`, and `serac` runs (via x64 emulation)
- [ ] On macOS arm64: `curl -fsSL https://serac.build/install | bash` should land `serac` in PATH
- [ ] On Linux: same as macOS

Closes the install-flow part of the Reddit feedback. The `cd serac` confusion from comment 3 is pure user error and not actionable in code — the new install message says `cd <project>` then `serac` which is at least less misleading than the previous wording.

Fixes #142 is unrelated; this isn't linked to an existing issue. Maintainer note: happy to file one if the "issue-first" policy is strict here, but the bug is verbatim from the Reddit thread so I went straight to a PR.

author: iwanabethatguy
body:
The on-disk `@oxc-project/runtime` package ships two variants of every helper: a CJS form at `src/helpers/<name>.js` that sets `module.exports = fn`, and an ESM form at `src/helpers/esm/<name>.js` that does `export default fn`. The plugin previously embedded only the ESM variant and reused it for every caller, which meant `require("@oxc-project/runtime/helpers/X")` returned the ESM namespace `{ default: fn }` rather than the function itself.

This PR embeds both variants and dispatches resolution by `ImportKind`: `require()` gets the CJS variant (callable directly), `import` / dynamic `import()` get the ESM variant. Relative imports between virtual helpers preserve the importer's directory so an ESM helper's `./typeof.js` stays in `esm/`. Fixes #9263, where `_defineProperty` resolved to the ESM namespace inside CJS-classified modules and threw `TypeError: _defineProperty is not a function` at init.

author: proofmancer
body:
Sender-side companion to docs#29 + landing#210 + ligate-cli#40 (Phase 3 senders/receivers).

Mirrors the pattern in ligate-chain + ligate-cli release.yml. After every `v*` tag publish (non-rc), dispatches a `sdk-released` event to `ligate-io/docs` and `ligate-io/ligate-marketing` so their `bump-versions.yml` workflows open a bump PR within ~30 s. Daily cron is the safety net.

## Setup needed before this is fully wired
Add `DOWNSTREAM_DISPATCH_PAT` to this repo's secrets at https://github.com/ligate-io/ligate-js/settings/secrets/actions, or set the same secret org-level.

If missing the dispatch step exits cleanly with a workflow-level warning; the release still publishes.

## Note on what this dispatch actually changes
Today docs/landing don't have any exact-version pins to `@ligate-labs/sdk` (the install command uses `^0.2.0` semver, which doesn't drift on minor/patch). So the immediate bump PR will be a no-op. The wiring matters because:
- A future major-bump (`^0.3.0`) needs the manual prose-side update — the workflow surfaces it.
- Any docs page that later pins to an exact SDK version automatically gets bumped.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] On next sdk release: receivers see the dispatch in their `bump-versions` workflow log (even if no PR opens because nothing drifted)

body:
Implements `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-23-household-subaccounts-design.md`. Built brainstorm → spec → plan → subagent-driven (per-task review) → independent final security review → fixes.

## What it does
One household login holds up to **N player profiles** (N = `plans.seats`: free 1 / solo 1 / family 4 / coach 20). After login, if there's more than one profile, a **"Who's training?"** picker chooses the active one for that session/device. Swings auto-attach to the active profile — no per-swing name picking, no mixed-up reports. **"Switch profile"** in the nav re-opens the picker. Solo/Free users (1 profile) auto-select and see zero change.

## Why this shape
The app already centralizes "the current player" in `st.session_state["player"]` (read everywhere via `auth.current_profile()`), so the picker just sets that one var and every existing page (upload, reports, training plan, dashboard) works unchanged.

## Changes
- **Schema** (`2026_05_23_household_profiles.sql`, applied to live DB): drop `players.user_id` UNIQUE (one login → many profiles), add `players.removed_at` (soft-remove), add `create_household_player()` SECURITY DEFINER RPC enforcing the seat cap from `v_my_plan` under a `FOR UPDATE` lock. Existing 2 player rows untouched.
- **auth.py**: `list_household_players`, `set_active_player` (IDOR-guarded), `needs_profile_pick` (solo auto-selects), `create_household_player`, `remove_household_player`, `current_household_seats`. `_fetch_player_row` now excludes removed + orders deterministically.
- **household_picker.py**: the editorial "Who's training?" chooser.
- **app.py**: picker gate after login (keys off explicit `_profile_picked`, not the auto-restored player) + switch-profile + clears the flag on logout/session-expiry.
- **player_settings_page.py**: Household section → create/remove profiles (name + bat hand + position, no email). Hidden for single-seat plans.
- **family_storage.py**: re-pointed at player profiles (public API unchanged). Email-invite/subscription_seats machinery parked.
- **bl_edge_chrome.py**: Switch Profile control (multi-profile only).

## Review findings fixed
Independent final review caught a **P0**: `_profile_picked` survived logout → logging into a different household in the same browser bypassed the picker. Fixed in both logout paths + sign_in. P1: `_fetch_player_row` ordering/removed filter.

## Test plan
- [x] 345 passing, 1 skipped (8 new household tests + full regression)
- [x] Migration applied to live DB + verified (constraint dropped, RPC + removed_at present, existing rows intact)
- [x] IDOR guard, seat-cap-under-lock, solo-no-picker, soft-remove all covered
- [ ] After merge: manual e2e — create 2 profiles, log out/in → picker → upload as Tommy → switch to Dad → separate history

author: dhanson-wp
body:
## What?

Adds a new in-editor Preview modal to the post and page editor.

Instead of requiring users to open a separate browser tab to preview content, this introduces a modal preview layer that opens on top of the current editor and preserves editing context.

The modal includes device preview controls for:

- Desktop
- Tablet
- Mobile

The existing external preview flow remains available from the View dropdown as “Preview in new tab”.

## Why?

Previewing content currently requires leaving the editing flow, usually through “Preview in new tab”. Device emulation, View Post, and previewing unsaved changes are also mixed together in ways that can be confusing.

Related issues/discussions:

- #65918
- #65005
- #41723
- #23126

This PR explores a concrete implementation for improving that experience by making preview feel like a layer within the editor rather than a full context switch.

It also creates a potential foundation for future preview extensions, such as:

- Website preview
- Email/newsletter preview
- Social preview
- Paid subscriber / public visitor preview
- RSS or print preview
- Plugin-provided preview modes

## How?

This PR introduces a modal-based preview surface that:

- Opens from the editor preview UI.
- Displays the current preview route inside the modal.
- Provides responsive device controls in the modal header.
- Supports Desktop, Tablet, and Mobile preview sizes.
- Allows users to close the modal and return to their previous editor context.
- Keeps the existing external “Preview in new tab” behavior available from the View dropdown.

## Screenshots

### Desktop preview

![Desktop preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dhanson-wp/gutenberg/pr-assets/post-page-editor-preview-modal/screenshots/post-page-editor-preview-modal/preview-modal-desktop.png)

### Tablet preview

![Tablet preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dhanson-wp/gutenberg/pr-assets/post-page-editor-preview-modal/screenshots/post-page-editor-preview-modal/preview-modal-tablet.png)

### Mobile preview

![Mobile preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dhanson-wp/gutenberg/pr-assets/post-page-editor-preview-modal/screenshots/post-page-editor-preview-modal/preview-modal-mobile.png)

## Testing Instructions

1. Open the post editor or page editor.
2. Create or edit a post/page with several blocks.
3. Click the Preview button in the editor header.
4. Confirm the preview opens in a modal without navigating away from the editor.
5. Switch between Desktop, Tablet, and Mobile preview sizes.
6. Confirm long preview content scrolls inside the modal surface.
7. Press Escape or use the close button to close the modal.
8. Confirm focus/context returns to the editor.
9. Confirm the existing “Preview in new tab” behavior still works from the View dropdown.

Repeat similar checks for:

- Page editor
- Post editor

## Accessibility

Things to verify:

- Keyboard focus moves into the modal when it opens.
- Focus is trapped inside the modal while open.
- Escape closes the modal.
- Focus returns to the triggering control after closing.
- Device controls are keyboard accessible.
- Modal title/label is announced correctly by screen readers.

## Notes / follow-up

This PR does not attempt to solve the entire preview extensibility problem described in #65005, but it may provide a core preview surface that future extensibility work could build on.

Potential follow-up questions:

- Should plugins be able to register additional preview modes?
- Should “Preview in new tab” also live inside the modal, or is the existing View dropdown location enough?
- Should this same modal be used consistently across posts, pages, templates, and the Site Editor?
- How should this work when previewing templates or full site routes?
- Should modal previews visually suppress editor/admin chrome such as the WordPress admin bar?

## Validation

- `npm run test:unit packages/editor/src/components/post-preview-modal-button/test/index.js`
- `npm run lint:js -- packages/editor/src/components/post-preview-modal-button packages/editor/src/components/header/index.js`
- `npm run lint:css -- packages/editor/src/components/header/style.scss packages/editor/src/components/post-preview-modal-button/style.scss`
- `npm run build`
- Manual browser smoke test in `wp-env` for opening, switching device sizes, internal scroll, closing with Escape, and preserving the existing external preview option.

### Motivation

- Provide a modular starter for a cyberpunk-themed multiplayer FPS with a browser client and Node.js server.
- Offer a small but complete example of server-authoritative gameplay with bots, projectile replication, and basic anti-cheat input sanitization. 
- Make it easy to iterate locally and deploy by including client, server, shared constants, and run scripts.

### Description

- Add a client app under `client/` with `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `src/main.js` implementing Three.js rendering, input/pointer lock, HUD, mobile controls, and Socket.IO integration. 
- Add a Node/Express Socket.IO server at `server/src/index.js` implementing player state, bot AI, projectile simulation, hit detection, respawns, and periodic snapshot emission. 
- Add shared game constants in `shared/constants.js` and a `package.json` with `dev`, `dev:server`, `dev:client`, and `start` scripts to run the app locally. 
- Add a top-level `README.md` describing features, project structure, setup, deployment notes, and extension/hardening suggestions.

### Testing

- No automated tests are included or run as part of this change.

body:
## 배경

dev/watch RSS 누수 epic (PR #3691~#3713) 의 측정 인프라를 회귀 가드로 자동화. `packages/core/src/napi/common.zig` 의 Debug GPA leak detector 가 1분 dev probe 후 stack trace 포함 leak 리포트 dump → workflow 가 `leak entries == 0` assertion.

문서:
- 저장소 내부: [`docs/DEBUG.md`](../blob/main/docs/DEBUG.md) 의 "NAPI 누수 측정" 섹션
- GitHub Pages: 사이드바 → "레퍼런스" → "NAPI 누수 측정 (Debug GPA)"

## 트리거 (PR 미차단)

- **`push: branches: [main]` + path filter** (NAPI / bundler / parser / transformer / codegen / `examples/web/`)
- **`schedule: cron "0 4 * * *"`** (KST 13:00) — 매일 1회 검증 (path 무관 cover)
- **`workflow_dispatch`** — 수동 트리거

매 PR 마다 안 돌림 — Debug NAPI 빌드 + 1분 probe = ~7-10분 추가라 PR 머지 지연 회피. main push 후 sanity + nightly + 회귀 의심 시 수동 실행.

## `/code-review max` 5-angle 결과 — CRITICAL bugs 다수 catch + 모두 fix

| Finding | Severity | Fix 적용 |
|---|---|---|
| F2/F3: `grep -c ... \|\| echo 0` 가 0-match 시 `"0\n0"` 캡처 → 모든 clean run false-red | **CRITICAL** | `set +e` block + `[ -z ] && X=0` 명시 fallback |
| F1: SIGTERM 이 POSIX atexit 발화 안 함 | HIGH | Bun graceful shutdown 의존 명시 (실측 PR #3713 검증) + 주석 |
| F4: `kill -KILL` 후 `wait` 가 무의미 (이미 reap) | HIGH | wait-with-timeout pattern (20s graceful → SIGKILL fallback) |
| F8: `sed -i.bak` 가 .bak 도 watcher trigger 가능 | HIGH | `sed -i` (ubuntu GNU sed, no backup) |
| F9: top alloc-sites grep `"in _"` 가 Zig stack trace 실 형식과 불일치 | MEDIUM | `^\\s+0x[0-9a-f]+ in ` regex |
| F11: path filter 가 parser/transformer/codegen 누락 | MEDIUM | 추가 |
| F5: 8s fixed sleep 이 cold runner 에서 부족 | MEDIUM | ready signal polling (`[serve]` / `bundled` 메시지) |
| F10: panic regex 오positive/저negative | MEDIUM | anchored regex (`^thread N panic:`, `^Aborted`, etc.) |
| F13: explicit shell defaults 없음 | LOW | `defaults.run.shell: bash` 명시 |
| F15: cp 의 `\|\| true` 누락 | LOW | ci.yml napi job 과 동일 패턴 |
| F6/F7: build:js 중복 (3회) | LOW | Pre-build step 제거 (predev hook + 별도 step 으로 충분) |
| F14: `-Dnapi-optimize=Debug` flag 존재 확인 | verify | build.zig:233 `napi_optimize` option 확인 ✓ |

## 정상 기준 (회귀 가드 통과 조건)

| 지표 | 기대값 |
|---|---|
| `leak entries` | `0` |
| `panics` | `0` |
| `rebuilt` | `>= 5` (20회 touch 중 watcher arm 지연 노이즈 허용) |

회귀 시: `::error::` 출력 + alloc-site 분포 + 전체 stderr (last 200 lines) + `actions/upload-artifact@v4` 가 stderr.log/stdout.log 7일 보관 → 회귀 분석 가능.

## 검증

- YAML syntax 검증 (Astro Starlight build 의 다른 작업과 동일 패턴)
- 코드 변경 0 → `zig build` / `zig build test` 무관
- 실 작동 검증은 main 머지 + `workflow_dispatch` 수동 실행 후 (CI runner 환경 의존성 — local 재현 불가)

## 영향

- **ZNTC core release 빌드 영향 0** — Debug NAPI 빌드 한정
- **PR 머지 비차단** — 매 PR 마다 안 돌림
- **회귀 영구 가드** — main push / nightly 로 자동 감지 → leak 87→0 의 epic 결과 유지

## Follow-up

- workflow 실 작동 검증은 머지 후 `workflow_dispatch` 수동 실행으로 확인
- 첫 실행이 fail 하면 (실 CI 환경 차이) artifact 분석 후 추가 PR

body:
I have implemented several micro-UX and accessibility improvements to the A.N.W. FOUNDATIONS landing page:

1.  **Visual Parity:** I synchronized the "resonance" animations (gradient overlays and icon translations) previously restricted to `group-hover` with `group-focus-within` and `group-focus-visible`. This ensures keyboard users experience the same visual delight as mouse users.
2.  **Semantic Structure:** I added `role="article"` and `aria-labelledby` to informational cards that used `tabindex="0"`. This provides better context for assistive technologies.
3.  **Focus Management:** I updated the smooth scroll script to programmatically move browser focus to the target section after scrolling. This prevents the "lost focus" issue common in single-page applications. Additionally, the "Back to Top" interaction now correctly restores focus to the skip-to-content link.

These changes were verified visually and functionally using Playwright screenshots and source inspection. All temporary test artifacts have been removed to preserve the static nature of the repository.

- Update the React `ArchetypeSelect` combobox to treat an absent `createUrl` as "no inline-create permission" — it hides the "+ Create" option and shows an empty-state hint ("No matching archetype. Ask an archetype editor to add it.") instead.

## Why

Before this change, any authenticated user could pollute the archetype catalog by typing a name not in the autocomplete and triggering the inline create. Typos, duplicates, casing variants, and joke entries leaked into a curated namespace maintained by `ROLE_ARCHETYPE_EDITOR` holders.

## Defense in depth

The server-side gate is the source of truth: even if the UI was bypassed (e.g. direct `curl`), a non-editor POST returns **403**. The Twig conditional is a UX nicety on top.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit: existing 205 archetype-related tests still pass (admin@example.com has `ROLE_ADMIN` → inherits `ROLE_ARCHETYPE_EDITOR`).
- [x] Functional: `testCreateRejectedForNonEditorUser` — borrower POSTing to `/api/archetype` gets 403.
- [x] Functional: `testNewDeckFormEmitsCreateUrlForArchetypeEditor` — admin sees the attribute.
- [x] Functional: `testNewDeckFormOmitsCreateUrlForNonEditor` — borrower does not see the attribute.
- [x] All linters: cs-fix, twig-cs-fix, eslint-fix, stylelint-fix, phpstan L10, lint-i18n, lint-yaml, lint-container, lint:twig.
- [x] Full PHPUnit + Vitest suites green (2378 + 26).
- [ ] **Manual browser**: as admin, register a deck with an archetype name that doesn't exist → confirm the "+ Create" option appears in the combobox.
- [ ] **Manual browser**: as a non-editor user, register a deck and type an unknown archetype name → confirm the empty-state hint appears and there is no "+ Create" option.
- [ ] **Manual browser (defense)**: as non-editor, try `curl -X POST /api/archetype -d '{"name":"...."}'` → 403.

## Out of scope

- A "request a new archetype" lightweight queue for non-editors (mentioned in the issue as a follow-up; could be a future feature).
- i18n of the new combobox empty-state string — `ArchetypeSelect.tsx` has many hardcoded strings already; introducing i18n there is a separate refactor.
- Updating the soft-delete name/slug collision behavior (#579 / F2.27) — that's the natural follow-up since archetype editors are now the only people resolving collisions.

Closes #584.

author: tonykuttai
body:
New PR: https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/199398

**Note**: This PR adds LTO support for the pragma comment copyright feature implemented in #178184. Should be reviewed/merged after #178184.

`LowerCommentStringPass` implements `#pragma comment(copyright, ...)` on AIX by creating a TU-local  `@__loadtime_comment_str` global in the `__loadtime_comment` section and attaching `!implicit.ref` metadata to all
defined functions. The PowerPC backend reads `!implicit.ref` and emits `.ref` directives from each function csect to the copyright string csect, so the AIX XCOFF linker keeps the copyright string alive whenever any function from the TU is live.

This change teaches `ModuleSummaryAnalysis` to include globals referenced via `!implicit.ref` metadata as explicit reference edges in the ThinLTO module summary via a new helper `findImplicitRefEdges`.

body:
## What

Add a typed `OpenWorkExtensionManifest` model and convert built-in extensions (Browser, OpenAI Image Gen, Ollama) from hard-coded catalog entries to manifest-backed entries. This is the foundation PR for the extension abstraction stack.

## Why

Extensions should be a superset that can be a skill, an OpenCode plugin, an MCP, a provider, or a full UI/runtime integration like Voice Mode or HandsFree Computer Use. Today they are hard-coded entries in `MCP_QUICK_CONNECT` with special-cased install/setup logic. This PR introduces the manifest contract so future PRs can add Handsfree, Voice Mode, and Den-imported Claude plugins as extensions without more special-casing.

## Shape

`Extension = manifest + resources + contributions + setup + lifecycle + source`

- **Source**: where it came from (builtin, Den Claude plugin, OpenWork manifest, MCP directory, manual)
- **Resources**: installable primitives (skill, MCP, OpenCode plugin, provider, secret, native binary, etc.)
- **Setup**: custom instructions, required env vars, primary CTA text, test action refs
- **Contributions**: allowlisted UI/runtime refs (settings panel, composer prompt, session side panel, rail item, server route, control actions, native capabilities, tests)
- **Lifecycle**: reload/detection hints for OpenCode config

## Changes

- New `apps/app/src/app/extensions.ts` with manifest types and built-in manifests for Browser, Image Gen, Ollama
- `constants.ts` generates the catalog from manifests via `extensionManifestToDirectoryInfo`
- Extension detail modal shows declarative setup instructions, resource labels, and contribution labels from the manifest
- Settings config registry resolves contribution refs alongside legacy IDs
- Den marketplace UI copy shifted from "packages" to "extensions"
- Den client types gain `DenOrgExtensionProjection` for future API support
- `isBuiltInOpenWorkExtension` uses manifest `source.origin + trusted` flag
- `docs/extensions-manifest-foundation.md` documents the PR stack and CDP flows

## PR Stack

1. **This PR**: typed manifest model, manifest-backed built-in catalog, generic manifest display, Den copy
2. **Handsfree PR** (next): trusted built-in extension manifest with native-binary, local MCP, macOS permissions
3. **Voice Mode PR** (next): trusted built-in extension manifest with settings, side panel, rail item, server route, Realtime secret, control actions

author: scalcerano
body:
## Summary

First real-inference building block for Component #11. Hand-rolled SentencePiece Unigram subword tokenizer in C99 (~280 LoC impl + ~340 LoC tests). Model-agnostic: any Unigram-trained vocab works.

**Why hand-rolled**: upstream SentencePiece is ~60 MB / 151K LoC C++ with protobuf + abseil + darts-clone dependency cascade. The algorithm itself is ~150 LoC of Viterbi. Focused-subset discipline matches the rest of the project (ed25519 ref10, ggml CPU subset, picotls minicrypto).

## Public API (`include/ants_tokenizer.h`)

- `ants_tokenizer_t` opaque ctx (1 KiB; state is ~32 B with headroom for trie / byte-fallback)
- `ants_tokenizer_vocab_entry_t { text, text_len, score, token_id }` — caller-owned vocab array
- `_init`, `_destroy`, `_encode`, `_decode`

## Algorithm

1. Pre-tokenization: prepend ▁ (U+2581), replace whitespace runs with a single ▁
2. Viterbi forward over caller's vocab (O(N × V) linear scan; trie comes later)
3. Backtrace to recover token IDs in left-to-right order

Bit-exact deterministic across platforms.

## Out of scope (follow-up PRs)

- Unicode NFKC normalisation (caller responsibility for now)
- Byte fallback for unknown chars
- JSON loader for `tokenizer.json` files (step 2: HuggingFace config parsing)
- Trie-based lookup
- Special tokens (CLS / SEP / PAD / MASK / UNK)

## Tests (13 functions)

Opaque ctx layout, init NULL/zero-shape args, destroy safety, encode arg validation + Viterbi correctness (hand-crafted vocab where `[▁hello, ▁world]` beats letter-by-letter -1.0 vs -10.0), letter fallback, whitespace collapse, NON_CANONICAL on uncovered input, BUFFER_TOO_SMALL with required-cap hint, encode determinism, decode round-trip, decode invalid-ID rejection, decode arg validation + BUFFER_TOO_SMALL.

## Test plan
- [x] Debug build (AppleClang + ASan + UBSan): 7/7 suites green
- [x] Release build: green

- [ ] CI 7-job matrix

author: daoyzheng
body:
When the user swipes / taps the chevrons / presses arrow keys to navigate between memories in the open modal, MemoryShell reuses the same MemoryDetail instance instead of remounting it. The old inline comment claimed ":key on this component resets it per-memory" — but that :key was dropped during the modal rebuild (sub-plan #3), so per-memory state was stuck on whichever memory was open at first mount:

- localReactions stayed pinned to the first memory's reaction set
- comments were only fetched once at mount; navigating showed the first memory's comments under every subsequent memory
- the viewer-mode heart-tap gate already had its own watcher

Adds a single watch(() => props.memory.id) that re-seeds reactions from the new prop, reloads comments for the new memory, clears inline-edit state (active edit, draft, delete-confirm), and folds in the existing viewerReacted reset. Exiting any in-progress caption edit triggers the existing watch(editing) cleanup which handles slidesEdit / stagedItems / editNote / etc. Navigation itself already passes the canClose discard prompt, so by the time this watcher fires the user has already confirmed (or had no edits).

author: tais
body:
Travelling into a sector with enemies crashed at the pre-battle "initiate battle" screen: InitPreBattleInterface() dereferenced a garbage pointer (EXC_BAD_ACCESS, e.g. pBattleGroup=0x6cd62760 -- a 64-bit GROUP* truncated to its low 32 bits).

The pre-battle GROUP* is carried to the dialogue handler through a UINT32 field (DIALOGUE_Q_STRUCT::uiSpecialEventData / FACETYPE::uiUserData1), so the pointer was truncated at the store and cast back to garbage at the read. Pass the group's ubGroupID (a UINT8 -- fits losslessly) through the chain instead and rebuild the pointer via GetGroup() at the read sites. This is exactly the fix the original 1.13 author sketched and left commented out ("we cast a UINT32 as GROUP*? ... likely garbage. Why the hell not use the id instead?").

Sites: stores in Strategic Movement.cpp (HandleImportantPBIQuote x2, TriggerPrebattleInterface); reads in Dialogue Control.cpp (the FACE_TRIGGER_PREBATTLE_INT path that crashed, + the TRIGGERPREBATTLEINTERFACE path). Built clean on all variants; verified entering the A10-east garrison and Drassen-from-north no longer crash.

## 概要

`radar workflow generate combined-with-triage` に **直コミット出力モード** `--output-mode pr|direct-commit`（既定 `pr`）を追加（closes #258）。

PR レビューを介さず default ブランチに直接書きたい監視ユースケースで、生成 YAML を手改変する必要がなくなる。

## 変更内容

- **`--output-mode pr|direct-commit`**（既定 `pr`）。`pr`|`direct-commit` 以外はパース時 exit 2 で reject。
- `direct-commit` 時:
  - `permissions: contents: write` のみ（`pull-requests: write` を出力しない）。
  - 最終ステップを commit & push に置換（**変更があるときだけ commit** ＋ 3 回 `git pull --rebase --autostash` リトライ）。`watch` / `combined` のステップと同形。
  - 「default ブランチに PR 必須のブランチ保護を掛けない」旨を生成 YAML にコメントで明示。
- template を 2 placeholder（`{{permissionsBlock}}` / `{{finalStep}}`）化し、生成器側でモードに応じて差し替え（既存の template 読み込み方式に合わせた最小変更）。`pr` 既定の出力は従来とバイト等価。
- help 文言・stdout（`output-mode:` 行）・docs（user-guide §triage workflow に `--output-mode` 表と注意書き）を同期。

## テスト

- `buildPermissionsBlock` / `buildFinalStep` のユニットテスト、`--output-mode` のパース（既定・direct-commit・不正値・値欠落）、end-to-end（direct-commit で `pull-requests: write` が出ない／commit&push ステップが出る、pr 既定で従来通り）を追加。
- 生成 YAML は両モードとも **actionlint クリーン**（ローカル検証済み）。
- 全 1238 テスト pass / tsc / biome / markdownlint クリーン。

## 関連

- ADR-0014（workflow generate）/ ADR-0018（triage workflow）

author: deestax
body:
## The production incident (2026-05-22)

Today's hosted Hetzner deploy at 07:42Z respawned per-user agent containers. Cron jobs fired at 07:57Z and wrote their output files to disk. The cron_watcher (lazy-started via the \`pre_gateway_dispatch\` hook) didn't actually start until 07:59:23Z — when the user sent their first chat message in the new container.

On the first tick:
- \`cutoff = time.time() - _BOOTSTRAP_AGE_SECS\` = 07:58:23
- The three 07:57 output files were >60 seconds old
- They were silently seeded into the in-memory \`_seen_mtimes\` as "historical" and **never delivered to the platform webhook**

The user saw nothing in their chats. The agent's diagnosis pointed at \"No active stream\" (a separate upstream code path) and proposed re-targeting jobs — neither of which was the real cause.

## Root cause

The watcher's \`_seen_mtimes\` was in-memory-only. Every container restart wiped it. The 60-second bootstrap-age cutoff was a heuristic to prevent fresh installs from replaying months of historical output — but it conflated \"we don't know what was delivered\" with \"we have no memory at all\". Any cron output written in the window between cron fire and watcher start was lost whenever that window exceeded 60 seconds.

The watcher's lazy start adds inherent delay (depends on when the user next sends a message). Hetzner deploys happen often enough that this race fires regularly. The same incident class was almost certainly happening on every prior deploy too, but the user didn't notice because the lost outputs were going to chats they weren't actively monitoring.

## The fix

Replace the in-memory + age-cutoff design with a **persistent JSON state file** at \`OUTPUT_DIR.parent / \".watcher-seen.json\"\` written atomically via \`tempfile\` + \`os.replace\`. State survives container restarts because \`/data/.hermes/\` is volume-mounted.

Control flow on every \`_tick\`:

\`\`\`
ensure_state_loaded (idempotent, runs once per process):
  load state from disk:
    file exists, valid JSON  → trust as source of truth
                               (even {} means \"post-first-run, anything new IS new\")
    file missing OR corrupted → first-run path:
                                  seed every currently-present file into _seen_mtimes
                                  WITHOUT delivery, persist immediately

main tick:
  for each output file:
    if (path, mtime) in _seen_mtimes → skip
    else:
      delivered = await _deliver(...)   # returns bool
      if delivered:
        _seen_mtimes[path] = mtime      # mark-after-success only
  if any deliveries happened:
    save state atomically (tmp file → os.replace)
\`\`\`

The mark-after-success ordering is critical. If we marked the file before the webhook call (as the prior in-memory code did), a transient platform 502 during a deploy → file disk-recorded as delivered → restart loads state → file skipped forever. The mark-after-success pattern means failed deliveries stay unrecorded and naturally retry on the next tick.

## Design alternatives considered

| Option | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Raise \`_BOOTSTRAP_AGE_SECS\` to 24h+ | Rejected | Doesn't fix the bug, narrows the window. Long cutoff would re-deliver every file under N hours on each restart → duplicate spam |
| Remove the cutoff entirely | Rejected | Every restart replays ALL historical files → catastrophic duplicate flood |
| Move watcher-start from \`pre_gateway_dispatch\` to eager plugin \`register()\` | Rejected | Still has a finite window. Also the lazy start was specifically added to avoid \`asyncio.get_event_loop()\` deprecation on Python 3.12+ |
| Track delivered state inside upstream's \`jobs.json\` | Rejected | Plugin scribbling into upstream's data structure violates the \"prefer upstream primitives, no monkey-patching\" rule. Plus upstream rewrites \`jobs.json\` on every job event → race |
| Add a \`delivered_at\` field via upstream PR | Deferred | Architecturally cleanest long-term; requires upstream merge cycle (weeks-months); doesn't solve today's data loss |
| **Persistent plugin-side state file (this PR)** | **Chosen** | Actually solves the bug. Plugin-side only. Single source of truth. Atomic write. Fresh-install protection preserved via missing-state branch. Testable in isolation. |

## Pre-PR code-review subagent (round 2)

After the initial commit (\`af93554\`), a code-review subagent dispatched against the diff found two HIGH-severity issues plus a few smaller items. All material findings addressed in the second commit (\`1a41e65\`):

**HIGH-1**: \`_load_seen_state\` built the result dict via a single comprehension that called \`float(mtime)\`. Any non-coercible value (string, null, list) raised \`ValueError\`/\`TypeError\` that propagated through \`_tick\` and was caught only by the outer-loop exception handler. Next tick crashed the same way → watcher stuck forever with no log indication that the state file was at fault. Fixed: coerce per-entry inside try/except, drop bad entries with a warning naming the offending key, return \`None\` if all entries malformed (matches existing corrupted-JSON contract).

**HIGH-2**: \`_tick\` marked files as delivered in \`_seen_mtimes\` BEFORE awaiting \`_deliver\` (which swallowed all exceptions and HTTP failures internally). A transient platform 502 during a deploy → file disk-recorded as delivered → permanent loss. This was a latent bug in the pre-fix code too, but in-memory wipe on restart accidentally provided retry behavior. Persistence escalated it into durable loss. Fixed: \`_deliver\` now returns \`bool\`; \`_tick\` only updates state on \`True\`. Failed deliveries naturally retry on next tick.

Plus a MEDIUM (tempfile leak on \`os.replace\` failure, fixed via \`finally\` cleanup) and a LOW (explicit \`.clear()\` before \`.update()\` in state load).

The deferred review findings (state-file pruning for deleted output files, multi-writer comment in docstring, PEP 562 simplification) are documented for follow-up but don't affect correctness.

## Coverage

**18 new tests** in \`tests/test_cron_watcher_persistent_state.py\`:

- \`TestStateFileContract\` — path lives next to \`jobs.json\`, versioned JSON format
- \`TestFirstRunSeedsWithoutDelivery\` — fresh install with months-old files seeds them as delivered, no replay
- \`TestPersistedStateRespected\` — files in state skip; files NOT in state deliver regardless of age (**the exact pin for the 2026-05-22 incident**); mtime change re-delivers
- \`TestAtomicWrite\` — uses tempfile + \`os.replace\`
- \`TestHelperFunctions\` — \`_load_seen_state\` return contract (\`None\` vs \`{}\` vs populated)
- \`TestMalformedStateValuesRecover\` (4 tests) — non-float string, null, list value, end-to-end tick-doesn't-crash
- \`TestFailedDeliveryNotPersistedAsDelivered\` (3 tests) — HTTP 502, ConnectionError, happy-path sanity check

Existing \`test_cron_watcher.py\` fixture updated to pre-create an empty state file (simulates post-first-run delivery semantics).

**Results:**
- Cron-watcher curated suite: 33/33 GREEN
- Full plugin suite: 503/506 GREEN (3 pre-existing failures on master, confirmed unrelated via \`git stash\` + re-run)

## Backward compatibility

An existing deployment upgrading to this code: on first plugin load, no state file exists → first-run path → seeds every currently-present output file as \"already delivered\" → persists. **Same behavior as the prior \`_BOOTSTRAP_AGE_SECS\` cutoff for the fresh-install case** (no historical replay). From then on, strictly better — every restart loads the state and resumes where the prior process left off. No migration step needed.

## Follow-up after merge

Once merged: hosted PR will bump \`agent/Dockerfile.stock:MYAH_PLUGIN_SHA\` to this PR's squash SHA, then \`deploy.yml\` auto-runs and per-user containers respawn with the new plugin. The first respawn writes a fresh \`.watcher-seen.json\` (seed-without-delivery on first tick because the file didn't exist before). Every subsequ

## Phase A — Critical detection & DB bugs

This is the first of 4 phased PRs from a fresh full-repo audit (filtered for: single-user Windows local; no auth/security/multi-cam/production deploy items per the spec).

### Bugs fixed

| # | Where | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | `backend/database.py` | `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` doesn't add `snapshot_url` to pre-snapshot DBs → first INSERT crashed with `no such column` | `ALTER TABLE` on startup if `snapshot_url` (and defensively `source`) missing |
| A2 | `backend/anomaly.py` | Loitering, running, restricted_zone, and fight pair-eval kept accumulating timers on predicted (held-over, no real detection) tracks for up to `MAX_AGE = 30` frames after the person left | `is_predicted` guard before behavioural timers; predicted tracks contribute `avg_speed = 0` to fight pairing |
| A3 | `backend/anomaly.py` | Fight detection had no grace time — a 1-frame speed dip wiped accumulated persistence (running already had `RUNNING_RESET_GRACE_TIME` for exactly this) | New `FIGHT_RESET_GRACE_TIME` (default 0.4 s) + `fight_last_qualifying_at` bookkeeping with proper teardown |
| A4 | `useStickyAnomalies.ts`, `AlertsFeed.tsx` | Sticky `restricted_zone` key was just `track_id`; one person inside two overlapping zones collapsed onto one card | Key now includes `zone_id` for restricted_zone |
| A5 | `Settings.tsx` | 2-second `/api/config` poll overwrote `restricted_zone_enabled` and `restricted_zone_min_dwell` mid-drag, snapping the slider back | 8-second lockout window after any user edit on those controls |

### What was tested

- `tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `vite build`: clean
- `python -m ast` on all modified backend files: parse-clean

### Out of scope for this PR

Tracker tuning in `/api/config`, DB retention, archive cleanup on `/api/alerts/clear`, monotonic alert IDs, frontend loading-progress UI, AI report persistence, schema-versioned camera profiles, real Gemini SSE streaming, doc cleanup — all coming in Phases B, C, D.

### Scope explicitly excluded by user

Auth, rate limiting, CSRF, CORS, SSRF, multi-camera, Re-ID, pose estimation, PPE/face/license, ROI cropping, Prometheus metrics, structured logging, Docker, CI/CD, i18n. Also untouched per "skip simulation": `backend/simulation.py`, the simulation-canvas idle-mode rendering path.

author: juanarce122
body:
## Summary

Completa HU-01 según [docs/stories/HU-01.md](./docs/stories/HU-01.md): añade guía visual de encuadre durante la captura, resalta visualmente los ítems de baja confianza en la confirmación, y aplica un timeout duro de 8s al endpoint de análisis IA con mensaje claro al usuario.

**Decisión D3:** las cuotas free/premium quedan diferidas a sprint de Billing (post Sprint 12). Este PR cubre solo lo visual + timeout.

## Cambios técnicos

### Componentes nuevos
- \`CameraGuide\` — overlay con 4 esquinas + texto "Encuadra el plato completo" sobre el preview. \`pointer-events-none\` y \`aria-hidden\` para no interferir con el click del usuario ni con screen readers.
- \`ConfidenceBadge\` (shared) — consolidado desde la copia inline que vivía en \`StepConfirm.tsx\`. Dos modos:
  - \`showAll=true\` (default): pills Alta/Media/Baja en cada nivel
  - \`showAll=false\`: solo "Verificar" en bajas (útil para usos compactos)

### Cambios en componentes existentes
- \`StepCamera\` renderiza \`<CameraGuide />\` superpuesto al preview cuando hay foto
- \`StepConfirm\` importa el ConfidenceBadge shared y elimina la copia inline; ítems con \`confianza < 0.6\` ahora tienen \`border-accent-warm/40\` y fondo \`accent-warm/5\` para destacarlos visualmente

### /api/analyze
- Timeout duro de **8s** vía \`Promise.race\` (el SDK \`@google/generative-ai\` v0.24 no acepta \`AbortSignal\` consistentemente)
- Configurable por env \`ANALYZE_TIMEOUT_MS\` (usado en tests con 120ms)
- 504 con \`code: "timeout"\` + mensaje: "El análisis tardó demasiado. Intenta con una foto más simple o usa la búsqueda manual."
- \`runtime: "nodejs"\` + \`maxDuration: 30\` (envoltorio del timeout interno)

### Tests (18 nuevos, 133 totales)
- 3 \`__tests__/components/CameraGuide.test.tsx\`
- 10 \`__tests__/components/ConfidenceBadge.test.tsx\` (alta/media/baja + modo compacto + aria-labels)
- 5 \`__tests__/api/analyze.test.ts\` (timeout 504, 400 sin imageBase64, JSON wrapping cleanup, JSON inválido → 500, response exitosa)

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm test\` — 133 tests verdes
- [x] \`npm run lint\` — sin errores
- [x] \`npx tsc --noEmit\` — sin errores
- [ ] CI corre verde
- [ ] Manual: tomar foto en \`/day/[date]\` → ver overlay con marco y texto durante el preview
- [ ] Manual: confirmar items donde alguno tenga confianza < 0.6 → verificar fondo accent-warm/5 + borde
- [ ] Manual: simular Gemini lento (poner ANALYZE_TIMEOUT_MS=1 en .env) → verificar mensaje claro de timeout

## Criterios de aceptación verificados

- [x] "cámara se abre con guía visual de encuadre" → \`CameraGuide\` sobre el preview
- [x] "muestra alimentos con porción en gramos y nivel de confianza (alto/medio/bajo)" → \`ConfidenceBadge\` con 3 niveles
- [x] "ítem con confianza baja se resalta visualmente" → border + fondo accent-warm en \`StepConfirm\`
- [x] "IA procesa en menos de 5 segundos" → no enforcement client-side posible; tenemos timeout server-side a 8s con mensaje claro. KPI a monitorear con datos de prod (Gemini Flash típicamente responde en 2-4s).
- [ ] "confirmo, se entrena el modelo con correcciones" → fuera de scope (feedback loop ML queda para sprint futuro)
- [ ] **Cuotas free/premium** → DIFERIDO al sprint de Billing (decisión D3)

## Riesgos conocidos

| Riesgo | Mitigación |
|---|---|
| Costo Gemini sin cuotas escala con uso | Diferido a sprint Billing; mientras tanto monitor de costos en Vercel |
| Timeout 8s puede ser corto para fotos complejas | Configurable por ANALYZE_TIMEOUT_MS; UX clara permite reintentar o usar búsqueda |
| Umbral 0.6 puede no calibrar bien con datos reales | Ajustar post-merge sin breaking change |

author: reicrafted
body:
…anity gate

LIOP and the custom-NumPy MLDB path now consume RunConfig.descriptor_params just like every OpenCV-backed descriptor.  The two modules' previously hard-coded module-level constants become keyword arguments with the same default values, so behaviour at descriptor_params={} is unchanged.

  liop_describe accepted kwargs:
    - n_neighbors          (int >= 2, default 4)
    - n_bins               (int >= 1, default 6)
    - patch_size           (odd int >= 3, default 41)
    - patch_radius_sigmas  (float, default 3.0)
  Descriptor dim is now n_bins * factorial(n_neighbors) (= 144 at defaults).

  mldb_describe accepted kwargs (custom path):
    - patch_size    (default 60; must be divisible by every grid dim)
    - sigma_scale   (default 10.0)
    - smooth_sigma  (default 1.5)
    - grids         (sequence of (rows, cols), default ((2,2),(3,3),(4,4)))
  Descriptor byte count is derived from grids.  Native AKAZE path still
  forwards descriptor_params to cv2.AKAZE_create() unchanged.

Both custom paths cache their per-config precomputation via functools.lru_cache (16 entries), so a sweep over a small set of LIOP/MLDB configurations doesn't repay setup costs per call.  Invalid configurations (even patch_size, indivisible grid, etc.) raise ValueError before any per-keypoint work.

Removed the affine sanity gate from orchestrator.py entirely.  With ground truth always present in the experimental setup, an implausible RANSAC output is already caught by the corner-error metric and labelled false_match.  The sanity gate previously diverted that population into no_match (abstention) on a hand-tuned 10% scale / 3 deg rotation threshold, which distorted the Precision metric.  Letting every successfully-estimated affine reach Stage 7 means the configured accuracy tiers alone decide right vs wrong, and Precision now reflects "the pipeline emitted N transforms, of which K were correct" without an internal hand-tuned filter eating part of the population.

What got removed:
  - _MAX_SCALE_DIFF = 0.10
  - _MAX_ROTATION_DEG = 3.0
  - _affine_is_sane() helper
  - import math (no other users in orchestrator.py)
  - The corresponding branch in _execute_pipeline
  - All stale references in README, project_overview, types.py, metrics.py, config.py docstrings

Tests: 60 -> 68. Eight new descriptor tests:
  - Verify descriptor_params actually flows through to LIOP (n_neighbors, n_bins change descriptor dimension as expected)
  - Verify LIOP invalid patch_size raises ValueError
  - Verify descriptor_params actually flows through to custom MLDB (grids changes byte count, smooth_sigma changes bits, invalid patch_size raises ValueError)
  - Regression: BRIEF byte-count and SIFT contrastThreshold still forwarded via descriptor_params to OpenCV factories

Documentation:
  - project_overview Stage 3: clarified that descriptor_params is forwarded to every descriptor (OpenCV factories + LIOP + custom MLDB + native AKAZE MLDB); listed accepted-keys per path
  - project_overview Custom Descriptor Implementations: replaced the "fixed at compile time" wording for both descriptors with full configurable-hyperparameters tables (key, default, type, effect)
  - project_overview Hard-coded constants: relabelled LIOP/MLDB rows as "defaults" with cross-refs to the Custom Descriptor sections; removed the two affine-sanity constants entirely
  - project_overview Configuration System: new subsection documenting what detector_params / descriptor_params accept, with a worked example
  - project_overview Stage 5: replaced two-gate description with single min-inliers gate; added a "No geometric sanity gate" paragraph explaining the design choice so a future reader doesn't reintroduce one
  - README: pipeline diagram updated; prose updated

author: vthestone
body: Two changes to keep the Streamlit app within its 200 MB websocket payload limit even with all 10 Master Plan overlays available: 1. Downsample at PNG generation time master_plan_visualize.py now caps the longest side at 2000 px (LANCZOS resampling). Each PNG shrinks ~10x without losing visible detail at typical web zoom levels. Total Master Plan payload goes from ~300 MB to ~60 MB on disk. 2. Serve overlays as HTTP resources New src/app/static_server.py (FastAPI/uvicorn) runs on localhost:8502 alongside Streamlit and serves any file under the project root. map_view.ImageOverlay now uses HTTP URLs instead of file paths, so Folium emits tags instead of embedding base64 in the HTML. 3. Lazy-skip unchecked layers streamlit_app.py only assembles RasterLayerSpec / VectorLayerSpec for layers the user has enabled. This keeps the Folium payload tiny regardless of how many layers the manifest declares. The static server is launched as a daemon subprocess by streamlit_app itself; users still run a single command (streamlit run ...). Dependencies added: fastapi, uvicorn.

author: wavefrontset
body:
## Summary

Migrates `apps/paperless/` to a `bjw-s/app-template` HelmRelease (chart `5.0.1`) and folds the standalone Redis into it as a **second controller** rather than a separate set of raw manifests. First of the two "fold Redis into app-template" migrations (blocky follows separately).

Redis stays **isolated to paperless** — its own controller + service in the paperless namespace. Per the earlier analysis, paperless's Redis is the Celery broker (wants `noeviction`), so it shouldn't share an instance with a DNS cache.

## What changed

- **Two controllers**: `webserver` (paperless-ngx) + `redis` in one HelmRelease.
- `releaseName: paperless` pinned up front, applying the lesson from #233 (avoids the `<ns>-<name>` doubling).
- Values in a ConfigMap-backed `values.yaml` so Renovate's `helm-values` manager bumps both the paperless and redis images.
- **Volumes scoped via `advancedMounts`** to the `webserver` controller only — Redis gets no volumes. NFS `consume`/`media`, plus `data`/`export` subPaths on the reused `paperless-data` PVC (kept as a raw manifest so Flux prune can't reap it).
- HTTP readiness/startup/liveness probes preserved exactly.
- `paperless.env` still consumed via the `settings` configMapGenerator (`envFrom`).
- **`PAPERLESS_REDIS` → `redis://paperless-redis:6379`**: app-template prefixes service names with the release name, so the broker is reached at `paperless-redis` (the only app-config string that had to change; the ingress→webserver wiring is internal to the chart).

## Validation

Rendered with `helm template paperless … -n paperless` (using the pinned release name) and confirmed:
- `webserver` deployment: paperless-ngx image, all 3 HTTP probes, `consume`/`media` NFS + `data`/`export` PVC subPaths, both `envFrom` refs
- `redis` deployment: `redis:8`, **no volumes**
- services `paperless-webserver` (8000) + `paperless-redis` (6379)
- `kustomize build apps/` succeeds

## Test plan

- [ ] Flux reconciles the HelmRelease (`flux get hr -n flux-system paperless`)
- [ ] Old raw `webserver`/`redis` Deployments + Services + Ingress pruned, new chart-managed ones created
- [ ] webserver reattaches the `paperless-data` PVC and both NFS mounts (existing documents/media visible)
- [ ] paperless connects to the broker at `paperless-redis` — document consumption/OCR tasks run (check the consume folder picks up a test doc)
- [ ] paperless.homelab loads; DB connection to CNPG intact
- [ ] Renovate proposes bumps for both `paperless-ngx` and `redis`

author: luotee
body:
## Summary

Activates the reserved **"Export as PPTX"** dropdown item (previously a *Coming soon* placeholder) with a real, **editable** PowerPoint export — native text and shapes, not a rasterised image. It sits alongside the existing *Export as image PPTX*.

Per our discussion, the rendering logic is **built directly into `@open-slide/core`** rather than shipped as a third-party package. This addresses both concerns raised on the original revision of this PR:

- **Security** — no third-party export package to trust; the code lives in this repo and is reviewable here.
- **Maintainability** — the renderer evolves in lockstep with the slide primitives (the deck-bundling stub is updated in the same repo, so primitives like `Step`/`Steps` stay supported).

The renderer measures the laid-out DOM with **Playwright (Chromium)** to stay pixel-faithful to what the browser draws. Playwright is the *only* thing a user installs, and it is an **optional peer dependency**: when it (or its Chromium binary) is missing, the export returns a copy-pasteable install command instead of failing.

> This supersedes the original external-package approach — the engine is now vendored in-repo, so installing `@helping-ai-workflow/slide-to-pptx` is no longer required.

## How it works

- New dev-server route `POST /__os/api/export/pptx` (registered in `api-plugin.ts`, `apply: 'serve'`).
- A preflight probes Playwright. **Missing** → JSON `{status:'playwright-missing'}` with `<pm> add -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium`. **Present** → SSE progress stream, then a base64 `.pptx` `done` event.
- Engine under `packages/core/src/vite/pptx/` (server-only): load deck → render HTML → measure with Chromium → IR → pptxgenjs → OOXML post-process.

## File layout

| Area | Files |
|---|---|
| Render engine (server-only) | `packages/core/src/vite/pptx/*` |
| Dev-server route + handler | `vite/routes/export-pptx{,-handler}.ts`, `pm-detect.ts` |
| Client trigger + toasts | `app/lib/export-pptx-native.ts`, `app/components/pptx-*-toast.tsx` |
| UI wiring | `app/routes/slide.tsx` (activates the reserved slot) |
| Deps / build | `package.json`, `tsdown.config.ts`, scoped `biome.json` override |

## Minimal-impact notes

- `slide.tsx`: only the reserved *Coming soon* slot becomes a working item, mirroring the existing `exportImagePptx`. HTML / PDF / image-PPTX paths are untouched.
- New runtime deps: `esbuild`, `pptxgenjs`, `jszip`, `fast-xml-parser` (server-side only — they never reach the browser bundle). `playwright` is a `devDependency` + an **optional** `peerDependency`, so existing consumers are never forced to download Chromium.
- `biome.json`: one override turns off `noExplicitAny` / `noNonNullAssertion` for `packages/core/src/vite/pptx/**` only (the vendored engine does heavy DOM/OOXML work); no author-owned path is affected.

## Test plan

- `pnpm typecheck` ✅ · `pnpm format:check` + `pnpm lint` ✅ · `pnpm test` ✅ 289/289 (new: `export-pptx-handler.test.ts` incl. path-traversal + playwright-missing, `pm-detect.test.ts`).
- End-to-end on a real consumer (21 decks): every deck exports; **0 shapes overflow** the 1920×1080 canvas; cover titles render exactly once.
- SVG stress fixtures verified in PowerPoint: multi-subpath `<path>` (X / +) no longer draws a connecting segment; filled paths (diamond / circle) render; cubic/quadratic/arc curves intact.
- Playwright-missing path verified end-to-end (returns the correct install prompt).

## Open question

The engine adds a few MB to `@open-slide/core` (pptxgenjs/jszip/etc.); Chromium (~130 MB) stays opt-in via the peer. If you'd prefer to keep core leaner, I'm happy to split the engine into a separate workspace package instead — your call.

author: copilot
body:
`awf-api-proxy` could be marked healthy before upstream LLM connectivity was ready, so early `awf-reflect` model discovery hit `503` and wrote incomplete `awf-reflect.json`. This also consumed Claude startup retry budget during the first minutes of a run.

- **Retry policy for startup 503s**
  - Added bounded retry logic in `fetchModelsFromUrl` for HTTP `503` responses.
  - Uses exponential backoff with explicit limits:
    - `AWF_MODELS_URL_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5`
    - `AWF_MODELS_URL_RETRY_BASE_MS = 250`
    - `AWF_MODELS_URL_RETRY_MAX_MS = 2000`
  - Non-`503` responses and other failures retain existing best-effort behavior (no throw, return `null`).

- **Behavioral intent**
  - Keep pre-flight reflect capture opportunistic, but avoid failing fast on transient proxy warmup states.
  - Improve chances that initial `awf-reflect.json` includes model lists instead of requiring teardown-time recovery.

- **Focused test coverage**
  - Added tests for:
    - `503 -> 503 -> 200` recovery path
    - repeated `503` path stopping at max attempts
  - Updated constant assertions for new retry/backoff settings.

```js
if (res.status === 503 && attempt < AWF_MODELS_URL_MAX_ATTEMPTS) {
  const backoffMs = Math.min(
    AWF_MODELS_URL_RETRY_BASE_MS * 2 ** (attempt - 1),
    AWF_MODELS_URL_RETRY_MAX_MS
  );
  await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, backoffMs));
  continue;
}
```

author: menobass
body:
## Summary

- Replaces `@tus/server` (Node.js, no Concatenation extension) with the official `tusd` Go binary, which supports the TUS Concatenation extension natively
- Enables `parallelUploads: 3` on `tus-js-client` — three 10MB chunks upload simultaneously instead of sequentially (~2.5–2.8x faster per the legacy app's benchmarks)
- Moves IPFS pinning to async `post-finish` processing — clients receive their 204 the moment the file lands on disk, not after the full IPFS pin completes

## How it works

tusd runs as a child process of Node.js, spawned after Express starts listening. Express proxies all `/uploads/*` traffic to tusd on `127.0.0.1:1080`. Two HTTP hook endpoints on Express drive the logic:

- **`POST /tusd-hooks` (pre-create):** validates auth (API key or upload token), creates the video DB record, injects `X-Embed-URL` into the 201 response via tusd's hook response format. Partial uploads (parallel chunk pieces) are auth-validated but not DB-recorded — the token is consumed only on the final concatenated upload.
- **`POST /tusd-hooks` (post-finish):** responds immediately (tusd already sent 204 to client), then runs IPFS pin + job creation asynchronously via `setImmediate`.

## Zero breaking changes

Existing frontends see identical behaviour — same `/uploads` endpoint, same `X-Embed-URL` header, same auth methods (X-API-Key + Bearer token), same error codes, same webhook format.

## Deploy step required

```bash
bash scripts/install-tusd.sh
```

Must be run on the server before starting the app. Downloads tusd v2.9.2 to `./bin/tusd` (gitignored).

## New env vars (optional, sensible defaults)

```
TUSD_PORT=1080          # internal port tusd listens on
TUSD_BINARY_PATH=./bin/tusd
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `bash scripts/install-tusd.sh` — binary appears at `./bin/tusd`
- [ ] `npm run dev` — logs show `[tusd] Supported tus extensions: ...,concatenation,...` and `[tusd] Using /uploads as the base path`
- [ ] Upload via demo page — `X-Embed-URL` visible in browser DevTools on the 201 Created response
- [ ] Upload completes — client gets success **before** IPFS pin log lines appear in terminal (confirms async)
- [ ] DB: video transitions `uploading` → `processing` → `published`
- [ ] Existing frontend with API key — no behaviour change

body: ### Description of the Change Adds the ability to export all redirect rules from the wp-admin redirect list table as either a CSV or JSON file. A format dropdown and an **Export** button appear in the top toolbar of the Redirects screen. Selecting a format and clicking Export downloads the file immediately. Each exported record includes: ID, Redirect From, Redirect To, HTTP Status Code, Enable Regex, Force HTTPS, Message, and Status. The export is protected by a nonce and a capability check using the existing `srm_restrict_to_capability` filter, so only authorized users can trigger a download. CSV output is also protected against formula injection attacks. Closes # Partially related to https://github.com/10up/safe-redirect-manager/issues/43 After adding the Export feature, we can add the .htaccess export support too. PR is designed to be able to easily extend any future export types. ### How to test the Change 1. Go to the **Redirects** list table in wp-admin (Admin Dashboard -> Tools -> Safe Redirect Manager). 2. Confirm an **Export** feature (CSV / JSON dropdown and "Export" button) appear at the top of the table. 3. Select **CSV** → click **Export** → verify a `.csv` file downloads with all redirect data and correct column headers. 4. Select **JSON** → click **Export** → verify a `.json` file downloads as a valid JSON array with the same data. 5. Confirm the existing **Filter** button still works normally. 6. author: noctonca
body:
`scripts/dev/build-and-run.sh` — what `make run` shells out to — still tried to exec the pre-bundle path `build/SOURCES/lba2cc`, so the build succeeded and then `exec` failed with `No such file or directory` and `make run` died with exit code 127. That commit updated the CI workflows, DMG/bundle scripts, and macos-readme, but missed the developer-facing build-and-run script.

## What this changes

In `scripts/dev/build-and-run.sh`:

- Also read `LBA2_PRODUCT_NAME` from `CMakeCache.txt` (fallback matches the default in the root `CMakeLists.txt`).
- On `Darwin`, prefer `$LBA2_PRODUCT_NAME.app/Contents/MacOS/$LBA2_EXECUTABLE_NAME` when it exists and is executable; fall back to the old direct path otherwise (handles bundle-disabled builds and stale build dirs).
- Linux and Windows/msys2 keep the old path verbatim — the `uname -s` guard never triggers on them, and the bundle treatment in `SOURCES/CMakeLists.txt` is itself gated on `if(APPLE)`.
- Bump the `LBA2_EXECUTABLE_NAME` fallback from the long-dead `lba2` to `lba2cc` to match the current default in `CMakeLists.txt` (`b40f5fa`, "build: rename default binary lba2 -> lba2cc"). The cache value is what gets used in practice; this only matters when `CMakeCache.txt` is missing or malformed.

## Test plan

- [x] macOS arm64: `make run` boots past "Initialising Sample device" and "LBA2 Classic Community 0.11.0-dev" — the `exec` call that previously failed now succeeds.
- [x] Path resolution dry-run: `BIN` resolves to `…/LBA2 Classic Community.app/Contents/MacOS/lba2cc`, executable, Mach-O arm64.
- [ ] Linux / Windows (msys2): unchanged code path — `uname -s` guard skips the bundle branch, exec target identical to before.

author: yyding1
body:
## Summary

Adds a new `local_attach` deployment type so agents can attach to a long-running, user-managed swerex sandbox (typically a docker container the user starts once and reuses across runs), instead of paying the spin-up/tear-down cost on every run via `LocalDeployment`. This unblocks workflows that need persistent state inside the sandbox — installed packages, OAuth-ed CLIs, bind-mounted workspaces, etc.

`examples/lark/demo.py` is the motivating use case: `lark-cli` needs an interactive OAuth login that has to survive across runs, which is awkward with the per-run container model.

## Changes

- **`local_attach` deployment** (`uni_agent/deployment/local_attach/`)
  - `start()` opens an HTTP client, verifies the server is alive, and (re)creates a clean default bash session.
  - `stop()` is a no-op; the container is owned by the user.
  - Registered in `deployment/config.py` and `deployment/__init__.py`.

- **`copy_to_remote` opt-out for system tools** (`uni_agent/tools/base.py`, `uni_agent/interaction/env.py`)
  - New `AbstractTool.copy_to_remote: bool = True`. When `False`, `install_tools()` skips the copy+chmod step and only runs `get_install_command()` + a `which <name>` presence check. `local_path` defaults to `None` on the base class.
  - Models tools whose binary the user installs separately and is already on PATH (npm/apt/brew installs).

- **`lark-cli` becomes a system tool** (`uni_agent/tools/lark_cli/`)
  - Sets `copy_to_remote = False`, drops the `local_path` override, and deletes the bundled `lark-cli` wrapper script.
  - Fixes a silent footgun: when `tool_install_dir` overlapped with the npm prefix (often `/usr/local/bin`), the framework's wrapper script would overwrite the real `@larksuite/cli` binary, and the wrapper itself could then no longer find a "real" lark-cli to exec into.

- **Demos** (`examples/agent_env/demo.py`, `examples/lark/demo.py`)
  - Both gain a `local_attach` dispatch branch. `examples/lark/demo.py` is now pluggable via `LARK_DEPLOYMENT={local_native|local_attach}` (default `local_native`, so existing behavior is preserved). Module docstring documents the one-time container bootstrap.

author: elektronaut
body:
`ExchangePostsController#create` averaged ~32 queries per write. The bulk came from `Post#update_post_counts` (3 COUNTs + 3 UPDATEs across exchange/user), `DiscussionRelationship.define` running `update_user_caches!` twice (4 COUNTs × 2), and a redundant `@exchange.reload` in the controller.

Switched `Post belongs_to :user/:exchange` to `counter_cache: true`, replaced the COUNT-based `update_user_caches!` with per-flag deltas via `User.update_counters`, simplified `.define` to a single `find_or_initialize_by`/`save`, and dropped the controller reload. A common follow-up post on an existing discussion now issues 7 queries instead of ~32.

## Problem

The build fails during BUILD_IMAGE because Railpack detects the Pipfile and attempts to install pipenv via pipx 1.12.0, which crashes with `ImportError: module 'pipx' has no attribute 'main'`. This is a toolchain version incompatibility in Railpack's bundled pipx.

author: tangvarie
body:
PR #23 的 4 条 review 反馈全部修复。Supabase 那边的 ALTER 已经先跑过（migration `phase2_session_indexes_fix`），本 PR 同步 `db.py` 代码到最终形态，保证新部署直接走对的 schema。

## 修复对照

| # | reviewer 命中 | 修复 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 路由索引非唯一 → 并发 insert 撕裂 session | `CREATE INDEX` → **`CREATE UNIQUE INDEX`** `generation_sessions_route_uniq` partial on `WHERE status='active'`。race 时一方撞 23505 → 失败方 re-lookup 拿到赢家 |
| 2 | `append_session_messages` turn_idx 竞态 → 撞 unique 后静默丢消息 | retry loop（`_APPEND_RETRY_MAX=3`）+ `_is_unique_violation` 识别（substring `23505` / `duplicate key` / `unique constraint`），race 时退避 50/100ms 重新算 max 重试 |
| 3 | `project_idx` 用 `created_at` 但查询按 `last_used_at` 排 → extra sort | 索引改成 `(project_id, last_used_at DESC)` |
| 4 | `get_or_create_active_session` lookup 失败直接 return None | refactor: lookup 失败仍走 insert; insert 失败 re-lookup 一次（catch race winner）; 抽出 `_lookup()` 内部 helper |

## Supabase 同步

已 apply 的 migration（这次顺手做了，所以本 PR 合并部署不需要额外手动操作）：

```sql
-- migration: phase2_session_indexes_fix
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS autowriter.generation_sessions_route_idx;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS generation_sessions_route_uniq
    ON autowriter.generation_sessions(...)
    WHERE status = 'active';

DROP INDEX IF EXISTS autowriter.generation_sessions_project_idx;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS generation_sessions_project_idx
    ON autowriter.generation_sessions(project_id, last_used_at DESC);
```

验证过：

```
generation_sessions_route_uniq    UNIQUE  WHERE (status = 'active')
generation_sessions_project_idx   btree   (project_id, last_used_at DESC)
```

## 行为影响

仍然零业务接入——CRUD helpers 没人调用。本 PR 仅让数据层在 Phase 2.1 接入前真正"并发安全 + 失败可恢复"。

## 还没做的

reviewer 没提但 Phase 2.1 接入时可能要补的：
- worker 并发场景明确——目前队列是串行单线程，理论上没有同 session 并行追加；future 如果要做"多项目并行生成"，retry loop 才真正派上用场
- Supabase Python client 的 PostgrestAPIError 类型可能在新版 SDK 里更精确（不再依赖 substring）；如果将来升级 SDK 可以把 `_is_unique_violation` 换成 `isinstance(exc, PostgrestAPIError) and exc.code == "23505"`

author: dongtigerlu
body:
## Problem

Running `prometheon validator run --config ~/prometheon-testnet.toml` on testnet 481 surfaced:

```
cycle 1 failed: Missing chain_network / platform_instance_id binding.
```

Same `EnvMatchGuard` failure as PR #53, but on snapshot endpoints rather than `/nonce`. The previous fix only patched the request body for `/nonce`; snapshot reads are GETs with no body, so the env-binding has to travel in headers.

## Where the gap was

`_signed_get_json` in `BitFanClient` builds the request as follows:

- The signed `ApiRequestPayload` (used to compute the signature) correctly carries `chain_network` + `platform_instance_id`.
- BUT the actual HTTP request only sent: `Authorization`, `X-Prometheon-Hotkey`, `X-Prometheon-Nonce`, `X-Prometheon-Timestamp`, `X-Prometheon-Request-Signature`, `Client-Name`.

The platform's `EnvMatchGuard` looks for env binding in headers `X-Prometheon-Chain-Network` + `X-Prometheon-Platform-Instance-Id` (option 1 of its three forms — the only one applicable to GET requests). Both were missing, so the guard 400'd before the handler ran.

## Fix

Add the two missing headers to `_signed_get_json`:

```python
"X-Prometheon-Chain-Network": self._chain_network.value,
"X-Prometheon-Platform-Instance-Id": self._platform_instance_id,
```

The values come from the same `self._chain_network` / `self._platform_instance_id` that are already embedded in the signed `ApiRequestPayload`, so signature coverage is unchanged. No new server-side trust assumption: a man-in-the-middle can't forge new header values because the signature still covers the canonical payload that contains them.

## Test changes

Added two assertions to `test_signed_get_includes_authorization_and_signed_headers` so future regressions on the header set fail at the unit-test level.

## Verification

- 488 tests pass.
- mypy strict clean.
- ruff check + format clean.
- Next `validator run` cycle should reach `compute_phase1_weight_plan` (or surface a different platform error if there is one downstream).

author: andymai
body:
## Summary

- Replaces the placeholder `elevator_ffi.yy` with an auto-generated `GMExtension` manifest so end-users can drop the extension folder into GameMaker Studio's Asset Browser instead of running the 5-step manual recipe.
- Schema modeled on [`YoYoGames/GMEXT-Steamworks`](https://github.com/YoYoGames/GMEXT-Steamworks/blob/main/source/Steamworks_gml/extensions/steamworks/Steamworks.yy) — the only public reference extension I could find with the same Windows + macOS + Linux desktop x64 shape we ship. Field ordering and the `copyToTargets` / `TargetMask` integers are copied verbatim because GMS appears to be strict about re-save diffs and there aren't official docs for the platform bit layout.
- Moves binaries from `binaries/` to extension root (sibling of the `.yy`) — `GMProxyFile.name` resolves against the manifest's directory, and Steamworks places its binaries the same way.

## Manifest scope (v1)

What the manifest **declares**:
- `elevator_ffi.ext` (zero-byte stub) as the canonical extension file, with three `GMProxyFile` entries for `elevator_ffi.dll` / `libelevator_ffi.dylib` / `libelevator_ffi.so`.
- `copyToTargets: 194` (desktop x64 only — no HTML5, mobile, or console targets).
- Calling convention via `kind: 4` on the file (cdecl on x64).

What it does **not** declare (intentional):
- **Zero functions.** `elevator_ffi_generated.gml` already binds every `_gms` shim via `external_define`; listing the same names in the manifest would double-bind at import time. Migrating function declarations into the manifest (and dropping the generated GML file) is the v2 follow-up issue #869 alludes to — it needs a working baseline import first.
- **No `IncludedResources`**. GMS treats sibling `.gml` files as separate Script resources during folder-drop import, so the helpers come along without being listed. If a GMS version regresses on that, switch to explicit entries.

## Layout changes

- `binaries/.gitkeep` removed; the directory is gone.
- `examples/gms2-extension/extension/elevator_ffi/.gitignore` added to keep `*.dll` / `*.dylib` / `*.so` build artefacts out of git.
- `elevator_ffi.ext` committed as a zero-byte stub at the new root location — the manifest's `filename` field references it, and GMS expects it to exist at import time.
- `.github/workflows/release-please.yml` updated to drop each cdylib at the extension root instead of `binaries/`.

## Manual verification needed

I can't validate that GMS Studio imports this cleanly without running GMS Studio locally. **Please verify before merging:**

1. Build the cdylib for your platform: `cargo build -p elevator-ffi --release`
2. Copy it next to the `.yy`: `cp target/release/libelevator_ffi.{so,dylib} examples/gms2-extension/extension/elevator_ffi/` (or `elevator_ffi.dll` on Windows).
3. Drag-and-drop `examples/gms2-extension/extension/elevator_ffi/` into a fresh GMS project's Asset Browser.
4. Confirm: the extension imports without errors, the binary is picked up for your target, and a Create-event probe of `ev_decode_u64(ev_abi_version())` returns `5`.

If anything fails on the GMS side (wrong field order, wrong target mask, missing field, wrong file layout), I'll iterate on this branch.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 scripts/gen-gms-bindings.py` — idempotent on re-run.
- [x] `bash scripts/lint-docs.sh --quick` — README changes pass.
- [x] Pre-commit hook (`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy`, `cargo test`, ABI pins) — all green.
- [x] Generated `.yy` is structurally valid JSON-with-trailing-commas (visually compared against Steamworks reference; field order matches).
- [ ] **Manual GMS Studio import on macOS arm64 / Windows / Linux** — pending your verification.

Closes #869 pending manual import verification.

author: mahalisyarifuddin
body:
Title: 🩺 Medic: Fix date inputs showing wrong local day due to UTC conversion

🔍 Diagnosis: In `HilalMap.html`, `elements.mapDate.valueAsDate = today;` was used. `valueAsDate` interprets the provided `Date` object based on its UTC value. For users in timezones like `Asia/Jakarta` (+07:00), opening the map at 6:00 AM local time means it is 23:00 the previous day in UTC. Consequently, the input would wrongly display yesterday's date.
📍 Location: `HilalMap.html` (around line 705)
💥 Symptoms: Date inputs default to the wrong day (yesterday or tomorrow) depending on the user's timezone and time of day.
💉 Treatment: Instead of using `valueAsDate`, constructed a local date string (`YYYY-MM-DD`) using `.getFullYear()`, `.getMonth()`, and `.getDate()` (with `padStart`), and assigned it to the `.value` property. This approach mirrors the robust local date formatting already present in `HijriCalc.html`.
🧪 Test: Simulated a browser timezone of `Asia/Jakarta` using Playwright and manually checked that local date `2024-05-15 06:00:00+07:00` correctly populated the input as `2024-05-15` instead of `2024-05-14`. Verified project-wide tests remain fully functional.

# Frontend Pull Request Description

## Title
**PR: Cashier POS Checkout, Interactive Maps, i18n Auditing, and Accessibility Hardening**

## Sprint Context
- **Sprint**: Sprint 4 (Cashier POS & Geographic Triangulation)
- **Period**: April 20, 2026 – May 4, 2026
- **Status**: Merged into `dev`

---

## Overview
This PR introduces major client-side visual and functional upgrades: a complete Cashier/POS portal overhaul, high-fidelity Leaflet map interfaces for branch locator and competitor analysis, standardisation of API responses with TypeScript contracts, and full i18n support across all five portals.

---

## Detailed Changes

### 1. Cashier POS Overhaul
- **POS Checkout Modal**: Designed and wired the cashier checkout interface supporting manual cash payments, card swipes, and insurance coverages.
- **Inventory Access Restriction**: Enforced read-only safety permissions on the cashier inventory page to restrict branch stock modifications to managers/owners.
- **Cashier Orders View**: Structured order lists to separate pending walk-ins, deliveries, and finalized counter sales.

### 2. High-Fidelity Map Integrations
- **Branch Management location Picker**: Integrated a draggable map location picker for branch registration forms, allowing owners to visually select branch coordinates.
- **Patient & SA Global Map**: Created maps to render neighboring pharmacies, including a sidebar filter list showing distances and active hours.
- **Competitor Toggles**: Added interactive map toggles for branch managers to see competing pharmacies within vicinity.

### 3. Internationalization (i18n) & Localization
- **Strings Decoupling**: Replaced hardcoded strings across all portals (Patient, Pharmacist, Cashier, Owner, and Superadmin) with `t()` translation keys.
- **Localization Files**: Completed and audited translation dictionary files for English (`en.json`), French (`fr.json`), and Kinyarwanda (`rw.json`).
- **Role Translations**: Wires localized navbar options, password reset screens, stats cards, and inventory tables.

### 4. Accessibility (a11y) & Code Quality Hardening
- **Accessibility Hardening**: Resolved screen-reader issues by assigning explicit `id` attributes to all forms, adding `aria-label` tags, and ensuring form inputs map correctly to `<label>` elements.
- **TypeScript & API Response Contracts**: 
  - Standardised types on the frontend by replacing generic `any` casts with strictly typed interfaces (`User`, `Order`, `Branch`, etc.).
  - Added silent catch blocks and toast errors to handle API failures gracefully.

---

## Major Paths Impacted

- `src/app/staff/orders/page.tsx` — POS checkout & order views
- `src/app/pharmacy/map/page.tsx` — Geographic triangulation map
- `src/types/index.ts` — Type definitions standardisation
- `src/context/AuthContext.tsx` — Route protection and role checks
- `public/locales/` — i18n translations dictionaries

---

## Verification & Build
- **Type Safety**: Verified zero compilation errors in the NextJS build sequence (`npm run build`).
- **ESLint & Accessibility Checks**: Passed strict linter validations with no active accessibility warnings.
