author: dpws
body:
## Summary

- Imperative singleton `toast` API + a single `<ToastViewport>` portal. Mount once at app root; fire from anywhere — no provider, no hook.
- 5 tones (`info`, `success`, `warning`, `error`, `loading`) with sensible icon + color defaults. `error` is `role=\"alert\"` (assertive); the rest are `role=\"status\"` (polite).
- All 6 positions supported via the viewport's `position` prop; per-call `position` override available as an escape hatch.
- Auto-dismiss defaults to 4000ms; per-call `duration` (ms or `'persistent'`). Pause-on-hover / pause-on-focus / pause-when-tab-hidden.
- Action slot (Undo/Retry), close (×) button, programmatic dismiss + update by id, `toast.promise()` sugar.
- \`maxVisible: 3\` default with peek-collapsed stack behind the visible toasts; hover-to-expand or \`expand: true\`.
- \`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce\` disables enter/exit + reflow + spinner animations.
- No new packages, no new tokens.

## Architecture

Three-layer split:

- **\`store.ts\`** — vanilla observable (no React imports). \`add/update/dismiss/subscribe\`. Testable in isolation.
- **\`api.ts\`** — public \`toast\` singleton. Thin wrapper over the store. Pure JS too. Reads viewport defaults from a module-level config slot the viewport writes on mount.
- **\`<ToastViewport>\`** — the only React surface. \`useSyncExternalStore\` + \`createPortal\` to \`document.body\`. Owns hover-expand state per position bucket. Detects multiple-viewport mounts and dev-warns + renders null on the second instance.

Per-toast dismiss timer is its own hook (\`useToastTimer\`) — captures remaining ms on pause, re-arms on resume, integrates with \`document.visibilitychange\` via a \`getVisible()\` indirection so tests can simulate hidden tabs without poking jsdom internals.

## Test coverage

**65 new tests** across 4 files:

- \`store.test.ts\` — 13 cases (add/update/dismiss mechanics, subscribe, id uniqueness)
- \`api.test.ts\` — 21 cases (tone shorthands, persistent default for loading, dismissible-forced-on-persistent, promise resolve+reject)
- \`useToastTimer.test.ts\` — 7 cases (pause/resume math, persistent skip, hidden=paused, unmount cleanup, mid-life duration change)
- \`Toast.test.tsx\` — 24 cases (integration: tones, role mapping, auto-dismiss, pause-on-hover/focus, action+close buttons, programmatic dismiss/update, position routing, maxVisible peek-collapse, hover-expand, \`toast.promise\` resolve+reject, multi-viewport dev-warning)

## Hard Rule 8

Two rounds with fresh-context reviewers (opus). Round 1 surfaced 4 Important findings:

1. **JSDoc on \`toast\` API was missing** — added to the callable + every method, with \`@example\` blocks on \`toast()\` and \`toast.promise()\`.
2. **\`prefers-reduced-motion\` didn't silence the spinner** — added \`.spin { animation: none }\` inside the media query.
3. **\`structure.test.ts\` regex was over-permissive after the T6 loosening** — tightened from \`\\b\${name}\` to \`\\b\${name}(\\b|[A-Z])\` so \`Toast\` matches \`ToastViewport\` but \`Button\` doesn't false-match a missing-Button scenario.
4. **No pause-on-focus integration test** — added one wired through the action button.

Round 2 verdict: clean enough to stop. 0 Critical + 0 Important.

All four gates green: \`make test\` (1324 passing) + \`make build-lib\` + \`make build\` + \`make lint\` + \`npm pack --dry-run\` (no test files in tarball).

## Regression-watch (flagged for future work, NOT in scope here)

- **\`lucide-react\` is missing from \`peerDependencies\`.** Pre-existing repo-wide issue; 16+ library files import from it but the package.json doesn't declare the dep. Workspace hoisting masks it locally. Should be filed as a separate fix.
- **\`mountedViewportCount\` is fragile under future React lifecycle changes.** StrictMode-safe today; future-proofing would use a \`Set<symbol>\` subscribed via useEffect exclusively.

## Test plan

- [ ] Tone gallery renders 5 toasts with correct accent stripe color + icon (3px stripe, not 1px)
- [ ] \`toast.error\` produces \`role=\"alert\" aria-live=\"assertive\"\`; other tones use \`role=\"status\" aria-live=\"polite\"\`
- [ ] Auto-dismisses after the configured duration; \`duration: 'persistent'\` does not
- [ ] Hovering pauses the timer; leaving resumes
- [ ] Tabbing into the action or close button pauses; blurring resumes (verified by the new round-1 test)
- [ ] Switching browser tabs pauses ALL timers; switching back resumes
- [ ] Action button fires \`onClick\` AND dismisses
- [ ] Close (×) dismisses; \`dismissible: false\` hides it; \`duration: 'persistent'\` force-shows it
- [ ] Programmatic \`toast.update(id, ...)\` mutates in place
- [ ] \`toast.success('msg', { id })\` with an existing id updates rather than duplicating
- [ ] \`toast.promise(p, msgs)\` cycles loading → success/error and returns the original promise
- [ ] Per-call \`position\` routes to the right bucket
- [ ] \`maxVisible: 3\` with 5 toasts shows 3 fully + 2 peek-collapsed; hovering fans them out
- [ ] \`expand: true\` keeps the stack always fanned
- [ ] \`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce\` disables enter/exit AND the loading spinner
- [ ] Two \`<ToastViewport>\` mounted → dev-warning fires, only the first renders
- [ ] Playground demo at \`/components/toast\` runs all 8 examples without console errors

body:
Description :
When a user has two contracts, the second one always fails with "3Int auth returned 401 / Username could not be found."

Root causes:
1. get_contracts() resolves numserie by taking the first IClient_Compteur in the included section, giving both contracts the same (wrong) serial. The correct path is contrat.pconso_id → IClient_Pconso → compteur → numserie
2. Each coordinator calls authenticate() independently, causing mutual Omega SSO session invalidation between the two config entries.
3. A single _3int_token is shared across contracts instead of per-contract.

author: kimsoungryoul
body:
## Summary

- **ADR-0052** documents the 3-methodology cross-validation of `aerospike-py.batch_read` hot path AND incorporates the load test results from [`aerospike-py#374`](https://github.com/aerospike-ce-ecosystem/aerospike-py/pull/374) (`feat!: LazyBatchRecords handle + GIL-detach to_numpy(dtype)`)
- Confirms **client-side Rust micro-optimization ceiling of ≤ 0.32% RPS** for plain (dict) batch_read
- Promotes **B7 (NumPy direct path) from "recommended" to "Accepted — implemented via PR #374"** with +13~43% RPS measured

## Dependency

This ADR assumes `aerospike-ce-ecosystem/aerospike-py#374` merges. Both PRs should land together (or this PR after #374).

## Why this matters

8 measurement cycles produced rich but fragmented data. This ADR consolidates the findings so future contributors don't re-litigate already-decided micro-optimizations and instead focus on the scenarios where measurable wins exist. PR #374's load test data turns the "B7 NumPy +20-40%" *recommendation* into a *measured contract* — +13~43% RPS depending on feature dimensionality.

## Four measurement methodologies

| # | Method | What it measured | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `oha` sweep (44 measurements) | RPS across {batch size} × {concurrency} × {GIL, no-GIL} × {plain, threaded} | plain c=10..200 GIL vs no-GIL = ±1% (no GIL bottleneck); threaded c=100 no-GIL +56.7% |
| 2 | Rust tracing crate stage timing | μs/call wall percentage of 5 sub-stages | `batch_to_dict_py` = **0.32% of wall** |
| 3 | py-spy --native (arm64 Linux container, `--privileged --cap-add SYS_PTRACE`) | Sample-based flamegraph with resolved symbols (`cargo rustc -- -C debuginfo=2 -C strip=none`) | `batch_to_dict_py` = **0.24% of samples** (5/2126) — matches methodology 2 |
| 4 | **PR #374 load test (DICT vs NUMPY)** | Single uvicorn worker `oha` benchmark, DLRM-shaped 200-record batch | **+13% / +31% / +43% RPS** for c=50 f16 / c=50 f32 / c=100 f32 |

Methodologies 2 and 3 converge on dict path's wall %. Methodology 4 confirms B7 (numpy path) supersedes dict path with measurable +13~43% RPS.

## Key findings

1. **Plain batch_read (dict path) client-side Rust optimization ceiling = 0.32% RPS** — `B3` / `B4` / `B5` / `B6` all collapse into noise floor (±2-5%). All rejected for 1.0.0 GA.
2. **`py.detach()` GIL-release-during-conversion is a new design pattern** distinct from PyO3 free-threaded (D1):
   - D1 (`gil_used = false`): build-wide no-GIL, +28.7% `PyDict::set_item` hidden cost
   - `py.detach()` (PR #374): in-conversion GIL release via raw `ptr::write_unaligned` — no PyObject creation, no critical section locking
   - Two paths are complementary: `to_numpy` for data-science workloads, no-GIL build for CPU-bound + ThreadPoolExecutor
3. **B7 NumPy path implemented via PR #374**: `handle.to_numpy(dtype)` + `torch.from_numpy` zero-copy chain. `conv_ms` 2.88× faster, `inference_ms` 1.74× faster.
4. **PyO3 free-threaded hidden cost quantified (first measurement)** — `PyDict::set_item` is **+28.7% slower** in 3.15t no-GIL build. `value_to_py` (PyObject creation) is unaffected (+0.3%).
5. **New candidates B9 / B10 deferred** — py-spy --native surfaced PyO3 cross-cutting cost. Leaf time small, cumulative inclusion high. Targeted at 1.0.x patch cycle.
6. **Stage timing infra is production-ready** — `AEROSPIKE_PY_INTERNAL_METRICS=1` + Prometheus `/metrics` exposes `db_client_internal_stage_seconds_*` histograms.

## macOS arm64 profiling limits documented

- Tachyon (`profiling.sampling`): sudo required + Rust frames stripped to `<native>`
- py-spy 0.4.2 on macOS arm64: `--native` itself unsupported
- podman amd64 emulation: `qemu-x86_64-static` wrapper hides emulated python from ptrace
- **Resolution**: arm64 Linux container path is the default for future measurement cycles

## Operational guide (1.0.0 GA companion)

After PR #374 merges, the recommended usage patterns become:

- **DLRM / PyTorch CPU-inference (highest priority)**:
  ```python
  handle = await client.batch_read(keys)
  arr = handle.to_numpy(dtype=dlrm_dtype)   # GIL-released raw memory write
  tensor = torch.from_numpy(arr)             # zero-copy
  output = model(tensor)
  ```
- **Existing dict-style code (no migration needed)**: `LazyBatchRecords` implements the Mapping protocol — `handle.items()`, `handle["k"]`, `"k" in handle`, `len(handle)` all keep working.
- **High-concurrency HTTP (RPS > 1000)**: `uvicorn --workers N`.
- **CPU bound + I/O mix**: 3.15t no-GIL build + ThreadPoolExecutor — +56.7% confirmed for threaded c=100.

## Cross-references

- Builds on ADR-0001 (PyO3 over CFFI — memory safety principle informs B9 deferral)
- Builds on ADR-0009 (Unified BatchRecords API — measurement target surface, PR #374 evolves this contract)
- Builds on ADR-0047 (NumPy Batch Owned Arrays — B7 path's memory model, PR #374 adds `py.detach()` to it)

## Test plan

- [x] Docusaurus build (`npm run build`) passes — no broken links, no MDX parsing errors
- [x] Frontmatter validates (`sidebar_position: 52` unique, no collisions)

author: copilot
body:
Four distinct gameplay/visual fixes: tile corruption overlays were deferred to turn-end instead of appearing during animation; graveyards couldn't spawn on frozen water; secondary damage (splash, cleave, pierce, brandmark) produced no floaters or animations; and pierce/cleave had no VFX at all.

## Tile corruption — instant visual

- **MAGMA_SPYR**: `BUILDING_ATTACK` event gains optional `tileCorruptedPosition`; `applyEvent` immediately writes `tile.status = CORRUPTED` so the overlay renders during animation.
- **CORRUPT_TERRAIN**: `corruptTerrain` now accepts `events?: GameEvent[]` and pushes a `TILE_CORRUPTED` event after placing the building. New `applyEvent` case adds the building + sets `tile.buildingId`, making the sprite visible from the moment the event plays rather than at `setGameState`.

## Graveyards on frozen water

`isValidGravestoneTile` previously excluded all `WATER` unconditionally:
```ts
// before
tile.terrainType !== TileType.WATER
// after
(tile.terrainType !== TileType.WATER || tile.status === TileStatus.FROZEN)
```

## Secondary damage events

`resolveAttack` gains `outEvents?: GameEvent[]`. SPLASH, CLEAVE, and PIERCE sections push `SPLASH_DAMAGE` / `CLEAVE_DAMAGE` / `PIERCE_DAMAGE` events plus `UNIT_DEATH`s into it. Both `attackUnit` (player) and `ATTACK_UNIT`/`RANGED_ATTACK_UNIT` (enemy) collect and queue these after primary deaths. New `applyEvent` cases deduct HP and fire floaters. Brandmark tick also gains a floater per branded unit.

## Pierce / cleave VFX

- **Cleave**: `CleaveVfx` added to `combatAnimationStore`; `CleaveVfxLayer` renders an expanding red slash ring (`@keyframes cleaveSlash`, 350 ms) centred on the attacker at 1.25-tile radius.
- **Pierce**: reuses `addProjectile` — fires a 🗡 from the primary defender's tile to the secondary target at 160 ms/tile.
- **Splash**: HIT shake on each secondary target.
- All three handlers in `processQueue` consume the following `UNIT_DEATH` inline so kills animate correctly.

author: omerarslan0
body:
Adds \`release.yml\` — the atomic release pipeline.

**Job graph (strict ordering):**
1. \`build\` — 6-platform NAPI build, \`fail-fast: true\`
2. \`publish-bindings\` — publishes 6 \`@nookdb/binding-<triple>\` packages with provenance
3. \`publish-dispatcher-and-main\` — injects \`optionalDependencies\` into dispatcher manifest, publishes \`@nookdb/binding\`, \`nookdb\`, \`@nookdb/react\`, \`@nookdb/electron\`, \`@nookdb/cli\` in order
4. \`publish-crates\` — \`cargo publish -p nookdb-core\`
5. \`github-release\` — extracts CHANGELOG section, creates GH Release

**Triggers:** \`v*.*.*\` tag push OR \`workflow_dispatch\` with \`dry-run\` input.

**Atomicity invariant:** \`publish-dispatcher-and-main\` only runs after ALL 6 \`publish-bindings\` succeed → a published main package always has all its bindings resolvable on npm.

Third piece of NookDB 1.0.0 release (Phase 3).

## Summary

Two small, unrelated-but-bundled changes per request:

### 1. QA-FIXES #18 — Bash PS1 first-prompt missing `\W` _(probable fix, needs device QA)_

Changes `pty-adapter.ts` default `shellArgs` from `['-l']` to `['-l', '-i']`. Login mode (`-l`) stays so the shell picks up `.bash_profile` / `.zprofile` env (PATH, NVM, etc.); explicit interactive (`-i`) forces bash to treat the session as interactive from word zero, which on some setups makes `.bashrc`'s prompt-defining block fire on prompt #1 instead of after the next keystroke.

**Honest caveat:** I couldn't pin down the exact root cause without device access. Sean's bash setup probes correctly locally (login PS1 has `\W`, env `PWD` already seeded by the existing line at `pty-adapter.ts:410`), and there's no `cd` injection between spawn and first prompt. The `-i` add is the most plausible single-line shot. If the broken first prompt still repros after this lands, we iterate live on-device — likely a redraw / attach-timing issue I can't see from here.

### 2. Close out Pairing Reboot phase doc

author: johngavin
body:
## Problem

PR #256 set the default backup target to iCloud Drive based on `~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/` existing. That directory exists on all macOS installs by default — but on this Mac **iCloud Drive sync is not active**. The dir contents:

```
$ ls -la ~/Library/Mobile\ Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/
.DS_Store
Desktop -> /Users/johngavin/Desktop
```

No synced files, no Documents folder pointing INTO iCloud. Backups written there would NOT replicate anywhere → silently fails the `backup-architecture` rule's "different failure domain" requirement.

## Fix

Switch the default `BACKUP_ROOT` to **Dropbox**, which IS active on this Mac:

```
$ ls -la ~/Dropbox
~/Dropbox -> ~/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox
```

Dropbox provides a genuine different-failure-domain target (Dropbox servers + paired devices).

### Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `.claude/scripts/unified_duckdb_backup.sh` | `ICLOUD_ROOT` → `DROPBOX_ROOT`, default points at `~/Dropbox/Backups/unified_duckdb/`; header comment + `--help` + flag docs updated; rationale comment notes "iCloud not active" so future agents don't re-make the same assumption |
| `plans/228-unified-duckdb-backup.md` | Recommendation flipped; iCloud row in comparison table marked "would silently fail" with explanation |
| `RECOVERY.md` | Backup location, failure-domain description, restore commands all point at `~/Dropbox/Backups/unified_duckdb/` |

### Override still supported

```bash
BACKUP_ROOT=/some/other/path ~/.claude/scripts/unified_duckdb_backup.sh --apply
# or
~/.claude/scripts/unified_duckdb_backup.sh --apply --dest /some/other/path
```

## Verification

- `bash -n unified_duckdb_backup.sh` → exit 0
- `SELFTEST=1 bash unified_duckdb_backup.sh` → **10/10 PASS**
- Dry-run smoke test: `dest=/Users/johngavin/Dropbox/Backups/unified_duckdb` ✓
- `~/Dropbox` resolves (symlink to `~/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox`) ✓

## Why iCloud wasn't caught earlier

The #228 agent saw the directory exist and assumed sync. Future safeguard: the rationale comment in `unified_duckdb_backup.sh` now explicitly notes the verification check (synced-content absence) so any subsequent agent that wants to flip back to iCloud has to grapple with that evidence.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Fixes Flyway/Hibernate configuration issues that could prevent migrations from working correctly in Docker.

**Changes to `application.yml`:**

1. **`ddl-auto: validate` → `none`** — With `validate`, Hibernate tries to validate entity mappings against the DB schema. On a fresh database where Flyway hasn't run yet, `validate` would fail because the tables don't exist. `none` is the correct setting when Flyway manages the schema.

2. **Removed explicit `hibernate.dialect: PostgreSQLDialect`** — Spring Boot auto-detects the dialect from the JDBC URL. The explicit setting was generating a Hibernate deprecation warning (`HHH90000025: PostgreSQLDialect does not need to be specified explicitly`).

3. **Added `validate-on-migrate: true`** — Flyway will now fail fast if migration checksums don't match (e.g., if a previously-applied migration file was modified), providing clearer error messages.

**Investigation results:** I built the Docker image, extracted the JAR, and confirmed migration files ARE correctly packaged at `BOOT-INF/classes/db/migration/`. I also ran the backend locally against a fresh Postgres — Flyway successfully applied both migrations and created all 10 tables. The "zero Flyway log lines" issue was likely caused by:
- Stale Docker image layers (fix: `docker compose build --no-cache backend`)
- Or the previous `baseline-on-migrate: true` bug (fixed in PR #3)

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] `docker compose down -v` to wipe all volumes
- [ ] `docker compose up --build` (or `docker compose build --no-cache backend` first if you suspect layer caching)
- [ ] Check backend logs for Flyway output — should see "Successfully applied 2 migrations"
- [ ] Verify tables: `docker exec bt-postgres psql -U bt_user -d billiontech -c '\dt'`

### Notes
- Verified locally: Flyway runs on startup, creates all 10 tables, seeds demo tenant + admin user. Backend tests still pass with H2.
- If you previously ran the app with `validate`, you may have a corrupted schema state. `docker compose down -v` will reset everything cleanly.

author: bgozlinski
body:
## Summary

  US-20 (M3 #3) — the heart of the reservation flow (FR-07). A logged-in user opens
  `/screenings/<id>/book/`, submits a seat count, gets a PENDING booking (15-minute
  window), and is redirected to a stubbed checkout. Race-safe via
  `transaction.atomic()` + `select_for_update()` on the Screening row.

  Three independently-testable layers:

  - **`BookingCreateView`** (`apps/booking/views.py`) — thin `LoginRequiredMixin` view.
    GET renders the form + screening summary; POST validates `BookingForm` (US-19),
    calls the service, then redirects on success or re-renders (200) on error.
  - **`create_booking`** (`apps/booking/services.py`) — shared web+API entry point.
    Locks the Screening row, re-checks availability + start time **under the lock**
    (authoritative; the form is a pre-check), creates the PENDING booking
    (`expires_at = now + 15m`), commits, then creates the checkout session **after
    commit** (the row lock is never held across a network call). Signals failure via
    `NotEnoughSeatsError` / `ScreeningInPastError`.
  - **`create_checkout_session`** (`apps/payments/services.py`) — stub returning the
    movie-detail URL + empty session id. US-24 fills this one function with the real
    Stripe SDK (FR-21).

  Available screenings' time-pills on the movie detail + screening list pages now link
  to `booking:create`; sold-out/past pills render as non-clickable spans.

  ## Design decisions (brainstormed)

  - Service extracted now (FR §4/§8 shared with the M4 API) — view stays thin, race
    logic is unit-testable without HTTP.
  - Stripe call **after commit** — never hold the DB row lock across the network; an
    orphan PENDING from a failed checkout is self-healing via `expire_pending_bookings`.
  - Race-loss → re-render the form (200) with a non-field error, keeping the user in
    context with refreshed availability.

  ## Linked

  - Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-23-us20-booking-create-design.md`
  - Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-23-us20-booking-create.md`
  - Closes US-20

  ## Definition of Done

  - [x] `create_booking` — atomic + `select_for_update` + re-check + PENDING (`expires_at = now+15m`); Stripe
  after commit; returns `(booking, checkout_url)`
  - [x] `NotEnoughSeatsError(available)` / `ScreeningInPastError` / `BookingError` base
  - [x] `create_checkout_session` stub → `(movie_detail_url, "")`
  - [x] `BookingCreateView` — GET render, POST valid→redirect+flash, invalid/`BookingError`→re-render 200
  - [x] `booking:create` at `/screenings/<int:pk>/book/`, included in `settings/urls.py`
  - [x] `booking_form.html` — summary + form + locale-safe JS live total
  - [x] Time-pill CTAs wired in both cinema templates
  - [x] 17 tests green (payments 1, service 6, threaded 1, view 9)
  - [x] `ruff` + `mypy` clean; `makemigrations --check` exits 0; `pytest --cov` ≥ 80%

  ## Test plan

  - **`tests/payments/test_services.py`** (1) — stub returns `(movie_detail_url, "")`
  - **`tests/booking/test_services.py`** (6) — PENDING + 15m expiry, checkout url, no session id with stub,
  `NotEnoughSeatsError` (+ `.available`), `ScreeningInPastError`, sequential overbooking impossible
  - **`tests/booking/test_services_concurrency.py`** (1) — `transaction=True` + 2-thread Barrier on a 5-seat
  screening; exactly one wins, total ≤ capacity
  - **`tests/booking/test_views.py`** (9) — anon GET/POST → login; GET 200 + 404; POST valid → create + redirect
   + flash; invalid form → 200 no booking; mocked service error → 200 non-field error; past screening → 200
  error

  ## Out of scope (follow-up)

  - Real Stripe Checkout → US-24 (replaces the payments stub)
  - Booking detail `/bookings/<id>/` → US-21
  - My-bookings / cancel / expire / webhook → US-22 / US-23 / US-26 / US-25

author: beng360
body:
## Summary

- Switch frontend dev stage from `oven/bun:alpine` to `node:22-alpine` (bun kept for package management)
- Add `experimental.turbopackMemoryLimit: 512MB` in next.config.ts to cap Turbopack cache
- Add `NODE_OPTIONS: --max-old-space-size=1024` in docker-compose.yaml to hard-limit V8 heap

## Root Cause

The Linux OOM killer was targeting the frontend's `bun` process (confirmed via `dmesg`):

```
Out of memory: Killed process 5252 (bun) total-vm:75025492kB, anon-rss:1617560kB
```

Three factors:
1. **Bun's JSC GC** doesn't collect aggressively under memory pressure — process grew from 550MB to 1.6GB
2. **No Turbopack memory limit** — in-memory module graph grew without bound (315 routes, 47K files)
3. **Docker VM has only 7.7GB** for 18 containers totaling 7.4GB at peak — OOM killer chose bun as largest process

Additionally, bun's `v8.getHeapStatistics()` polyfill reports a fake 296MB `heap_size_limit`, which broke Next.js's built-in memory restart (exit code 77 at 80% of heap limit) — it could never trigger correctly.

## Result

| Metric | Before (bun) | After (node) |
|--------|-------------|--------------|
| Startup memory | 548 MB | 244 MB |
| Peak after compilation | 1.6 GB+ (unbounded) | ~800 MB (capped) |
| V8 heap limit | 296 MB (fake polyfill) | 1024 MB (real) |
| Auto-restart at 80% | Broken | Works correctly |

## Test plan

- [x] `docker compose build frontend` succeeds
- [x] Container starts, Next.js compiles and serves pages
- [x] `turbopackMemoryLimit: 536870912` shown in startup logs
- [x] Memory stays bounded after compiling multiple routes
- [x] Process tree: `node next-dev` (PID 1) → `next-server` (child) — proper fork/restart chain

author: phanijapps
body:
## Summary

Closes the top of gap #1 from `memory-bank/future-state/2026-05-22-hermes-comparison-gaps.md` — the Hermes Curator equivalent, on the right substrate. After re-framing (Hermes "skill" structurally maps to a z-Bot **ward**, not a z-Bot skill), this PR ships Phases A + B from the spec at `memory-bank/future-state/2026-05-23-ward-curator-spec.md`.

Phase C (LLM consolidation) is intentionally deferred to a follow-up.

### Phase A — per-ward usage telemetry

- New `gateway-services::WardUsage` service that owns the sidecar `~/Documents/zbot/wards/.usage.json`.
- Schema mirrors Hermes: `use_count`, `patch_count`, `last_used_at`, `last_patched_at`, `created_at`, `created_by` (`bundled` / `user` / `agent`), `state` (`active` / `stale` / `archived`), `pinned`, `archived_at`.
- Atomic writes (temp + rename) + internal `std::sync::Mutex` for serialised RMW. Malformed sidecars are treated as empty.
- Bump points wired:
  - `ensure_wards_dir` / `ensure_wiki_ward` → `mark_created(Bundled)` for `scratch` and `wiki`.
  - `RunnerDelegationInvoker::spawn_delegation` → `bump_use` for every `ward:<name>` delegation, before any locking. Failures warn but never block.
- Read endpoints (under `/api/curator/` to avoid colliding with `/api/wards/:ward_id/...`):
  - `GET /api/curator/usage`
  - `GET /api/curator/usage/:ward`
  - `POST /api/curator/usage/:ward/pin`

### Phase B — heuristic cleanup endpoint + weekly cron

- New `gateway-services::WardCurator` service: walks the sidecar, applies transitions on agent-created, non-pinned wards using `anchor = max(last_used_at, last_patched_at, created_at)`:
  - `age > archive_days` → `Archived` + ward dir moved to `wards/_archive/<name>/`
  - `age > stale_days` (active) → `Stale` (sidecar only)
  - stale + recent activity → reactivated
- Bundled / user-authored / pinned wards counted but skipped.
- Defaults match Hermes: `stale=30d`, `archive=90d`, `backup_keep=5`.
- Pre-run `.tar.gz` snapshot of `wards/` (excluding `_curator_backups/` and `_archive/`) under `wards/_curator_backups/<utc-iso>.tar.gz`. Older snapshots beyond keep=5 pruned at start of each run.
- Per-run audit log: `<vault>/data/curator_logs/<ts>/{run.json, REPORT.md}`.
- Endpoints:
  - `POST /api/curator/cleanup` with optional body `{ dry_run, stale_days, archive_days }`. Empty body / `{}` runs with defaults. Dry-run skips backup and mutation. No-op runs (zero transitions) also skip the backup.
  - `POST /api/curator/restore` body `{ "backup": "<utc-iso>" }` un-tars the named snapshot back over `wards/`.
- `gateway/templates/default_cron.json` ships a Monday 03:00 entry that POSTs to the cleanup endpoint via a `general-purpose` agent + `curl`.

### Out of scope / known follow-ups (explicit)

- **Cold-path `mark_created(Agent)` hook** — the `ward(action='create')` tool lives in `agent-tools` and would need a cross-crate callback (or an event-bus listener). Until then, agent-scaffolded wards lazy-insert as `user`, which the curator skips by design. Safe default.
- **LLM-less `kind: "http"` cron action** — the weekly cron currently spawns a `general-purpose` agent to invoke `curl`. Direct HTTP cron actions would remove the LLM-in-the-loop fragility. ~50 lines in `gateway-cron`, separate PR.
- **Phase C (LLM consolidation curator)** — heals `defect_ward_routing_fragmentation` retroactively. Separate PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo build --workspace` — clean
- [x] `cargo test -p gateway-services --lib` — **151** passed (16 new tests across `WardUsage` and `WardCurator`)
- [x] `cargo test -p gateway --lib` — **223** passed
- [x] `cargo test -p gateway-execution --lib` — **410** passed
- [x] `cargo clippy -p gateway -p gateway-services -p gateway-execution --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] Endpoint hit live: `POST /api/curator/cleanup {dry_run:true}` returns `{scanned:2, skipped_non_agent:2, transitions:[]}` (scratch + wiki correctly skipped as bundled)
- [x] Endpoint hit live: `POST /api/curator/cleanup {}` returns the same — no-op skips backup as designed
- [ ] Live archival flow (requires seeding a fake `created_by:agent` ward — full walkthrough in the chat; not testable on a fresh vault since the cold-path provenance hook is the deferred follow-up above)

## Spec & related docs

- Spec: `memory-bank/future-state/2026-05-23-ward-curator-spec.md`
- Gap analysis: `memory-bank/future-state/2026-05-22-hermes-comparison-gaps.md`

author: scott-davidjones
body:
## Summary
Makes `agent-browser` actually work for the top-level agent. With `runtime.persistentAgent`, the top-level agent's bash runs **inside the warm `dae-worker` (the daedalus image) via HostRuntime** — that's the only place a stateful browser CLI can run, because a per-call `container.image` spawns a throwaway container per command and kills the browser between `open` and `snapshot`. So the Chromium runtime libs belong in this image.

## Changes
- `Dockerfile`: install Chromium's system libs via `playwright install-deps chromium` (Node is already in `node:24-slim`). Also adds the common foundation agent bash assumes (`wget xz-utils bzip2 procps iproute2 iputils-ping less`) + `LANG=C.UTF-8`.

## Companion change (separate, in the brain)
`artemis.md` must **drop `container.image`** so its bash runs in the warm worker (HostRuntime) rather than per-call containers. (Done in the brain repo.)

## Why HostRuntime, not a dev-* leaf
`runtime/docker.ts` runs `container.image` agents as `docker run --rm` **per command** — boot lag per call, and the browser daemon dies between commands. HostRuntime keeps bash in the persistent worker: warm, and the Chromium binary the bootstrap downloads is in the same container the bash uses.

## Validation
`playwright install-deps chromium` on `node:24-slim` is the same step already validated earlier (built clean, libs present via `ldconfig`). The build self-fails if `install-deps` errors.

## Deploy
- Merge → release → `dae update` on casa (rebuilds the daedalus image with the libs).
- Apply the `artemis.md` change (drop `container.image`) to casa's brain.

author: phjodor
body:
The Telegram worker runs runtime.turn() in a worker thread and only sends a message once the full reply is ready, so during a long turn the human sees nothing that confirms their message registered. This adds a lightweight typing indicator.

_keep_typing() re-sends ChatAction.TYPING on a 4s interval (Telegram clears the indicator after ~5s) for the duration of the turn. It is started before the turn and cancelled in a finally block in both _on_text and _on_photo, so it stops on success, error, and silence alike. Send errors are swallowed so the indicator can never fail a turn, and no_response/silence semantics are unchanged: the indicator stops as soon as the turn returns, before the reply/silence branch. No new dependencies (ChatAction ships with python-telegram-bot, pinned >=21.0).

## Summary

Fix scroll prevention for lightbox and tutorial overlays when `overflow-x:clip` is applied to the `<html>` element. Previously, `overflow: hidden` on `body` alone was insufficient in this case because the scroll container shifts to `<html>`.

## Changes

- **styles.css (line ~713)**: Added `html:has(body.lightbox-open)` selector alongside `body.lightbox-open` to ensure scroll is locked at the `<html>` level when lightbox is active
  - Updated comment to explain the issue: when `overflow-x:clip` exists on `<html>`, the scroll container becomes `<html>` rather than `body`, so `body` alone's `overflow:hidden` is insufficient
  
- **styles.css (line ~1148)**: Applied the same fix for tutorial overlay with `html:has(body.tutorial-open)` selector alongside `body.tutorial-open`

## Implementation Details

Both changes use the CSS `:has()` pseudo-class to target the `<html>` element when the respective `.lightbox-open` or `.tutorial-open` class is present on `body`. This ensures that scroll prevention works correctly regardless of whether `overflow-x:clip` is set on the root element, maintaining consistent behavior across different CSS configurations.

author: svilgelm
body:
A few robustness fixes from a code review of the pkgsite client.

- Detect oversized success bodies and fail with a clear error instead of silently truncating them into invalid JSON (and breaking connection reuse).
- Surface the cancellation cause when the context is cancelled during retry backoff, rather than masking it with the transient error.
- Cap the backoff shift so `retryBase << attempt` cannot overflow into a misleadingly small delay.
- Rework the response cache as a true LRU (promote on read) bounded by both entry count and total bytes, so large doc/README/license payloads cannot grow it without limit.

Adds unit tests for each. `go vet` clean and the full suite passes under `-race`.

body:
## Summary
Replaced Next.js `useRouter` with `window.location.assign()` for post-authentication redirects in login and signup forms. This ensures a full page reload after authentication, allowing server-side session validation and middleware to properly execute.

## Changes
- **LoginForm.tsx**: Removed `useRouter` hook and replaced `router.refresh()` + `router.push()` with `window.location.assign(redirectTo)`
- **SignupForm.tsx**: Removed `useRouter` hook and replaced `router.refresh()` + `router.push()` with `window.location.assign('/golf-intelligence')`

## Implementation Details
Using `window.location.assign()` triggers a full page navigation that:
- Forces a complete page reload from the server
- Allows server-side middleware and session validation to run
- Ensures the user's authenticated session is properly established before rendering protected pages
- Simplifies the redirect logic by removing the need for client-side router state management

author: debugging-in-prod
body:
Go's encoding/json treats `[]uint8` (and named slices of uint8-underlying types) as byte slices and base64-encodes them on the wire. Since TileType was uint8, `[]TileType` came across HTTP as a base64 string like "AgICAgIC..." instead of `[2, 2, 2, ...]`.

The dashboard renderer indexes `snap.tiles[y*width + x]` expecting a number, instead got a single character; every TILE_COLORS lookup missed and fell through to TileUnknown's `#111` near-black. The canvas rendered mostly black with only the furniture glyphs visible (furniture is a struct slice and serializes correctly).

Fix: TileType's underlying type goes from uint8 to int. JSON will then encode `[]TileType` as a normal number array. Doc comment now explains why so it doesn't regress.

Verified locally that the post-fix endpoint will return tiles as an array; the deployment will refresh the snapshot fixture and the renderer will see actual TileType values.

author: consultingfuture4200
body:
## What

Closes MBOX-307 (parent epic MBOX-282 — `/dashboard/chat`).

The chat answered content questions via RAG but gave unhelpful **and factually wrong** answers to operational/aggregate questions ("how many emails have we ingested," "who do we email most," "what do you have access to"). Those fall below the RAG relevance floor → the 4B model got no grounding → and the old `PLAIN_SUFFIX` ("answer from general knowledge") let it confabulate a partly-false self-description, e.g. claiming *"email content is not stored on the device"* — the opposite of what the appliance does.

Per the issue's decision (**stats-context injection, not 4B function-calling**), this computes the appliance's real numbers with cheap read-only aggregates and injects them as a compact facts block into the chat context — the same mechanism as the RAG context block.

## Changes

- **`dashboard/lib/queries-chat-stats.ts`** (new) — `getApplianceStatsContext()`: inbound totals + 24h/7d/30d windows + earliest/latest `received_at`, category breakdown (from the `inbox_messages.classification` denorm), top-5 inbound senders + top-5 outbound recipients (`sent_history`), draft queue counts (pending/approved/sent/rejected). Kysely via `getKysely()`, counts coerced from the numeric-as-string convention, empty tables → zeros. **No migration** (read-only over existing tables).
- **`dashboard/lib/chat/assemble.ts`** — pure `renderApplianceStatsBlock` (≤ ~12 lines, sized for the 4096-ctx model); inject it as an always-present `system` turn (independent of retrieval reason), distinct from and ordered before the RAG block. Persona rewritten to describe the box accurately (it DOES ingest/embed/store email locally) and forbid fabricating numbers/capabilities; dropped the "answer from general knowledge" line; kept the DR-56/SM-74 no-quote guard.
- **`dashboard/lib/chat/orchestrate.ts`** — compute stats alongside retrieval via an injectable `getApplianceStats` seam; a stats-query failure degrades to no block (logs, does not abort the turn).
- **Tests** — DB-backed stats helper (seeds inbox/sent/draft rows, asserts counts); assemble renderer + persona accuracy + block ordering; orchestrate graceful-degradation. Existing assemble tests updated to the rewritten prompt strings.

## Verification (local only — no live-box deploy)

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run db:codegen:verify` — types up to date (no schema change)
- `npx biome check` on changed files — clean
- Vitest: chat-assemble + chat-orchestrate 29/29; queries-chat-stats 5/5 against a throwaway `postgres:17-alpine` fixture (real `test/fixtures/schema.sql`)

LOCAL-ONLY invariant (DR-53) preserved — stats come from the local Postgres `mailbox` schema, nothing cloud-bound.

The previous fix called `getVoices()` to check if an Arabic voice was installed, but `getVoices()` returns `[]` on the first call (voices load asynchronously). This caused it to always fall back to English.

Remove the `getVoices()` check entirely — just set `utt.lang = 'ar'` and let the OS pick its own Arabic TTS engine. On Android with Google TTS (pre-installed), this speaks Arabic directly without needing to enumerate voices.

author: alexktchen
body:
## Summary

This PR establishes comprehensive documentation and verification infrastructure to prevent silent data truncation caused by PostgREST's `max_rows = 1000` limit. It includes normative standards, a detailed audit of existing risks, fix tracking, and test scripts.

## Key Changes

### Documentation
- **STANDARD-資料分頁與筆數限制.md**: Mandatory specification defining three approved pagination patterns (cursor-based, JSONB aggregation, server-side range loops) and strict rules for money/quantity fields. Includes code review checklist and tool recommendations.
- **AUDIT-資料截斷風險清單-2026-05-23.md**: Comprehensive inventory of 26 identified truncation risks across the codebase, categorized by severity (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) with specific file locations, risk descriptions, and remediation strategies.
- **FIX-LOG-資料截斷修復.md**: Structured log for tracking remediation progress with standardized entry format.

### Code Fixes
- **supabase/migrations/20260628100010_rpc_member_campaign_detail.sql**: New RPC returning JSONB (single row) to aggregate campaign item details and ordered quantities, eliminating PostgREST truncation risk for campaign detail pages. Marked `@money-critical`.
- **supabase/migrations/20260628100020_rpc_member_campaign_aggregates.sql**: New RPC returning JSONB array to aggregate order counts and quantities across all campaigns, fixing both the old `rpc_member_campaign_order_counts` SETOF truncation and the `listActiveCampaigns` orderRows reduce pattern.
- **supabase/functions/liff-api/index.ts**: 
  - Refactored `getCampaignDetail()` to use single `rpc_member_campaign_detail` RPC call instead of multiple queries
  - Refactored `listActiveCampaigns()` to use `rpc_member_campaign_aggregates` RPC, eliminating unsafe frontend reduce aggregation of order quantities
  - Added truncation sentinel logging when main query returns ≥1000 rows

### Verification Scripts
- **scripts/audit-pagination/test-11-12-campaign-detail-ordered-qty.mjs**: Node.js test verifying campaign detail RPC correctly aggregates >1000 order items
- **scripts/audit-pagination/test-11-12-via-mgmt-api.sh**: Bash test using Supabase Management API to verify ordered_qty accuracy with >1000 orders
- **scripts/audit-pagination/test-13-14-campaign-aggregates.sh**: Bash test verifying campaign aggregates RPC handles >1000 campaigns correctly
- **scripts/audit-pagination/README.md**: Guidelines for test script naming, environment setup, and execution

## Notable Implementation Details

- **JSONB Single-Row Pattern**: Both new RPCs return `RETURNS jsonb` instead of `RETURNS TABLE`, making them immune to PostgREST's 1000-row limit regardless of data volume
- **Cleanup Verification**: Test scripts include explicit verification that fixture cleanup succeeded, detecting silent transaction rollbacks caused by triggers
- **Truncation Sentinels**: Added console.error logging when queries approach or hit the 1000-row limit to catch future regressions
- **Money-Critical Annotations**: All functions handling quantities/amounts marked with `@money-critical` comments referencing the standard document
- **Backward Compatibility**: Old RPC `rpc_member_campaign_order_counts` SQL preserved (not deleted) to avoid symbol resolution issues if other callers exist

## Verification Status

✅ All fixes verified in erp-dev environment:
- Campaign detail RPC correctly returns `ordered_qty=1100` when given 1100 order items
- Campaign aggregates RPC correctly counts 1100 orders across campaigns
- Test data cleanup confirmed complete (no orphaned fixtures)

author: a-afanasyev
body:
## Summary

Sprint 10 PR-4 — operator-driven "mute this sensor" backend. Without this, a stuck sensor creates a reopen-loop (verifier reopens → УК new ticket → operator closes → verifier reopens) until \`max_reopens_per_24h\` trips engineer_required. Suppression lets the operator say "yes I know, ignore this for N hours" with a 24h cap.

**Hooks into PR-2 verifier via the conditional-require pattern already shipped** in \`alertVerificationService._drainOne\` — as soon as \`AlertSuppression\` model exists, the verifier consults \`isActive()\` before emitting \`VERIFY_*\` events. **Zero changes to verifier code.**

Plan: \`docs/superpowers/plans/tingly-munching-badger.md\` (Sprint 10 PR-4)
Builds on: PR #46 (PR-2 verification scaffolding)

## What changes

**Migration 026** — \`alert_suppressions\` table
- Keyed on \`(infra_type, infra_id, alert_type)\` — NOT alert_id, so suppression survives the reopen chain (each reopen gets a new alert_id but the underlying entity stays the same)
- \`reason\` enum (\`faulty_sensor\` / \`under_repair\` / \`planned_maintenance\` / \`known_issue\` / \`other\`) for operator analytics
- Partial \`idx_suppression_active\` keyed on cleared_at + tuple + suppress_until (Postgres rejects \`NOW()\` in partial WHERE — runtime query filters expired rows from heap, partial scan first cut)
- Conditional GRANT block (mirrors 022/025 pattern)

**\`src/models/AlertSuppression.js\`** (~180 LoC)
- \`isActive(infraType, infraId, alertType)\` — fail-open on DB error to avoid blocking verifier from a transient DB hiccup
- \`create(data)\` — validates required fields, duration > 0, duration ≤ 24h cap, reason enum membership
- \`clear(id, clearedBy)\` — idempotent (returns null on already-cleared row)
- \`findById\`, \`list({active, infraType, infraId, alertType, limit})\` — limit clamped to 500
- Exports \`MAX_SUPPRESSION_HOURS\` + \`VALID_REASONS\` constants

**\`src/controllers/alertController.js\`** — 3 new handlers
- \`suppressAlert(req, res)\` — POST /api/alerts/:alertId/suppress — looks up the alert tuple, validates body, creates suppression with \`req.user.user_id\` as suppressed_by
- \`clearSuppression(req, res)\` — DELETE /api/alerts/suppressions/:id — records who cleared
- \`listSuppressions(req, res)\` — GET /api/alerts/suppressions — translates query params to model filters

**\`src/services/alertService.js\`** — adds \`getAlertById(alertId)\` (needed by suppressAlert to read {infra_type, infra_id, type} from the alert row)

**\`src/routes/alertRoutes.js\`** — 3 new routes (all admin-only, \`applyCrudRateLimit\`)
- \`POST /:alertId/suppress\`
- \`GET /suppressions\` — list with filters
- \`DELETE /suppressions/:id\` — clear early

## Test plan

- [x] \`npm run lint\` clean
- [x] \`npm test\` — 104 suites / 2093 tests pass (was 2068; +25 new)
- [x] **25 new AlertSuppression model tests**:
  * isActive: truthy when active row matches; false when no row; fail-open (false) on DB error
  * create: validates required fields, duration > 0, duration ≤ 24h cap, reason enum, accepts all 5 reasons, defaults comment/suppressed_by to null
  * clear: updates cleared_at + cleared_by; idempotent (null on already-cleared); throws on missing id
  * list: no-filter default (ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 100); active=true/false; tuple filters; limit clamp to 500
  * findById; exported constants (MAX_SUPPRESSION_HOURS=24, VALID_REASONS=5 items)
- [x] **1 new alertVerificationService test**: suppression-active path — \`AlertSuppression.isActive=true\` → \`markSuppressed(verificationId)\` + NO \`VERIFY_LEAK\` emit; quota check skipped (return-early after suppression branch)
- [x] PR-2 verification tests unchanged (default \`isActive=false\` mock keeps original assertions green)
- [x] Migration 026 applied locally; \`\\d alert_suppressions\` shows partial index, CHECK constraint, FK references

## API examples

\`\`\`bash
# Suppress LEAK alerts for controller of alert #21 for 4 hours
curl -X POST /api/alerts/21/suppress \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin_token>" \\
  -d '{"duration_hours": 4, "reason": "faulty_sensor", "comment": "Sensor stuck on"}'

# List currently-active suppressions
curl /api/alerts/suppressions?active=true \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin_token>"

# Clear early
curl -X DELETE /api/alerts/suppressions/5 \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin_token>"
\`\`\`

## Rollout

Standalone — no feature flag needed. Suppression has zero effect until an operator creates one. The verifier (PR-2) is still dormant via \`ALERT_VERIFICATION_ENABLED=false\` so even active suppressions don't affect anything in prod until that flag flips.

## Follow-ups

- **PR-3**: wires \`alertService.resolveAlert\` to enqueue verifications, completing the reopen loop
- **PR-5**: admin UI «Схема интеграции с УК» — adds "Suppress" button on alert detail screen + suppression list view

body:
### Motivation
- Prompt-injection proof fields and top-level chat-context summaries could be left stale/default after the final prompt was built, causing Support Snapshot to contradict the actual dispatched prompt.
- When planner/envelope indicated `mission-planning` but chat-context metadata remained `direct-answer`/`unknown`, the Command Deck produced unhelpful “Current mission: Unknown” answers despite available project-awareness fields.
- Provide a bounded, truthful degraded mission synthesis for mission-planning/operator next-action prompts so answers are useful without inventing unavailable truths.

## 📚 Description

User backlog: "when trying to shoot but there is no ammo (and requires reload) then communicate this to the user with an animation like shooting but no ammo effect and display a text saying R to reload". Implemented as a deny sfx + a 0.8s centred prompt above the pistol.

This is the last of the ammo overhaul (PR1-3 ammo reserve / boxes / low-ammo warning, PR5 reload animation). Combined they cover the full ammo gameplay loop with audio + visual feedback at every state transition.

## 🔖 Changes

### Combat
- `:empty-click-secs 0.0` initial on world; `empty-click-seconds 0.8` const; decayed in `decay-timers`.
- New `empty-trigger-pull` helper arms the timer + plays `:click` sfx.
- `tick-shooting` rewritten as a `cond`:
  1. no fire → world
  2. `can-fire?` → fire-shot
  3. **empty-mag with no other gate active → empty-trigger-pull**
  4. else → silent
- Suppressed during fire-cooldown / jam / reload because each of those already has its own visual cue and stacking another would be noise.

### Sound
- New `:click` event → `Basso.aiff` (macOS deny sound — dull thud, gun-adjacent transient).

### Render
- New `paint-empty-click` helper + p17 chain step.
- Yellow ` -- CLICK -- press R to reload ` when reserve > 0; red ` -- CLICK --   OUT OF AMMO   ` when both pools dry.
- Centred via measured `strlen` so the two variants line up even when their lengths differ.
- Anchored at row `vh - 7` (two rows above the pistol muzzle).

### Tests
- 5 new `tick-shooting` cases pin every gate: happy path arms timer; skip on fire-cooldown; skip on jam; skip during reload; no-fire short-circuit.

### Docs
- `combat.md` documents the dry-fire path.
- `can-fire?` docstring updated since empty mags are no longer silent.

## ✅ Verification

- `composer ci` → 0 lint, 357 tests (+5 in this PR).
- `clean-code-reviewer`: caught (a) missing jam-gate test (blocker, fixed), (b) red label off-centre due to length mismatch (fixed: dynamic centring via `strlen`), (c) stale `can-fire?` docstring (fixed), (d) suggested reload-cooldown test (added).

author: patrick-erichsen
body:
## Summary

This PR adds V1 NVIDIA-style Skill Cards to ClawHub as generated Markdown artifacts. The product shape is intentionally artifact-first: ClawHub stores a generated `skill-card.md` on each skill version, renders it on the skill detail page, exposes it through HTTP, and provides a CLI verification endpoint/command.

## Background and User Impact

Agent skills are installable instruction bundles, so users need a clearer way to inspect provenance, release evidence, and scanner context before trusting a skill. Before this change, ClawHub had scan metadata and file hashes, but no generated human-facing Skill Card artifact tied to a release. Users also could not script against a single verification envelope, and `clawhub update` needed to keep working when generated release files like `skill-card.md` are included in installed bundles.

## What Changed

- Adds a Skill Card generation queue that runs after static scan and ClawScan inputs have settled.
- Builds a server-owned evidence packet containing publisher, server-resolved provenance, release data, file hashes, parsed metadata, capabilities, and ClawScan risk findings.
- Reuses NVIDIA's public Skill Card tooling as the context-generation helper, then renders final public Markdown through a neutral ClawHub template to avoid NVIDIA-only boilerplate.
- Stores generated cards as `skill-card.md` in `skillVersions.files` and replaces that file on regeneration for the same version.
- Adds a generated bundle fingerprint after attaching the card while preserving the source fingerprint.
- Lets `/api/v1/skills/resolve?slug=&hash=` match either the original source fingerprint or a generated bundle fingerprint.
- Adds `/api/v1/skills/:slug/card?version=&tag=` for Markdown card retrieval.
- Adds `/api/v1/skills/:slug/verify?version=&tag=` for JSON verification metadata.
- Adds `clawhub skill verify <slug>`, with JSON as the default output and `--card` for raw Markdown.
- Adds a Skill Card tab in the skill detail UI only when `skill-card.md` exists.
- Adds local dev worker support so background workers can run in a normal local product loop.
- Adds a GitHub Actions Skill Card worker triggered after the Security Scan Codex Worker completes, plus manual dispatch.

## Security and Trust Boundaries

Provenance remains fail-closed. The Skill Card evidence packet uses only server-resolved GitHub import provenance stored on the version; it does not trust author-claimed frontmatter or generic publish payload metadata. The CLI and `/verify` verdict use structured DB security metadata, not Markdown parsing.

## Validation

- `AUTOREVIEW_AUTO_TESTS=0 .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch` clean after accepted fixes.
- `bunx vitest run convex/lib/skillCards.test.ts convex/lib/skillPublish.test.ts --pool=forks --maxWorkers=2`
- `bun run lint:oxlint -- convex/lib/skillCards.ts convex/lib/skillCards.test.ts convex/lib/skillPublish.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `bun run ci:static`
- `bun run ci:unit`
- `bun run ci:types-build`
- `bun run ci:packages`
- `bun run ci:e2e-http`
- `bunx tsc -p packages/schema/tsconfig.json --noEmit`
- `bunx tsc -p packages/clawhub/tsconfig.json --noEmit`

## Notes for Review

This deliberately avoids a rich formal trust-card schema in V1. The generated Markdown artifact is the product surface, with `/verify` serving as the scripting-oriented JSON surface.

author: eyupcanakman
body:
When a `case` expression is used as a step in a pipeline, the JavaScript code generator could declare the same `_pipe$N` variable twice in one scope. That is a `SyntaxError`.

A directly matching `case` branch generates its code into the enclosing scope, so the counters for the compiler's internal variables have to survive past it. Before this only the `$` case subject counter was kept. The `_pipe` counter got reset, so the next step in the outer pipeline reused the name.

Fixes #5743.

author: bmaurer
body:
## What got implemented:

- Support ECDSA certs
- Throw on cert/key mismatch
- Throw if only one of key/cert is provided
- Infer HTTPS mode if key/cert is provided: we don't really need explicit HTTPS env
- Support an extra `DOCUSAURUS_` prefix for env variables (`DOCUSAURUS_HTTPS=true`), taking precedence over unprefixed env variables

Let's consider all this as a v3 bug fix, that will be backported and released in a patch release.

---

On v4, we'll:
- Add the new CLI args, as a new public api feature to document and mention in a release blog post => https://github.com/facebook/docusaurus/pull/12082
- Think about deprecating env vars (?)



---
---
---

## Original PR:

Two related fixes to `getHttpsConfig` in `docusaurus start`:

1. The validator in `getHttpsConfig.ts` used `crypto.publicEncrypt` / `crypto.privateDecrypt` to sanity-check the cert/key pair, but those APIs only work for RSA keys. Passing ECDSA (or EdDSA) certs — common in many corporate PKI setups — caused the dev server to throw `operation not supported for this keytype` even though the cert is fine.

   Replaced with `crypto.X509Certificate` + `crypto.createPrivateKey`, which work for any key type and additionally catch genuine cert/key-pair mismatches (the old code silently produced garbage in that case rather than throwing).

2. Certs could previously only be supplied via the `SSL_CRT_FILE` and `SSL_KEY_FILE` environment variables. Added matching `--ssl-cert <path>`, `--ssl-key <path>`, and `--https` CLI flags. CLI takes precedence; passing both `--ssl-cert` and `--ssl-key` implies HTTPS.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

Extended `getHttpsConfig.test.ts` from 5 to 13 tests. The original 5 still pass (no behavior change for the RSA happy path). New coverage:

- ECDSA cert + key is accepted (would have thrown before this PR).
- Valid cert + valid-but-different key is rejected with a clear "do not match" error.
- `getHttpsConfig({ sslCert, sslKey })` reads from CLI options when no env vars are set.
- CLI options take precedence over env vars when both are set.
- A missing CLI cert file produces a `You specified --ssl-cert...` error (the env-var path still reports `SSL_CRT_FILE in your env...`).
- `--ssl-cert` + `--ssl-key` together implies HTTPS without `--https`.
- `--https` alone returns `true`.

New ECDSA fixtures generated with `openssl ecparam -name prime256v1` are committed alongside the existing RSA fixtures.

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  13 passed (13)
```

### Manual

Generated a self-signed P-256 cert and ran:

```
docusaurus start --ssl-cert ./host.crt --ssl-key ./host.key --host 0.0.0.0
```

Server starts, `curl --cacert ./host.crt https://localhost:3000/` returns 200 with `verify=0`. Without this PR the same invocation fails at startup with the `unsupported keytype` error from `publicEncrypt`.

### Test links

https://deploy-preview-12065--docusaurus-2.netlify.app/

author: ekosamaghub
body:
## Outage post-mortem

The site returned `ERR_CONNECTION_ABORTED` shortly after launching the first queue crawl.

**Root cause:** `frontend/app/page.tsx` is a server component that `await`s three API calls during SSR, and `apiFetch` had **no timeout**. When the parallel crawl workers (4 GitHub workers + the Railway worker, two separate runs) exhausted Timescale's connection limit, the Railway API's DB calls hung. The homepage SSR then awaited forever → Vercel's render function timed out → the browser saw `ERR_CONNECTION_ABORTED`. A `try/catch` was present but only catches *errors*, not *hangs*.

## Fixes

1. **`frontend/lib/api.ts` — 8s `AbortSignal.timeout` on `apiFetch` + `getActiveRun`.** The key resilience fix: a slow/overloaded backend now degrades to offline/empty state instead of hanging SSR. Decouples site availability from backend health.
2. **`crawl.yml` — workers 4 → 2.** Caps peak concurrent DB connections.
3. **`worker.py` — Railway worker no longer auto-runs discovery.** GitHub Actions is the canonical crawler; running discovery on Railway too doubled the crawl + connection load. Opt back in with `WORKER_DISCOVER=1`.

## Immediate mitigation (already advised, separate from this PR)
- Cancel the running crawl workflow to free DB connections.
- Restart the Railway API service if it's wedged.

## Test plan
- [x] `worker.py` compiles; `crawl.yml` valid YAML; `AbortSignal.timeout` wired in both fetch paths.
- [ ] After merge + Railway redeploy: re-run `Nightly Crawl` and confirm the site stays up under load (watch `/runs/progress`).
- [ ] Consider a follow-up: a real psycopg connection pool in the API + a shared connection across `claim/heartbeat/complete` in `drive_queue` if 2 workers still pressures the DB.

author: laulpogan
body:
## What

Adds `wire session bind <name>` so an existing session can be attached to the current cwd without going through `destroy --force && new` (which loses keypair, slot, daemon).

## Why

Walk-up auto-detect (session.rs:550) climbs from cwd looking for a registered ancestor. If `~/Source` is registered (as a session called `source`), every child cwd inherits that identity:

| cwd | resolved session | character |
|---|---|---|
| `~/Source/wire` | `source` (inherited) | 🐻 cedar-bayou |
| `~/Source/slancha-website` | `source` (inherited) | 🐻 cedar-bayou |

Two CC sessions in different projects render with the same character. The walk-up behavior is correct in principle (a sub-tool inside `~/Source/wire/tools/foo` should still resolve to `wire`), but there's no ergonomic way to say "this leaf project IS its own session." `wire session new` doesn't help when a session with that name already exists but isn't bound to any cwd.

## Behavior

```
cd ~/Source/wire
wire session bind wire                # explicit name
wire session bind                     # auto-derive from basename(cwd)
```

- Errors loudly if the named session doesn't exist (hints to `wire session new`).
- Idempotent: re-binding to the current binding returns `changed=false`.
- Re-binding to a different session overwrites with a stderr warning.
- Uses `update_registry` (flock-serialized) so it composes safely with concurrent MCP auto-init.

## Verified live on `~/Source/wire`

Before: `auto-detect → sessions/source → 🐻 cedar-bayou`
After:  `auto-detect → sessions/wire   → 🛡 noble-creek`

## Tests

- `session_bind_attaches_existing_session_to_cwd_v0_7_1`
- `session_bind_errors_on_unknown_session_v0_7_1`
- `session_bind_is_idempotent_when_already_bound_v0_7_1`

3/3 pass locally. Full test suite + clippy + fmt clean.

## Follow-up (not this PR)

Operator intuition: "new Claude session in a new folder = new wire identity, automatically." Today an unregistered cwd falls through to the bare WIRE_HOME default identity. Natural-default would be: walk up only to git root, auto-mint a session keyed on git-root-basename if no match. That's a bigger semantic change; tracking separately.

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo test --test cli session_bind` passes
- [ ] After bind, `wire whoami` from that cwd resolves to the bound session's character
- [ ] Re-bind to same name is a no-op
- [ ] Re-bind to different name overwrites
- [ ] Bind to unknown session errors

author: polliard
body:
## Summary

Design **and implementation plan** for **repo-standards@v2** of the issue triage pipeline. Closes the design phase of #19 and unblocks implementation.

### Two documents in this PR

| Doc | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Design spec | `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-23-triage-decomposition-v2-design.md` | Architecture, label model, data flow, schemas, permissions, error handling, testing, rollout |
| Implementation plan | `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-23-triage-decomposition-v2.md` | Bite-sized TDD task list (15 tasks + rollout runbook) — what an engineer / agent should do, in order, with code |

### Key decisions locked through brainstorming

- **Two label families.** `kind/*` (work-type: bug/enhancement/refactor/chore/security/rfc/docs + new `hook`/`finding`) and `agile/*` (plan-tree position: epic → feature → story → task). They answer orthogonal questions and coexist on the same issue.
- **Two reusable workflows** in `repo-standards@v2`:
  - `triage.yml@v2` — classification (labels every new issue).
  - `triage-decompose.yml@v2` — propose + approve loop (auto-proposes children for `agile/{epic,feature,story}`, files them on `/triage approve-decomposition`).
- **Auto-cascade.** Each created child carries `status/triage`, so the next layer's classification + proposal fires automatically. `status/triage` is removed only when decomposition is signaled-complete by the human at that level.
- **Idempotency** via three hidden HTML comment markers (`classified` / `proposal` / `applied`) with 12-char SHA-256 body-hashes. GitHub issue is the source of truth; no external state.
- **Permission gate** on `/triage approve-decomposition`: `author_association ∈ {OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR}`.
- **Rollout**: RC tag (`v2.0.0-rc1`) + 1-week soak on aiConstitution before promotion to `v2.0.0` and 22-repo rollout.

### Plan corrects one spec discrepancy

Spec §8.3 wrote `ts` for the audit-log timestamp field; plan uses `chronon` to match `~/.ai/Common.md §5.2` and the existing `triage-audit.sh`. Spec will be amended in a follow-up commit.

### Scope

This PR adds design + plan docs only. The implementation lives in `convergent-systems-co/repo-standards` on a separate branch (`triage/v2-design`); see plan Task 1 for the engineer's starting point.

Consumer-side rollout (aiConstitution caller bump, 21-atom-repo relabel) is plan §16 (Rollout Runbook) — checklist work executed after the upstream PR merges.

- [x] Plan passes self-review (full spec coverage, no placeholders, type consistency, valid bats patterns)
- [x] Principal review on this PR (you, before merge)

body:
## Summary

- The initial-run `Sweep(...)` call in `sweep/run_sweep.py` was missing `postprocess=POSTPROCESS_HOOK`. The hook fired on initial runs because every `RunSpec` carries it, but the manifest header recorded `postprocess: null` — so `Sweep.from_manifest` reloaded with `_postprocess=None` and `resume()` overwrote every retried spec's hook with `None`. Resumed runs ran GMAT and were marked `ok` but never produced `comparison.parquet`, which made `make aggregate` emit silent NaN rows.
- Pass `postprocess=POSTPROCESS_HOOK` to the constructor so the header records the hook string and the resume path restamps it correctly.
- Add a regression test (`TestDispatchSweep.test_initial_run_passes_postprocess_to_sweep`) that monkeypatches `Sweep` and `LocalJoblibPool` and asserts the kwarg reaches the constructor.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run ruff check` clean
- [x] `uv run ruff format --check` clean

body:
### Motivation
- The Snapchat adapter relied on broad HTML keyword matches (e.g. "saved", "submitted", "posted") to signal success, which produced false positives and corrupts run history and cooldown behavior.
- The goal is a narrow hotfix so the adapter only returns `success=True` for unambiguous, actionable confirmation signals.
- While reviewing Snapchat, the same broad-keyword pattern was found in X and LinkedIn confirmation logic and required narrow hardening as well.

### Description
- Replaced Snapchat generic `page.content().lower()` confirmation checks with an explicit `_detect_ads_confirmation(page)` helper that only returns success for: created/entity URL or link evidence, Snapchat-specific success toast/dialog, or a confirmation/review route transition, and otherwise returns the requested ambiguous failure response (`PLATFORM_AUTOMATION_ERROR`) with an explanatory `raw` message and screenshot capture when practical.
- Tightened X confirmation to require either an explicit status URL or an explicit "Your post was sent" toast instead of relying on broad page-content markers like `posted`.
- Tightened LinkedIn confirmation to require an explicit success toast when no post URL is captured instead of a broad `shared`/body-text fallback.
- Files changed: `src/platforms/snapchat.py`, `src/platforms/x.py`, `src/platforms/linkedin.py`; commit hash: `eeaad32a50978638b3e8e3e141d0d609d956e2db`.

author: mikelward
body:
## Summary

Adds a new **Rain accessory** option under Settings → Format. Default is **Off** (existing prose is byte-identical). When set to **Umbrella**, the rain mention in both the morning precip clause and the evening event tie-in folds in "bring an umbrella":

> Today, it will be 14° to 20°. Wear a sweater. **Rain at 3pm, bring an umbrella.**
>
> … Tonight, rain at 9pm, bring **a jacket and umbrella**.

The accessory rides on the existing rain mention — triggered on the same `POSSIBLE_THRESHOLD` (≥ 30%) the rain clause already uses, so no new tunable.

The enum data model is `RainAccessory { NONE, UMBRELLA }`, shaped so additional choices (rain jacket, hood, rain boots, tiered per-probability accessories, …) can be added later without a DataStore migration. This PR ships **only the umbrella variant** per the user's request; the follow-ups are flagged in TODOs near the new code.

## Implementation

- `RainAccessory` enum + `UserPreferences.rainAccessory` field in `:core:domain` (`Settings.kt`); `DataStore` key `rain_accessory` + setter + read in `SettingsRepository`.
- `InsightFormatter` gains a `rainAccessory` constructor arg (defaulted to NONE). The existing `isAccessory` filter still strips user-typed umbrella `ClothesRule`s from the items list — the format-option choice instead:
  - Appends "bring an umbrella" via two new templates `insight_precip_with_accessory` / `insight_precip_chance_with_accessory` on the morning precip clause.
  - Re-injects the accessory key into the evening tie-in's items list after the filter, which lets the existing `insight_tie_in_with_rain` template carry it and promotes the bare-rain path to the item-led template.
- **Condition-gated end to end**:
  - The morning precip-clause accessory mention only fires when `PrecipClause.condition` is RAIN or DRIZZLE. SNOW and THUNDERSTORM (which the precip clause can carry) skip the accessory — the setting is rain-keyed by name, snow doesn't want an umbrella, and umbrella-under-lightning is bad practice.
  - The evening tie-in accessory injection follows the same gate. To make this possible, `EveningEventTieInClause` carries a new optional `precipCondition: WeatherCondition?` field, populated by `DeriveInsight` from the same per-model peak's condition. Cached payloads written before the field existed land as `null`, which the formatter treats as "unknown, skip the accessory" — the next forecast cycle populates the field.
- All 8 `InsightFormatter.forContext/forRegion` call sites (Today screen, ClothesCastNavHost, CastTestDispatch, InsightTtsUtterance, BugReport, FetchAndNotifyWorker, FormatSettings preview cards) plumb `prefs.rainAccessory` through. `TodayState` carries the value into the `InsightCard` composable.
- Settings UI: new `FormatDropdownRow<RainAccessory>` in the "What to say" section using the existing generic component. Both preview cards on the Format page reflect the choice live.
- `ClothesRule.DEFAULTS` comment refreshed — the prior TODO about personalising the wet-weather accessory is replaced by a pointer to `UserPreferences.rainAccessory`, plus a new TODO for tiered per-probability accessories (the user's explicit follow-up).
- German prose templates added in `values-de`. The phraser's existing EN→DE map already had `umbrella` → `Regenschirm`, so the German prose lands naturally ("Regen um 15 Uhr, denk an Regenschirm.") with no phraser changes.

## Privacy

No new off-device exposure. The accessory key is rendered locally; the resulting prose flows to Gemini TTS only when the user has opted into BYOK TTS, on the same path as every other weather-derived recommendation already does. Surfaced on the `settings_snapshot` event as `rain_accessory` (enum name, NONE or UMBRELLA) — bumped on `TelemetryPrivacyContractTest`'s allowlist.

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew :core:domain:test :core:data:test` — passes
- [x] `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest` — passes
- [x] `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug` — passes
- [x] New tests in `InsightFormatterTest` cover both tiers (LIKELY/POSSIBLE), the overnight collapse, drizzle (accessory still fires), snow + thunderstorm (accessory suppressed) on the morning path, the evening tie-in injection (items+rain, bare-rain promotion, no-rain-time silence), evening tie-in suppression on SNOW / THUNDERSTORM / null `precipCondition`, and German rendering.
- [x] New `SettingsRepositoryTest` round-trip for `RainAccessory` + NONE default.
- [x] New Roborazzi snapshot `SettingsFormatRainAccessoryPreview` captures the prose change end-to-end.
- [ ] Visual smoke on a real device — toggle the option, watch the Today prose update live.

## Out of scope (deferred follow-ups)

- Additional accessory variants (rain jacket, hood, rain boots, …) — enum is forward-compatible, just needs phraser + resource entries.
- Tiered/per-probability accessories ("umbrella ≥ 30%, rain jacket ≥ 70%") — TODO marker left in `Settings.kt` near the enum.
- The bare-rain template `insight_evening_rain` still says "Tonight, rain at 9pm." even when the underlying peak is snow — pre-existing infelicity unrelated to this PR. The new `precipCondition` field makes it easy to fix in a follow-up by branching the template per condition.

author: kishanbagaria
body:
## What

Replaces the fixed-interval polling loops in `PlatformAPI` (25ms / 250ms / exponential-backoff `Task.sleep`) for sent-message, sent-thread, and attachment-load waits with event-driven waits on the existing `IMDatabase.changes` `Topic<Void>` — the same debounced (25ms) filesystem-watcher tick the rest of the system already uses. Idle waits stop issuing wasted SQL queries; detection latency matches the old 25ms cadence.

New `DatabaseTickWaits` helper holds the three wait functions; each loops `subscribe → query → satisfied? return : waitForChange(tick OR deadline)`. The subscribe-before-query ordering avoids lost wakeups. `Topic` gains `onTermination`-based subscription cleanup (keyed by `UUID`) and moves `yield()`/`finish()` out of the non-reentrant `os_unfair_lock` critical section.

## Hardening (from eng review)

- **Backstop:** `waitForChange` caps each wait at ~1s, so a dropped/coalesced FS tick re-queries at poll cadence instead of hanging to the full timeout (restores the old pollers' self-healing).
- **Graceful degrade:** `changeTopic()` no longer fails the wait if `beginListeningForChanges()` throws — it logs and returns the (silent) topic; the backstop carries the wait.
- **Cancellation:** sent-message/sent-thread waits run inline instead of `Task.detached`, so caller cancellation propagates and they stop promptly.
- **DRY:** extracted `ensureDatabase(_:)` for lazy DB init.

## Tests

`DatabaseTickWaitTests` — 11/11 passing:
- Event-driven re-read (only re-queries on a tick) for all three helpers
- Partial-link return after link timeout
- Timeout/error paths: sent-message timeout-throw, sent-thread deadline-with-nil, attachment no-attachments / terminal-failure / timeout
- `Topic` terminated-subscription cleanup + `finishCurrentSubscribers` deadlock guard

author: elliotchung
body:
## Summary

8 sequential per-iteration-researcher iterations exploring the `position-tier-gate` execution-algorithm family. All 8 algorithms PASS the canonical gate (≥+5% PnL vs `simple` baseline), but only iter-1's `position-tier-imbalance-gate` introduces a new mechanism — iters 2-8 are gate-axis variations that cluster around or below iter-2 and inform a structural-exhaustion conclusion.

**Family-best: iter-2 `position-tier-imbalance-ema-gate`** (pnl=4503.25, sharpe=20.79).

## Iterations (chronological)

| # | Algo                                          | Status        | PnL    | Sharpe | Trades | Note                                       |
|---|-----------------------------------------------|---------------|-------:|-------:|-------:|--------------------------------------------|
| 1 | position-tier-imbalance-gate                  | PASS          | 4344.5 | 21.27  | 62251  | New family — single-tick imbalance + cap=1 |
| 2 | position-tier-imbalance-ema-gate              | PASS (best)   | 4503.25| 20.79  | 62220  | EMA smoothing; refinement no-op vs iter-1  |
| 3 | position-tier-ofi-gate                        | PASS / regr   | 2201.75| 11.89  | 56305  | OFI signal structurally worse than imbalance |
| 4 | position-tier-imbalance-cap2-gate             | PASS / regr   | 2686.5 | 10.89  | 86259  | cap=2 hurts on every axis → cap=1 optimal  |
| 5 | position-tier-vol-regime-gate                 | PASS / parallel | 4377.0 | 20.67  | 59258  | Vol-regime axis ≈ EMA-imbalance axis       |
| 6 | position-tier-directional-vol-gate            | PASS / parallel | 4491.75| 21.08  | 61886  | Directional vol recovers same-side bursts  |
| 7 | position-tier-tod-gate                        | PASS / regr   | 3933.5 | 21.26  | 57989  | Calendar (TOD) filter removes net-positive entries |
| 8 | position-tier-reduce-only-defer-gate          | PASS / regr   | 3521.0 | 17.79  | 62160  | Exit-side defer: ~$0.016/trade adverse drift |

## Structural conclusion (from agents' honesty notes)

The position_cap=1 + reduce-only-fast-path is the binding constraint. Seven mechanism axes were explored (imbalance, EMA-imbalance, OFI, cap-relax, sym-vol, dir-vol, TOD, exit-defer) and all PnL outcomes cluster in a ~$2k band, with iter-2 retaining family-best. **No snapshots were taken** — none of iters 3-8 beat iter-2 on the refinement-axis targets in `research/config.yaml → refinement.targets`.

## Caveats (per §8 honesty)

- **2026-03-19 excluded** from every iteration's aggregate: reproducible Nautilus/Rust 8 GiB OOM on `subscribe_quote_ticks`-using algos despite 22 GiB host RAM free. Same partition runs fine for `simple`. Documented in `research/NOTES.md` (iter-1) and reproduced/verified on iter-2/3/8. All aggregates are N=11 of 12 train dates.
- **Slippage axis is uninformative**: 0.0 / 0.0 for both algo and baseline across all 11 dates (zero-cost fill model — pre-existing limitation, see `research/NOTES.md` 2026-04-30).
- **Trade counts**: all iterations have 56k+ trades; no low-trade-count flag triggered.

## Operational notes

- Branch contains 16 commits: 8 iteration commits + 8 `chore(...): backfill execution metadata` follow-ups produced by the iteration pipeline.
- `uv.lock` was modified at session start (unrelated, left untouched).
- Iteration 1 took 4 attempts due to a structural issue where the per-iteration-researcher subagent paused for `<task-notification>` events the parent could not deliver (no SendMessage tool). Resolved by giving subsequent agents explicit "synchronous-foreground-Bash only, one date per call, ~10 min timeout" constraints — every subsequent iteration completed on the first attempt.

## Test plan

- [ ] Inspect each iteration's `execution_algos/<id>/NOTES.md` and `results/backtest-results.json` for raw numbers
- [ ] Confirm `research/program_database.json` has 9 entries (1 pre-existing + 8 new)
- [ ] Confirm `research/NOTES.md` documents the 2026-03-19 OOM hazard
- [ ] Review iter-2 vs iter-3/4 honesty notes — agents correctly distinguished "PASS vs baseline" from "improvement over family-best"
- [ ] Decide whether to snapshot iter-2 (`position-tier-imbalance-ema-gate`) as the position-tier-gate family-best (not done in this PR pending review)

## Summary
- Changes pause pronoun follow-ups to use fresh Mission Control context instead of demanding a mission id when the target is unambiguous.
- If exactly one running mission is in current context, Spark sends one `/mission pause` equivalent through the existing Mission Control command path and confirms naturally.
- If the contextual mission is already paused, Spark says so without sending a command. If there are multiple running missions or no running target, Spark asks for a specific target / exact command.

## Bug Record
- Exact prompt sequence: `what is currently running or paused in Mission Control? keep it short and do not start anything.` then `can you pause that one?`
- Initial observed failure before this PR: the follow-up fell through to the generic exact-id pause warning.
- Product correction from user review: pausing should not always require a mission id when Spark has fresh, unambiguous context.
- Classification: protected-action pronoun fallback / route gap with contextual action resolution.
- Source boundary: `conversationIntent` classification, `handleTextMessage` admin natural-text routing, and a `spawner` helper that resolves fresh board state before sending a command.

## Tests
- Red regression first: `BOT_TOKEN=123:test node node_modules/ts-node/dist/bin.js tests/buildE2E.test.ts` failed with the old exact-id warning before the contextual route existed.
- Mocked handler regression: one running mission plus `can you pause that one?` must POST exactly one contextual pause command and confirm `I paused Mission Command Running Probe.`
- `node node_modules/ts-node/dist/bin.js tests/conversationIntent.test.ts`
- `BOT_TOKEN=123:test node node_modules/ts-node/dist/bin.js tests/buildE2E.test.ts`
